articles.title: Jessica Simpson celebrates turning 46 in bikini as she admits her children have never seen her perform
articles.excerpt:

Jessica Simpson celebrated 46 exactly how a self-described "sun lover" would.

The singer marked the occasion with a close-up selfie...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Jessica Simpson celebrated 46 exactly how a self-described "sun lover" would.

The singer marked the occasion with a close-up selfie showing her tanning in a black-and-white polka-dot bikini, simply captioning the photo, "💫46💫 July 10/26 ".

Simpson reclined beneath a purple crocheted cover while wearing oval dark sunglasses. Her blonde hair was styled in a loose side braid, and she accessorized the polka-dot bikini with layered turquoise bead necklaces, a square green pendant, dangling stone earrings and stacked bracelets.

SHAKIRA SOAKS UP THE MIAMI SUN AS BIKINI-CLAD NINA DOBREV, KIM KARDASHIAN SHOWCASE SUMMER GETAWAYS

Jessica Simpson marked her 46th birthday with a bikini selfie while celebrating another trip around the sun. (Jessica Simpson/Instagram)

With the sun illuminating her face, the "With You" singer completed the birthday look with glossy lips and a relaxed expression.

Fans quickly filled the comments with birthday wishes and compliments for the pop star.

The birthday post comes as Simpson continues her return to music after years away from the stage.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

A post shared by Jessica Simpson (@jessicasimpson)

During Thursday's episode of "The Jennifer Hudson Show," the singer revealed that her children have never seen her perform live because she put her music career on hold to focus on motherhood and building the Jessica Simpson Collection.

"They've never seen me perform," Simpson said. "I really wanted to be a mom. I wanted to focus on the Jessica Simpson Collection."

Now that she has returned to the stage, Simpson said her children have embraced the next chapter of her career.

VICTORIA BECKHAM REVEALS STRICT NO-PHONES RULE AT FAMILY DINNER KEEPS HER KIDS GROUNDED

Jessica Simpson shares daughters Maxwell and Birdie and son Ace with her estranged husband, Eric Johnson. (Pierre Suu/GC Images)

"The kids are very proud of me," she said. "They supported me... They knew I was following my dreams, and they saw how happy it made me and how much peace it gave me. It feels brand new again, which is a beautiful thing."

Simpson said her children supported her as she began traveling to Nashville to write and record new music. She also explained that her latest music reflects a more personal approach to songwriting.

"I'm gonna only be honest through music from here on out," Simpson said. "Like I can't sing other people's lyrics if I'm gonna put my name on it."

She credited the release of her 2020 memoir, "Open Book," with helping her reconnect with herself after decades in the spotlight.

"I've never felt so heard. I've never felt so seen in my life," she said. "I connected with my younger self."

HALLE BERRY FLAUNTS TONED FIGURE IN PLUNGING SWIMSUIT DURING TROPICAL GETAWAY

The birthday post also comes months after Simpson reflected on her lifelong love of tanning in an interview with Elle magazine.

The Texas native described herself as a lifelong "sun lover," recalling summers spent by the pool and admitting she rarely thought about sunscreen growing up.

Simpson said maintaining a bronzed appearance became part of the preparation for her role as Daisy Duke in the 2005 movie "The Dukes of Hazzard." (Donald Weber/Getty Images)

"I am a born-and-bred Texan sun lover. My birthday is in July and every birthday party I had was in the pool. My buns were always tan," Simpson told the outlet.

Today, Simpson said she still enjoys having a tan but approaches time in the sun differently.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Jessica Simpson recently returned to music after stepping away from performing to focus on raising her family. (Aeon/GC Images)

"I still like the tan, trust me, but there are ways to go about it," she said.

She also reflected on how her perspective has evolved with age.

"I've never been that person who is terrified to be out in the sun because of wrinkles," Simpson said. "It just happens and is a part of life."

Danielle Minnetian is an Entertainment Production Assistant for Fox News Digital covering celebrity news, entertainment trends and pop culture.

articles.title: Mandela Barnes drops out of high-stakes Wisconsin governor’s race
articles.excerpt:
Former lieutenant governor says path to Democratic nomination no longer viable as democratic socialist rival surges ahead

Mandela Barnes, the former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, dropped out of t...
articles.body_text:
Former lieutenant governor says path to Democratic nomination no longer viable as democratic socialist rival surges ahead

Mandela Barnes, the former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, dropped out of the Democratic primary for governor on Thursday, upending the high-stakes contest less than two weeks before the 11 August election.

Barnes announced the decision in a video posted on social media, saying he no longer saw a viable path to the nomination as democratic socialist Francesca Hong surged ahead with a commanding lead.

“It’s become very clear who our nominee is going to be,” Barnes, 39, said.

The Marquette Law School poll showed Hong significantly ahead of Barnes in a distant second place, with 38% compared to his 16%, having consolidated liberal support, especially among young voters, although about a third of primary voters remained undecided.

Soon after Barnes’s withdrawal, the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported it had sent questions to the candidate about past allegations of inappropriate behavior that had been anonymously submitted to the Wisconsin Democratic party, local party officials and others.

According to the Journal Sentinel, the state party hired a law firm in 2025 to investigate the claims sent in a letter that Barnes had used his position in the party to pursue inappropriate relationships with “young adult women”.

The party’s internal review and outside investigation found no actionable evidence because the claims were “anonymous and unspecific”, the Journal Sentinel reported, citing an unnamed person familiar with the matter.

“There are no allegations of misconduct or wrongdoing against Mandela,” it said in a statement.

His departure adds another twist in the Democratic primary for governor in Wisconsin, a perennial presidential battleground that has also been at the center of national disputes over election administration since the 2020 election.

He is the third Democrat to exit the race, following lieutenant governor Sara Rodriguez, who withdrew two weeks ago amid a campaign finance scandal. After Rodriguez’s exit, Milwaukee county executive David Crowley re-entered the race with the endorsement of Governor Tony Evers, who is not seeking re-election.

Earlier this summer, Missy Hughes, a former state economic development director, ended her campaign.

On Wednesday, a judge rejected an effort backed by the Democratic party to let voters who had already cast absentee ballots void their initial vote and vote again, over concerns that many early ballots had been cast for candidates who were no longer in the race.

Crowley moved quickly to appeal to Barnes’s supporters: “There’s a place for you in what we’re building.”

Evers told reporters he was surprised by Barnes’s decision to withdraw but reiterated his support for Crowley, saying he believed Crowley was the strongest candidate “even if Mandela was in”, the Associated Press reported.

The Democratic gubernatorial nominee in Wisconsin is expected to face Republican US congressman Tom Tiffany, who is backed by Donald Trump.

Barnes was once viewed as a rising star in Democratic politics. In 2022, rather than seek re-election as lieutenant governor, he ran for the US Senate, narrowly losing the race to incumbent Republican Ron Johnson.

articles.title: Hiker's unexplained death exposes deadly alcohol withdrawal risk many don't recognize
articles.excerpt:
The actor explained that his wife gave him an ultimatum when it came to his drinking, which ultimately got him to stop.

When hiker Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, was found dead near Sykes Hot Springs in Ca...
articles.body_text:
The actor explained that his wife gave him an ultimatum when it came to his drinking, which ultimately got him to stop.

When hiker Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, was found dead near Sykes Hot Springs in California’s Ventana Wilderness, initial speculation pointed to foul play, according to a press release from the Monterey County Sheriff's Office.

However, official coroner's reports revealed her cause of death to be probable alcohol withdrawal seizures brought on by chronic alcohol use disorder.

Friends who were hiking with Shields said she had gone to the river that morning. A short time later, one of them found her unresponsive in the water, according to reports.

IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

"This is a probable seizure that occurred as a result of chronic alcohol use disorder, but there was nothing that stood out that indicated any type of criminal activity," Andres Rosas, commander and the primary public information officer for the Monterey County Sheriff's Office, told KSBW 8.

Given the results of the investigation and forensic examination, no further investigation is taking place.

The recent death of a Big Sur hiker was ruled a probable case of fatal alcohol withdrawal seizures, exposing a dangerous and often hidden medical crisis. (iStock)

The incident highlights a little-known danger of severe alcohol dependence, as suddenly stopping alcohol can trigger life-threatening neurological events.

Alcohol acts as a depressant on the central nervous system. When someone drinks heavily over a prolonged period, the brain adapts by ramping up chemical signals to keep bodily systems functioning, according to experts.

When alcohol is abruptly stopped, that blocker on the central nervous system is removed. The brain then enters a state of dangerous overexcitation, leading to severe hyperarousal.

Withdrawal symptoms typically begin within six to 24 hours after the last drink, with the risk of seizures peaking between 24 and 48 hours.

Alcohol withdrawal can quickly progress from tremors, sweating and anxiety to severe grand mal seizures and a condition called Delirium Tremens. (iStock)

In wilderness settings or isolated locations, a sudden seizure can result in immediate loss of consciousness, trauma, respiratory arrest or an inability to seek emergency care, experts note.

Clinical guidelines from the National Institutes of Health categorize alcohol withdrawal by the following key progression stages.

This may include minor withdrawal symptoms, including insomnia, tremors, anxiety, gastrointestinal upset, headache, diaphoresis (excessive sweating), heart palpitations, anorexia, nausea, tachycardia (abnormally fast resting heart rate) and hypertension.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

This stage is marked by visual, auditory or tactile hallucinations.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

People in this stage may experience sudden loss of consciousness accompanied by severe muscle contractions (seizures). Another potential symptom is delirium tremens, a medical emergency involving extreme agitation, fever, racing heart, hyperthermia and cardiac instability.

Attempting to detox without medical supervision can result in sudden loss of consciousness, trauma and death, experts warn. (iStock)

Health agencies, including the National Institutes of Health, strongly advise that individuals with a history of heavy drinking or prior withdrawal episodes should never attempt to detox alone or in remote settings.

Medical detox programs use tailored medication protocols to safely taper brain activity and prevent seizures.

Help is available for people struggling with alcohol use disorder. The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) National Helpline provides free, confidential treatment referrals 24 hours a day at 1-800-662-4357.

Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

articles.title: Saints lock up Chris Olave with 4-year extension worth $132M after training camp hold-in
articles.excerpt:
Chris Myers and Mark Schlereth praised the Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints futures in NFC South matchup.

New Orleans Saints star receiver Chris Olave agreed to a four-year extension worth $132...
articles.body_text:
Chris Myers and Mark Schlereth praised the Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints futures in NFC South matchup.

New Orleans Saints star receiver Chris Olave agreed to a four-year extension worth $132 million with $90 million guaranteed, sources confirmed to OutKick’s Armando Salguero.

Olave was set to play the 2026 NFL season on his fifth-year option, and he was a hold-in at training camp because of it. He wanted a new deal before taking part in practices.

The Saints decided to reward their 2022 first-rounder with his desired extension before potential free agency in 2027.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) walks on the sideline during the second half at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Oct. 5, 2025. (Stephen Lew/Imagn Images)

Olave will remain a cornerstone piece for the franchise alongside new starting quarterback Tyler Shough , whom they drafted in the second round in 2025.

This deal marks the highest one the Saints have dished out to a receiver since Michael Thomas received a five-year pact worth up to $20 million per season in 2019. At the time, it was a record.

DRAKE LONDON SIGNS $141M DEAL WITH FALCONS, BECOMING THIRD HIGHEST-PAID RECEIVER IN NFL: REPORTS

Now, Olave will be making $33 million per season, cementing him as one of the highest-paid receivers in the NFL.

The Ohio State product earned that over his rookie deal with the Saints, especially this past season. Across 16 games, Olave notched career-highs in yards (1,163), touchdowns (nine) and receptions (100).

Chris Olave of the New Orleans Saints celebrates after a touchdown during a game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on Dec. 28, 2025, in Nashville, Tenn. The Saints defeated the Titans 34-26. (Getty Images)

Olave started thriving once Shough took over as the team’s starting quarterback, quickly finding chemistry with his new signal caller, and the Saints clearly believe that connection will lead them to playoff glory once more.

The Saints have not reached the playoffs since the 2020 campaign, though they have sprinkled in 9-8 seasons in there. However, they’ve gone 11-23 across the past two seasons, and head coach Kellen Moore’s first year was a 6-11 finish in New Orleans.

But there were positives that came out of the lackluster record, with the offense being the main highlight. The Saints are excited to see what Shough can do with a full offseason understanding he’s the starting quarterback as well as working more in Moore’s system.

Chris Olave of the New Orleans Saints reacts during training camp at Ochsner Sports Performance Center in Metairie, La., on July 30, 2026. (Getty Images)

Olave benefitted from said system, and the Saints bolstered their offensive weapons by signing Travis Etienne Jr. to their backfield. With Saints legend Alvin Kamara returning for another season, the running backs depth chart is filled with explosive playmakers, while Olave, tight end Juwan Johnson, and 2026 first-round pick Jordan Tyson out of Arizona State have this group primed for success.

articles.title: Trump says Board of Peace reaches agreement on disarmament of Hamas in Gaza
articles.excerpt:
United States President Donald Trump has said that his ‘Board of Peace’ has reached an agreement to disarm the Palestinian group Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza.

“This agreement is a critica...
articles.body_text:
United States President Donald Trump has said that his ‘Board of Peace’ has reached an agreement to disarm the Palestinian group Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza.

“This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social website on Thursday. “At the same time, Israel will have the security it deserves, with Gaza no longer used as a base for terror attacks.”

Hamas has not yet commented on the statement.

Trump framed the disarmament as part of the ceasefire deal he brokered in October to end Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians and devastated the Palestinian enclave. Israel has repeatedly violated the ceasefire agreement, killing more than 1,200 Palestinians, seizing more territory, and continuing to restrict the movement of people and goods into and out of Gaza.

Trump said that Israel would withdraw from Gaza and be replaced by an International Stabilisation Force working with a “new Palestinian police force” once disarmament was complete.

“Under this agreement, Gaza will finally be in the hands of a new Palestinian government that serves its PEOPLE,” Trump added.

Hamas leaders have been in the Egyptian capital Cairo since late last week discussing the ceasefire deal with mediators from Egypt, Qatar, and Turkiye. An unnamed Hamas official was quoted earlier on Thursday as saying that the talks were “positive” and “making progress”.

Hamas had announced on July 6 the dissolution of the body it led that had governed Gaza for nearly two decades.

articles.body_text:
Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong was asked about appearing on far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's livestream on MS NOW Wednesday.

Mandela Barnes, who served as Lt. Governor of Wisconsin from 2019 to 2023, suspended his gubernatorial campaign on Thursday, citing a lack of support to capture the Democratic Party nomination.

"It’s become very clear who our nominee is going to be," Barnes said in a video statement.

"While I may be suspending my campaign, I’ll never give up my fight for Wisconsin," he continued.

WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO ‘ABOLISH POLICE’

Then-Senate candidate Mandela Barnes is seen leaving a canvas launch event on Nov. 7, 2022, in Glendale, Wisconsin. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

Barnes, who was endorsed by Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., as the "kind of bold leader we need to take on the Trump Administration," did not name the candidate he believes will capture the party’s nomination later this month.

His departure from the race comes as a surprise amid a crowded Democratic field to fill the empty seat of outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers. Barnes was considered a frontrunner in the race because of his proximity to Evers and his name recognition. It also coincides with rumblings that Barnes may have abused his position in the past to make sexual advances towards women in the workplace—an allegation currently under investigation by the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, which published its report shortly after Barnes' video post.

Barnes' campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on if his decision to suspend the campaign was in any way connected to the reporting. However, a Barnes spokesperson told Politico that "there are no allegations of misconduct or wrongdoing against Mandela."

With Barnes’ departure, the remaining major candidates include Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong, a Democratic socialist, and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley.

TOP DEM HOPEFUL FLIPS SCRIPT AFTER YEARS IN SOCIALIST ORBIT WITH PUZZLING CLAIM

Congressman Adam Schiff speaks at the "Just Majority" Burbank Press Conference on May 26, 2023 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Jerod Harris/Getty Images for Demand Justice) (Jerod Harris/Getty Images for Demand Justice)

Notably, Hong has received backing from a number of nationally recognized progressives, including Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif. She has raised nearly $709,000 as of late June, according to state records.

By comparison, Crowley has secured $250,000 and enjoys the support of a number of local organizations and figures.

Evers, pointedly, endorsed Crowley over Barnes, citing Crowley’s experience.

In his departure video, Barnes urged Democrats to unite against Republicans in the November general election.

"Now I said from the very beginning when I launched this campaign that the no. 1 goal was taking on and defeating Tom Tiffany to deliver big wins for Democrats up and down the ticket," Barnes said, referring to the presumptive Republican nominee.

"Now it’s our time to come together and focus our efforts on that one goal. We have to do everything to be Tom Tiffany. This is life or death for Wisconsinites who are losing their healthcare under a Trump administration."

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Wisc., speaks during a television interview outside of the Capitol after being sworn in as a member of Congress on Tuesday, May 19, 2020. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Barnes built his campaign on a platform of increasing taxes on the country’s top earners, freezing energy costs, providing universal childcare and lowering the cost of housing.

The gubernatorial primary will take place on Aug. 11.

Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

articles.title: Toddler's tragic death sparks manslaughter charges after alleged poisoning
articles.excerpt: Interventional cardiologist Dr. Craig Basman warns about the addictive dangers of kratom, a plant native to Southeast Asia. He explains how the compound 7-OH in concentrated kratom products interacts ...
articles.body_text:
Interventional cardiologist Dr. Craig Basman warns about the addictive dangers of kratom, a plant native to Southeast Asia. He explains how the compound 7-OH in concentrated kratom products interacts with opioid receptors, mimicking potent drugs like fentanyl and morphine. This can lead to severe dependence, potential overdose and challenging withdrawal symptoms.

A Florida father and the mother of his children are behind bars after police said they failed to seek emergency care when a 2-year-old girl turned blue, suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally after allegedly ingesting kratom pills.

Jerome Jonathon Jordan, 35, and Charlene Rea O'Connell, 32, are each charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and child neglect causing great bodily harm in the death of 2-year-old Jonnie Jordan, according to the West Melbourne Police Department.

The charges come more than two months after Jonnie was rushed to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne on May 18.

Hospital staff pronounced the toddler dead shortly after she arrived.

STEPDAD ACCUSED OF SEX ASSAULT AS COPS WIDEN PROBE INTO GIRL’S LETHAL BENADRYL INGREDIENT DOSE

Jerome Jordan and Charlene O'Connell were booked into the Brevard County Jail on charges including aggravated manslaughter of a child. (West Melbourne Police Department)

Investigators said the tragedy unfolded the night before at O'Connell's Palm Bay home, where Jonnie allegedly got into kratom pills belonging to Jordan and O'Connell.

Police said they believe the toddler consumed as many as two-and-a-half pills before both adults realized what had happened.

According to investigators, Jordan and O'Connell watched as Jonnie's lips turned blue, she suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally. But instead of calling 911 or taking the little girl to a hospital, police allege they failed to seek medical care.

DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED

The West Melbourne Police Department announced the arrests following its investigation into the toddler's death. (West Melbourne Police Department)

Authorities said Jordan then drove Jonnie back to his sister's apartment in West Melbourne and put her to bed.

Hours later, after waking up and finding the toddler unresponsive, Jordan rushed her to the hospital, where doctors pronounced her dead.

Investigators said Jordan initially urged hospital staff to administer Narcan, leading detectives to suspect an overdose early in the investigation.

SHARON STONE'S TERRIFYING WEED WITHDRAWAL SPARKS WARNING ABOUT TODAY'S POTENT MARIJUANA

An aerial view of Florida's Space Coast near West Melbourne, where police investigated the death of a 2-year-old child. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

The Brevard County  Medical Examiner's Office determined that Jonnie died of acute mitragynine intoxication, according to police.

According to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, part of the National Institutes of Health, kratom is a herbal substance made from the leaves of a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia and is commonly sold in powders, capsules, gummies and drinks.

Some people use it for its stimulant or pain-relieving effects, though federal health officials have repeatedly warned about its safety.

This Sept. 27, 2017 file photo shows kratom capsules in Albany, N.Y. (AP Photo/Mary Esch, File)

While kratom remains legal under federal law, the Drug Enforcement Administration announced earlier this month it had begun the process of temporarily placing high-potency 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products and certain related synthetic compounds into Schedule I, citing their high potential for abuse and opioid-like effects. The action does not apply to natural kratom leaf products.

Following the medical examiner's findings and a months-long investigation, police arrested Jordan and O'Connell on Thursday. Both are being held without bond at the Brevard County Jail.

Police said Jordan's sister, whose apartment Jonnie was taken to after leaving O'Connell's home, is not facing any charges.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Indiana's Curt Cignetti roasts the SEC as ESPN starts their promotional campaign already: 'we don't whine'
articles.excerpt:
Will Stein discussed his team's schedule and notes that he'd love to only have to play 8 conference games instead of the mandatory 9.

The 2026 college football season hasn't even started, and the war...
articles.body_text:
Will Stein discussed his team's schedule and notes that he'd love to only have to play 8 conference games instead of the mandatory 9.

The 2026 college football season hasn't even started, and the war of words and messaging is already ramping up.

The SEC this year moves to nine conference games, a large shift that will necessarily impact win-loss records and takes away one of their biggest advantages over the Big Ten or other nine-game conferences. As a result, at SEC media days recently, several coaches and even conference commissioner Greg Sankey started their promotional and excuse campaign for the College Football Playoff.

Despite not reaching the National Championship game for three straight seasons and going 2-7 in the playoff against other Power 4 conference teams, the SEC has started their campaign by saying that they deserve more teams in the tournament. Why? Because of their depth and strength of schedule.

SEC WANTS MORE PLAYOFF FAVORITISM AS GREG SANKEY COMPLAINS ABOUT 'UNSATISFACTORY' TALKS WITH CFB PLAYOFF

Sure, depth and strength of schedule matters, but winning your games matters too. And that's where the SEC coaches and Sankey are going through a bit of a contradictory crisis.

SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey speaks to the press during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott in Tampa, Fla., on July 20, 2026. (Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images)

When the SEC was dominant, winning title after title, the narrative went that the depth meant that their teams were battle hardened by playoff time. Other conferences didn't progress through the regular season gauntlet of SEC teams, making them less prepared at the end of the year.

Now that the SEC has fallen behind the Big Ten and are moving to nine conference games, the narrative-building has changed. Just listen to ESPN's Laura Rutledge make excuses for a season and schedule that hasn't happened yet.

LANE KIFFIN MAKES RIDICULOUS EXCUSES FOR SEC'S POOR RECENT PERFORMANCE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

"So, I think one of the reasons why the SEC may not have advanced as far in the playoffs as some SEC fans would like to see," Rutledge told Pat McAfee recently. "It's because the competition within the league is so difficult that nine games of craziness week in and week out are little different than other parts of other conferences. I'm not dissing on the Big 10.

"By the time they get to the end, there are not many left. For one, they eliminate each other, but furthermore, they're gassed. They're injured. They have issues. I'm not making excuses. I'm just pointing out facts because you were pointing out facts," she continued.

"I'm not making excuses," then makes excuses. Because ESPN is heavily invested in promoting the SEC, as their biggest media partners.

ESPN announcer Paul Finebaum before the 2024 SEC Championship game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Dec. 7, 2024. (Brett Davis/Imagn Images)

First, we have yet to see what a nine-game schedule does to the SEC. Second, implying that the previous eight-game schedule was just too much for these teams to handle is actually an argument against the strength of the conference. Third, what happened to the SEC being so battle hardened they could handle the rigors of a playoff run? Now they're just too tired.

Let's look at the 2024 Ohio State National Championship team as a counterpoint, shall we? The Buckeyes in 2024 had road games at Oregon, ranked No. 3 in the country at the time, and Penn State, which was also then ranked No. 3. It hosted No. 5 Indiana and finished with an always tough, physical, rivalry game against a solid Michigan team. It played three playoff teams in the regular season, including the No. 1 overall seed, Oregon, and another physical opponent in Iowa. All within seven weeks. Sounds pretty tough!

They then blew out a vaunted SEC team, Tennessee, 42-17, easily handled another top SEC team, Texas, and beat a very good Notre Dame team in the championship game. That's what good teams do. Indiana in 2025 played Ohio State to finish the season, then blew out Alabama, Oregon, and handled Miami to win a title. That's what good teams do.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Stop making excuses and win important games.

Speaking of excuses and Indiana, if there's one head coach who hates them more than anyone, it's Curt Cignetti. The defending champ took a very pointed shot at the SEC and the excuses culture they've created.

Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti speaks during news conference ahead of the College Football Playoff national championship game between Miami and Indiana, Sunday, Jan. 18, 2026, in Miami. The game will be played on Monday. (AP Photo/Chris Carlson)

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

"I mean we don’t run a hype machine up here in the Midwest," Cignetti said on Thursday at Big Ten media days. "We believe everything’s earned, not given. And when we fall short, we say, ‘We fell short.’ We don’t cry a river, whine and complain. All right? And that’s why we’re the best."

Though, to be fair to the SEC, Notre Dame's in the Midwest and boy oh boy did they cry a river, whine, and complain after getting left out of the playoff last season.

He has a point though, about the current strategy around the SEC. For some reason, instead of saying, "hey, we believe we're the best, we'll go through whatever gauntlet we have in front of us, and beat people up in the playoff, because we're the best," they're saying "woe is us, it's just too tough to win games."

Maybe that's the reason the SEC has fallen behind, because they're consumed with talking about the difficult of playing road games at Mississippi State instead of Nebraska. Or Kentucky instead of Wisconsin. Maybe focus on winning, it's a guarantee the rest will take care of itself.

articles.title: Chris Hemsworth shares terrifying footage from 'crazy' plane ride through lightning and severe turbulence
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Chris Hemsworth's latest family vacation took a frightening turn when the actor found himself aboard a small plane caught in the mid...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Chris Hemsworth's latest family vacation took a frightening turn when the actor found himself aboard a small plane caught in the middle of a lightning storm.

On Wednesday, the "Thor" star, 42, captured the Costa Rican family trip with wife Elsa Pataky and their three children in a YouTube vlog, including a "life-threatening" plane ride.

Footage from the trip captured lightning flashing around the aircraft as turbulence shook the cabin. Hemsworth's unease was evident in the clip, as he could be seen mouthing, "What the f---?"

In the caption of the video, Hemsworth also called it a "crazy plane ride."

CHRIS HEMSWORTH SHUTS DOWN CLAIMS ALZHEIMER'S FEARS FORCED HIM TO QUIT HOLLYWOOD: 'REALLY... P---ED ME OFF'

Chris Hemsworth shared terrifying footage from a "life-threatening" flight in Costa Rica. (Getty Images; Chris Hemsworth YouTube)

The flight landed safely, and the scare didn't stop the Hemsworth family from making the most of the vacation.

The action-packed trip featured everything from surfing and ATV riding to cliff jumping, fishing and hiking through waterfalls. At one point, Pataky playfully shoved her husband into a waterfall.

CHRIS HEMSWORTH, BRAD PITT, BEN AFFLECK ARE AMONG MALE STARS GETTING BETTER WITH AGE: PHOTOS

The couple, who married in 2010, share daughter India and twin sons Sasha and Tristan. The family has long embraced an adventurous lifestyle, frequently sharing glimpses of outdoor excursions from their home in Australia and while traveling abroad.

Elsa Pataky and Chris Hemsworth share three children.  (Gisela Schober/Getty Images)

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The vacation scare comes several years after Hemsworth publicly revealed he was rethinking how he approached work and family after a health revelation during filming of National Geographic's "Limitless."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

While undergoing genetic testing for the series, the actor learned he carries two copies of the APOE4 gene, which is linked to an increased risk of developing Alzheimer's disease later in life.

Hemsworth and his family recently took a trip to Costa Rica.  (Tuane Fernandes/picture alliance via Getty Images)

Shortly after the news was made public in 2022, he took a break from acting. Together, the two bits of news led to rumors that he was retiring, or that he'd already developed the disease, which he said was very upsetting to hear.

"It really kind of p---ed me off because it felt like I had been vulnerable with something personal and shared this," he admitted in an interview with Vanity Fair in 2024.

"No matter how much I said, ‘This is not a death sentence,’ the story became that I have dementia, and I’m reconsidering life and retiring and so on."

He then joked, "I did read a really funny comment at the bottom of one article: ‘I hope Chris forgets he’s retiring and comes back.’"

Fox News Digital's Emily Trainham contributed to this post.

Christina Dugan Ramirez is an entertainment journalist with more than 15 years of experience, including a decade at PEOPLE writing high-profile cover stories, covering Hollywood's biggest events, and interviewing many of the industry's most influential stars before joining Fox News Digital in 2024.

articles.title: NFL legend Rob Gronkowski has simple advice for Caitlin Clark: 'Keep shutting up the haters'
articles.excerpt:
Former New England Patriots star Rob Gronkowski tells Caitlin Clark to ‘keep shutting up the haters.’

NFL legend Rob Gronkowski has high praise and some simple advice for Caitlin Clark: "Keep shuttin...
articles.body_text:
Former New England Patriots star Rob Gronkowski tells Caitlin Clark to ‘keep shutting up the haters.’

NFL legend Rob Gronkowski has high praise and some simple advice for Caitlin Clark: "Keep shutting up the haters" with her play.

Amid the rampant discourse about Clark that has dominated the internet, Gronkowski told Fox News Digital in a recent interview that she’s doing a "great job" of handling it all.

"She's doing a great job handling herself. She really is. I'm not in her shoes. I'm not in her situation. If I was, though, I would kind of handle it very similar to how she's handling it. She really is doing a great job," Gronkowski told Fox News Digital in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever dribbles the ball during a game against the Seattle Storm July 28, 2026, at Climate Pledge Arena in Seattle. (NBAE via Getty Images)

"I would just say one piece of advice, keep balling because if you keep balling, you're going to keep shutting up the haters."

The Indiana Fever have won their last four games, and Clark has been great, averaging just over 30 points per game during that winning streak. While Clark has been good, so have her teammates, as Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston have both been key contributors.

Gronkowski praised Clark’s teammates for supporting her throughout the season.

"What I do appreciate, what she's going to need to help with is her teammates. That's who's going to lift you up. If you've got your teammates protecting you, that says a lot right there. It really does. And she does. Her team does pick her up. They protect her as well, and that's huge," Gronkowski told Fox News Digital on behalf of eBay.

NFL LEGEND ROB GRONKOWSKI DETAILS TRAVIS KELCE AND TAYLOR SWIFT'S 'MAGNIFICENT' WEDDING

Caitlin Clark during the WNBA All-Star Game at the United Center (Getty Images)

"That says a lot about your personality and about who you are throughout the season, how you practice, how you prepare, is that if your teammates are behind you, you know that doing the right things."

Gronkowski said Clark will truly be the face of the WNBA once the league steps in and does something about the hard fouls she has received, in addition to winning something significant.

"I think she's going to be the face eventually, like truly where the WNBA steps in and they're like, ‘OK, like enough of all this wishwashing that's going on with her and the punishment that that she's taking out on the basketball court. Let's truly make her to face the league. I think I would say it once she keeps balling out and also wins something pretty significant," Gronkowski said.

The New England Patriots legend said he isn’t a diehard fan and is more of a casual fan of the WNBA. He talked about how in the NFL and NBA, you don’t become the face of the league until you have about "four or five years under their belt."

Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski (Bob Breidenbach/The Providence Journal /USA Today Network via Imagn Images)

Gronkowski, a four-time Super Bowl champion, is one of the greatest tight ends of all time. He spent nine seasons with the Patriots before retiring in 2019. He came out of retirement in 2020 and played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Tom Brady for two seasons before retiring again.

In 11 seasons, the five-time Pro Bowler caught 621 receptions for 9,286 yards and 92 touchdowns.

Clark and the Fever will look to keep it rolling when they play the Portland Fire on Friday at 10 p.m. ET.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X, and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Amazon’s Zoox secures US federal approval for steering-wheel-free robotaxis
articles.excerpt: Zoox, Amazon’s brand of autonomous vehicles, has won approval in the United States for limited commercial deployment of its steering-wheel-free robotaxis, a first for the autonomous transportation ind...
articles.body_text:
Zoox, Amazon’s brand of autonomous vehicles, has won approval in the United States for limited commercial deployment of its steering-wheel-free robotaxis, a first for the autonomous transportation industry.

On Thursday, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) gave its approval for Zoox to begin charging customers for rides, once it secures state and local approval.

As part of that approval, the company was granted an exemption from federal rules that require human controls on motor vehicles.

NHTSA administrator Jonathan Morrison told the Reuters news agency that Zoox had so far met its safety requirements. But he indicated there would be a staggered rollout, and no Zoox vehicles would be immediately available for sale to the public.

“We can say pretty clearly that the systems in place on the Zoox exceed the equivalent performance requirements of a compliant vehicle,” Morrison said. “But we still want to make sure that the automated driving system will operate appropriately.”

According to Morrison, Zoox had received clearance to commercially deploy up to 2,500 vehicles in each of the next two years.

The NHTSA is also placing additional reporting requirements on Zoox for issues such as crashes or stopping inappropriately on roads.

Still, the approval marks a milestone for companies developing robotaxis that deviate from the models of standard motor vehicles.

Zoox’s cars are rectangular, carriage-style vehicles with rows of passenger seats that face each other, rather than both facing forward. The cars can travel up to 120km, or 75 miles, per hour. There is no driver’s seat, nor pedals or a steering wheel.

The company has already began offering free rides in Las Vegas and San Francisco last year. It will soon begin charging for service, first in Las Vegas, with additional markets to follow as it completes state requirements.

Advocates for autonomous vehicles argue that NHTSA’s safety regulations were written before self-driving technology emerged. Such regulations, they say, can impede the development of new models of cars.

Critics, however, warn that loosening restrictions on autonomous vehicles could turn city streets into real-world technology experiments, putting lives at risk.

They point to incidents where driverless vehicles have struck pedestrians or animals, or have stalled in roadways, blocking traffic and emergency vehicles.

Just this month, Morrison issued a letter telling developers of autonomous vehicles (AVs) to “immediately focus” on fixing what NHTSA identified as “a clear pattern of driverless AVs interfering with law enforcement and other first responders”.

Following the letter, Zoox recalled its fleet of 105 autonomous vehicles to update the software, saying they might not detect heavy smoke, particularly in active emergencies.

The Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety group raised concerns about Zoox’s plan to operate without a steering wheel or other standard controls because the company didn’t provide detailed evidence to show that its vehicles could operate safely on public roads.

“Lots of promises, lots of glossy language, lots of ‘We believe, we think we’ll do this.’ Yet there really was no data behind the promises, and that’s really concerning to us,” Peter Kurdock, the group’s general counsel, told The Associated Press news agency.

Zoox and Tesla are working to catch up to the industry-leading Waymo, which already operates in multiple cities.

Waymo is owned by Google’s parent company, Alphabet, and its vehicles are electric Jaguar SUVs, which include steering wheels and pedals for manual control if needed.

Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said this approval is an important milestone for autonomous vehicles.

“This achievement reflects a shared commitment to enabling innovation while maintaining the highest standards of safety,” Evans said.

Amazon hopes to eventually produce as many as 10,000 robotaxis a year at a plant near Silicon Valley as it works to challenge Waymo.

Amazon paid $1.2bn to acquire self-driving startup Zoox. The company said that more than half a million people have already ridden in its vehicles.

articles.title: Washington school district reviewing incident of employee making celebratory remark about Charlie Kirk's death
articles.excerpt:
Legal strategist Katie Zacharia analyzes the Utah County Attorney's push to move the Charlie Kirk assassination case to trial.

A Washington school district says it has launched a review after a woman...
articles.body_text:
Legal strategist Katie Zacharia analyzes the Utah County Attorney's push to move the Charlie Kirk assassination case to trial.

A Washington school district says it has launched a review after a woman identified online as a high school nurse appeared in a confrontation that went viral this week about Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. During the dispute, she allegedly said, "Thank God he's dead."

The Lake Washington School District confirmed to Fox News Digital Wednesday it is aware of the video circulating on social media involving a district employee and said it is reviewing the circumstances while emphasizing that the views expressed do not reflect those of the district.

"Lake Washington School District (LWSD) is aware of a video circulating on social media involving a district staff member," a spokesperson for the school district told Fox News Digital in a statement Wednesday.

"We have received concerns from community members regarding the statements and conduct shown in the video."

OKLAHOMA STATE AGENCY FIRES STAFF ATTORNEY AFTER ANTI-ICE SOCIAL MEDIA TIRADE

Charlie Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, greets supporters during an event in San Diego, Calif., May 1, 2025. (Michael Ho Wai Lee/Getty Images)

In the video shared on X by the account Right Angle News Network, a woman identified in the post as a nurse at Eastlake High School named Kelsey Ballin allegedly says, "Oh my God, thank God he’s dead, bye," after someone else references Charlie Kirk.

She also appears to mockingly blow a kiss, stick out her tongue and give the finger during the incident, which reportedly took place at a farmer's market. Other people in the video were wearing Kirk "Freedom" T-shirts during the incident.

Kirk was assassinated Sept. 10 while speaking at Utah Valley University during his American Comeback Tour.

UTAH VALLEY UNIVERSITY SCRAPS CONTROVERSIAL COMMENCEMENT SPEAKER WHO CRITICIZED CHARLIE KIRK AFTER HIS MURDER

Tyler Robinson, left, is accused of fatally shooting Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, right, at a public speaking event at Utah Valley University in September. (Bethany Baker/Pool via Reuters; Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

Eastlake High School is part of the Lake Washington School District, located in Sammamish, Washington, and serves grades 9 through 12.

"The district takes these concerns seriously," the spokesperson continued. "While we cannot comment on individual personnel matters, district leadership has initiated a review of the circumstances surrounding this incident and will follow established processes as the review moves forward. It is important to note the views expressed in the video do not reflect the values or positions of Lake Washington School District.

"LWSD is committed to providing welcoming, safe and inclusive learning environments for all students, families, staff and community members. We expect all employees to uphold the professional standards and the values of the district and to contribute to a culture of respect, dignity and civil discourse."

WISCONSIN TEACHER FIRED AFTER SOCIAL MEDIA POST ADVOCATING TO 'MAKE AMERICANS GREAT ASSASSINS AGAIN'

UVU students pause to reflect as they gaze over the spot where Charlie Kirk was assassinated, in Orem, Utah, Sept. 17, 2025. (Matthew Finn/Fox News)

"At the same time," the spokesperson added, "district employees retain rights and protections as private citizens. Balancing these principles is central to how the district approaches situations like this one. Because this is an ongoing personnel matter, we are unable to provide additional information at this time. We remain committed to our values as an organization for developing students that are prepared as members of a diverse community."

When asked about its policies governing employees' conduct outside of work and on social media, the district referred Fox News Digital to its staff conduct policy and separate guidance addressing employees' use of social media.

Fox News Digital reached out to Turning Point USA for comment, and was referred to an X post Thursday from Andrew Kolvet, spokesman for TPUSA, where he reshared the X post from Right Angle News Network and wrote, "Why are so many of these awful humans drawn to children, schools, and medicine?"

Fox News Digital reached out to Ballin for comment.

Rachel del Guidice is a culture reporter for Fox News covering the intersection of politics, faith, family, and American culture.

articles.title: Fox News Poll: GOP divisions shape Texas Senate race
articles.excerpt:
Harris Faulkner hosts a 'Voters' Voices' panel, exploring voter motivation, top midterm issues like the economy and the rise of socialism.

President Donald Trump won the Lone Star state by nearly 14 ...
articles.body_text:
Harris Faulkner hosts a 'Voters' Voices' panel, exploring voter motivation, top midterm issues like the economy and the rise of socialism.

President Donald Trump won the Lone Star state by nearly 14 percentage points in 2024, but a new Fox News Poll of Texas registered voters suggests this year's Senate race is far less settled. Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton has yet to fully unify the GOP despite the president’s endorsement in the GOP primary against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn.

In addition, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve than worry Democratic challenger James Talarico is too extreme, and more Democrats than Republicans are extremely motivated to vote (by 7 points) and extremely interested in the midterms (by 6).

Those dynamics give Talarico a 3-point edge over Paxton (51% vs. 48%) in the Senate contest (within the survey’s margin of sampling error).

Talarico's advantage in the race grows to 6 points among both extremely motivated and extremely interested voters (53% vs. 47% in each group).

FOX NEWS POLL: DEMOCRATIC ENTHUSIASM SHAPES NORTH CAROLINA SENATE RACE

Most independents (68%) and virtually all Democrats support Talarico (98%), while fewer Republicans are unified behind Paxton (89%).

In part, that’s because one quarter of non-MAGA Republicans back Talarico (24%).

Paxton is the choice among White evangelical Christians, White men without a college degree, rural voters, regular worship attenders, men and voters ages 65 and older.

Some of Talarico’s best groups are Black voters, moderates, voters under age 30, Hispanic voters, women and voters with a college degree.

"Although Paxton dominated Cornyn in the GOP primary, that bruising contest left scars," said Republican pollster Daron Shaw, who conducts Fox News polls with Democrat Chris Anderson.

"He has considerable work to do with non-MAGA Republicans and independents, and that undoubtedly requires aggressively tying Talarico to the Democratic Party’s far left."

By a 12-point margin, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve as a senator than believe Talarico is too extreme (59% vs. 47%).

Twice as many Republicans are concerned about Paxton's character as Democrats are that Talarico is too extreme (36% vs. 17%).

FOX NEWS POLL: COOL YOUR SERVERS! VOTERS REJECT DATA CENTERS

Still, about 8 in 10 Paxton and Talarico supporters say their backing is more about where the candidates stand on the issues than who they are as people.

Trump received a 55% favorable vs. 44% unfavorable rating in the 2024 Texas Fox News Voter Analysis (FNVA) election survey. Today, those numbers have flipped: 45% favorable vs. 54% unfavorable, for a minus-9 net negative rating.

Paxton garners a minus-6 net personal rating, 45% favorable vs. 51% unfavorable, while Talarico is in positive territory by 6 points, 49% vs. 43%.

Talarico is more popular than the Democratic Party while the GOP edges out Paxton.

While both parties are viewed negatively, the GOP is underwater by only 2 points (48% favorable vs. 50% unfavorable), compared with the Democratic Party at minus-9 (45% vs. 54%).

Despite Texas being a border state, nearly 4 in 10 say inflation will be the most important issue to their Senate vote, while 2 in 10 say immigration and 1 in 10 say healthcare, political divisions and unemployment.

By more than a 2-to-1 margin, Texas voters say they are falling behind financially rather than getting ahead (35% vs. 16%). Half are holding steady.

In the race for governor, incumbent Republican Gov. Greg Abbott is favored by 1 point over Democrat Gina Hinojosa.

Part of Abbott's edge comes from a touch more crossover support: 12% of Talarico supporters back Abbott, while 9% of Paxton supporters back Hinojosa.

Hinojosa has the advantage among extremely motivated (+6) and extremely interested voters (+5).

Abbott has a net positive personal rating by a single point (50% favorable vs. 49% unfavorable). Hinojosa is in positive territory by 11 points (45% vs. 34%), although nearly 1 in 5 are unable to rate her.

Texas last elected a Democratic governor in 1990 (Ann Richards), a Democratic Senator in 1988 (Lloyd Bentsen), and a Democratic presidential candidate in 1976 (Jimmy Carter).

Hispanic voters say their Senate pick will be driven by inflation, as roughly 4 in 10 say it will be the most important issue to their vote and another 4 in 10 say they’re falling behind financially. This mostly matches views among all Texas voters.

And as is the case with voters overall, there is an enthusiasm gap, as more Hispanic Democrats than Hispanic Republicans are interested and motivated to vote in the midterms.

Overall, Hispanic voters prefer Talarico by 18 points (59% vs. 41%).

Some 9% of Hispanic GOP voters crossover to support Talarico while 5% of Hispanic Democrats favor Paxton.

In 2024, Trump topped former Vice President Kamala Harris among Hispanic voters in Texas by 1 point, according to the Texas FNVA survey (49% Harris vs. 50% Trump).

By 20 points, more Hispanic voters are concerned that Paxton lacks the character to serve as senator than feel Talarico is too extreme (61% concerned vs. 41%).

For the governor’s race, Hispanic voters back Hinojosa by 16 points in the new survey. By comparison, they preferred Beto O’Rourke over Abbott by 14 points in 2022.

More than half of Hispanic voters view Talarico (57% favorable), Hinojosa (53%), and the Democratic Party (53%) positively, while more than half have negative views of Paxton (56% unfavorable), Abbott (56%), Trump (61%), and the Republican Party (59%).

Conducted July 23-27, 2026, under the direction of Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company Research (R), this Fox News survey includes interviews with a sample of 1,006 Texas registered voters randomly selected from a statewide voter file. Respondents spoke with live interviewers on landlines (72) and cellphones (681) or completed the survey online after receiving a text (253). Results based on the full sample have a margin of sampling error of ±3 percentage points.

The survey includes an oversample of 296 Hispanic voters, bringing the sample size for that subgroup to 556 (±4). Sampling error for results among subgroups is higher. In addition to sampling errors, question wording and order can influence results. Weights are generally applied to age, race, education and area variables to ensure the demographics are representative of the registered voter population. Sources for developing weight targets include the most recent American Community Survey, Fox News Voter Analysis and voter file data.

articles.title: Argentina’s Milei seeks to deport foreigners that spread ‘hate’ of country
articles.excerpt:
Argentinian President Javier Milei has signed an emergency decree empowering the government to eject foreigners who spread “hate” about the South American nation.

The legality of the measure, signed ...
articles.body_text:
Argentinian President Javier Milei has signed an emergency decree empowering the government to eject foreigners who spread “hate” about the South American nation.

The legality of the measure, signed on Thursday, has already been questioned by experts. The decree allows the government to bar, deport or revoke the visas of those who express “hate” or tarnish national symbols.

In announcing the measure, Milei’s office addressed the global animus Argentina faced after its appearance in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

The country reached the final match of the tournament, but its second-place finish was tarnished by accusations of racism among its players and fans. Milei framed that backlash as a campaign to discredit the country.

“In light of recent displays of hostility toward the Argentine Republic and Argentines, the national government reaffirms that the defence of the nation, its citizens and its symbols is non-negotiable,” the president’s office said.

“Anyone who attacks the Argentine Republic is not welcome in our country.”

The decree comes at a time when many Argentinians have expressed frustration over what they see as unfair criticism of their team during the recent World Cup.

That tournament, which concluded on July 19 with Spain defeating Argentina, prompted speculation about favourable officiating for the Argentinian side.

After the final match ended, a brawl appeared to break out on the football pitch. FIFA this week announced it would initiate a disciplinary probe against three Argentinian players and one coach, citing allegations of “unsporting behaviour”. One Spanish player was also cited.

FIFA also said it would investigate incidents of “discriminatory chants and gestures” and “inappropriate messages” from the Argentinian side.

Many Argentinians expressed frustration to see sports fans around the world, including much of Latin America, rally behind Spain, and the allegations of racism prompted heated discourse on social media.

The libertarian Milei has asserted, without evidence, that global criticism is the result of a coordinated “anti-Argentina campaign” financed by leftists in Brazil, Mexico and the United States Democratic Party.

Brazil recalled its ambassador last weekend in response to those accusations and insults directed at the country’s president and members of its judiciary.

Thursday’s presidential decree in Argentina says that it does not apply to ideological disagreement or political, academic or civic criticism protected under Argentina’s constitution.

But it does not include details about how the term “hate” will be defined and whether immigration authorities will search the social media histories of tourists and foreign residents.

articles.title: President Trump pushes lawmakers on legislation as 'Protect College Sports Act' hangs on by a thread
articles.excerpt:
Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports on a bipartisan effort by lawmakers to regulate college sports contracts on ‘Fox Report.’

It was always going to be an uphill battle to...
articles.body_text:
Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports on a bipartisan effort by lawmakers to regulate college sports contracts on ‘Fox Report.’

It was always going to be an uphill battle to pass the Protect College Sports Act, and now the process is at a crossroads that has gotten the attention of President Donald Trump.

Following negotiations that took place between multiple conferences around college athletics and senators Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) and others, we have officially reached a fork in the road.

There had been numerous phone calls between Big Ten commissioner Tony Petitti and SEC commissioner Greg Sankey over the last 24 hours related to their stance on the Protect College Sports Act, and whether or not each conference was prepared to put their support behind the legislation.

TICK TOCK: SEC AND BIG TEN RECEIVE REVISED PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT AS SENATE VOTE TIMELINE LOOMS

Now, as of Thursday evening, the mood has shifted in the nations capital as to whether this bill will ever make it to the Senate floor.

Earlier in the day, after OutKick-Fox News reached out for comment regarding their stance on the ongoing negotiations, a White House official had this to say about the legislation.

"The White House has been following these negotiations closely, and the President has been actively engaged. President Trump wants to save college sports, and he wants the bill done"

Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks to Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., before a Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee confirmation hearing on President-elect Donald Trump's nomination of Sean Duffy for secretary of transportation in Washington, D.C., on Jan. 15, 2025. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

Clearly, Donald Trump wanted this legislation to make its way to his desk to be signed. But now, even with the potential for Senate Majority Leader John Thune to still bring cloture to a vote on Monday, which would allow the bill to be argued, there is dwindling optimism that anything of note will actually happen at this moment.

Essentially, all parties involved could not come to an agreement on certain language in the bill in time for vote.

"This is the legislation we need now. It will grant student-athletes unprecedented academic, health, and wellness benefits, rein in out-of-control agents, and stabilize transfer, eligibility, and revenue-sharing rules," NCAA President Charlie Baker said in a statement.

"While no bill is perfect, I implore college sports leaders and Senators to support this bill now. It is our best chance to deliver the benefits and level playing field student-athletes deserve while providing the protections institutions need to sustain college athletics long-term."

Obviously, things can change. But, the likelihood of that shrinks every day.

CONGRESS MAY FINALLY HAVE A BIPARTISAN PATH FORWARD ON COLLEGE ATHLETICS WITH CRUZ-CANTWELL LEGISLATION

The bipartisan bill was created to help navigate college athletics in this messy time, and out of courtrooms, with numerous eligibility lawsuits filed within the past week alone.

The back and forth between conference members, along with senators, centered around a number of different issues.

In their concessions to those within the SEC, Big Ten, ACC, Big 12, Notre Dame and Group of Six members, these were topics discussed over the past few days.

Obviously, with the clock ticking to get this legislation to the Senate floor, those in Washington were waiting on conferences to either put their support behind this or move on.

What we learned on Thursday was that it takes a lot longer than four weeks to come to an agreement on potential federal help.

Maybe, universities should just handle this on their own and stop asking Congress for help.

I guess we'll find out for certain over the next week, but the Protect College Sports Act is barely hanging on.

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

articles.title: Trump Education Department probes school after teacher allegedly required same-sex students to kiss
articles.excerpt: Education Secretary Linda McMahon reveals the Trump administration is actively defending parental rights amidst troubling reports from school districts nationwide. McMahon highlights Department of Jus...
articles.body_text:
Education Secretary Linda McMahon reveals the Trump administration is actively defending parental rights amidst troubling reports from school districts nationwide. McMahon highlights Department of Justice investigations in Maryland, Michigan and Vermont, where school boards are accused of encouraging gender transitions and hiding information from parents, some even asking sexually explicit questions in surveys for seventh graders.

The Trump administration has opened a federal investigation into Denver Public Schools after allegations that a high school teacher required students of the same sex to kiss as part of a classroom assignment, the Department of Education announced Tuesday.

"Schools have an obligation to prevent and address sexual assault," Kimberly Richey, assistant secretary for civil rights, said in a statement. "Yet in Colorado, school personnel are alleged to have compelled the sexual assault of minor students by forcing them to engage in blatantly sexualized conduct in class. It is abhorrent and the Trump Administration will fully investigate this perverse incident to protect students’ safety and vigorously uphold students’ rights across America."

The Education Department said it is investigating whether Denver Public Schools violated the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA), a federal law that gives parents the right to opt their children out of certain surveys, evaluations and instructional activities involving sensitive topics, including sexual behavior and attitudes.

COLORADO TEACHER FIRED AFTER STUDENTS ALLEGEDLY PRESSURED TO KISS CLASSMATES IN SKITS

A Denver Public Schools emblem and sign on the Evie Garrett Dennis Campus that houses five separate schools with 1,600 students in Pre-K through 12th grade in Northeast Denver, Colorado on March 16, 2016. (Katie Wood/The Denver Post via Getty Images)

The Department said that it is "investigating incidents that took place at a Denver Public Schools high school involving a teacher who allegedly required students of the same sex to kiss each other in front of the classroom as part of a class assignment."

The Denver Public Schools board voted 7-0 on May 20, CBS News reported, to consider the firing of French language and culture teacher Jennifer Honka at Northeast Early College for "incompetence and neglect of duty," finding she had at times allegedly suggested that students kiss during in-class skits.

An April 30 independent review, a copy of which was obtained by CBS Colorado, found that the students who were allegedly encouraged to kiss were always the same sex.

"One student told an NEC chemistry teacher about the skits in April 2024," CBS News reported. "The student was very uncomfortable and did not know what to do," the report said. "She went ahead and kissed another student at (Honka)'s direction. The student then shared a digital meme with (the chemistry teacher) that included a picture of (Honka) and the caption 'she makes girls kiss.' The meme had circulated among the students."

CBS News also reported that "one student interviewed directly in the independent review also testified that Honka always selected girls to act in the skits. Despite a nearly 50-50 split between boys and girls in the class, the student ‘could not recall Honka choosing a boy actor.’ This student refused to participate and testified that she received a zero score for a grade on this assignment."

TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS WOKE SCHOOLS ACCUSED OF HIDING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

A classroom with students. (Getty Images)

"Parents are entitled by law to be notified if their children will be surveyed or evaluated on sensitive information about sex behaviors or attitudes," the announcement from the Department of Education said. "SPPO will investigate whether parents were notified about this student evaluation and whether parent or student opt-outs or complaints were ignored. Additionally, OCR will investigate whether the District appropriately responded to the incident, consistent with the requirements of Title IX."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for Denver Public Schools said, "Denver Public Schools is reviewing the notice of directed investigation from OCR. It would be too early to comment on their assertions."

"The safety, emotional well-being, and dignity of our students are the absolute highest priorities of DPS," the spokesperson continued. "Our actions to date have been wholly consistent with those priorities. Immediately after learning of student concerns with this teacher in March 2025, the District placed the teacher on administrative leave and completed a thorough investigation. Based on the results of that investigation and an independent review by a state administrative law judge, the DPS Board of Education voted unanimously to terminate the employment of the teacher in May 2026."

"We deeply appreciate the bravery of the students who came forward and the staff who acted immediately as mandatory reporters," the spokesperson added. "We remain fully committed to holding personnel to the highest standards of conduct and ensuring a safe, supportive learning environment for all students."

WASHINGTON MOTHER PULLS CHILDREN FROM SCHOOL AFTER PRIDE LESSON SHOWN IN MUSIC CLASS WITHOUT NOTICE

A Department of Education sign is displayed outside their federal student aid office on May 18, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

The department announced a separate investigation into Washington state's Bethel School District over an LGBTQ Pride Month display that included vials labeled as testosterone.

In June, the school district said administrators discovered testosterone vials "that still contained a small amount of unknown liquid" included in a Pride Month display at Graham-Kapowsin High School and removed them after concluding the items had not been approved by school leadership.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Bethel School District said, "We are aware of the U.S. Department of Education investigation and will be cooperating in any way we can. In early June, district officials were made aware of a display at Graham-Kapowsin High School that included empty vials of testosterone as one of its visuals. The display also contained some vials that still contained a small amount of unknown liquid."

"The inclusion of the vials was entirely unauthorized and did not receive approval from school leadership or administration," the spokesperson continued. "Administrators immediately removed the vials and identified the individuals responsible for adding them without leadership approval. The vials were then turned over to the Pierce County Sheriff's Office."

"We are also actively reviewing our display oversight protocols to ensure all school materials strictly align with our educational standards and community expectations," the spokesperson added. "Our primary focus remains on maintaining a safe, respectful, and focused learning environment for all of our students."

Rachel del Guidice is a culture reporter for Fox News covering the intersection of politics, faith, family, and American culture.

articles.title: ABC accuses FCC of 'retaliation' as federal agency threatens to revoke Disney's broadcasting licenses
articles.excerpt:
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr tells Fox News Digital that broadcasters need to operate in the public interest and airing a significant presidential address is part of the deal.

ABC submitted a scathing f...
articles.body_text:
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr tells Fox News Digital that broadcasters need to operate in the public interest and airing a significant presidential address is part of the deal.

ABC submitted a scathing filing to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Wednesday in opposition to petitions to deny its stations' license renewals.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr called the licenses of eight ABC-owned stations for early renewal in April. The Disney-owned ABC station's licenses were originally scheduled to be renewed between 2028 and 2031, but the FCC expedited the process amid ongoing tensions between the Trump administration and ABC late-night host Jimmy Kimmel.

The eight stations must demonstrate they have been operating in the public interest as part of an ongoing look at Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) practices. While the FCC filing did not specifically mention Kimmel, ABC argues the action is retaliatory.

CONSERVATIVE GROUPS URGE FCC TO BACK OFF ABC LICENSE REVIEW, WARNING IT COULD HURT RIGHT-LEANING MEDIA

"There is no question why the Commission is singling out these eight stations: Each is owned by ABC, and the Administration has openly and repeatedly called for the revocation of ABC’s licenses, because it dislikes the content and viewpoints expressed on ABC network programs," ABC’s legal team wrote.

Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

KFSN-TV in Fresno, KABC-TV in Los Angeles, KGO-TV in San Francisco, WLS-TV in Chicago, WABC-TV in New York, WTVD in Durham, N.C., WPVI-TV in Philadelphia and KTRK-TV in Houston are the Disney-owned stations in question.

"The outpouring of support for the Stations has been unprecedented for a license renewal proceeding," ABC wrote.

CONSERVATIVE WATCHDOG TELLS FCC THAT 'THE VIEW' IS A DEMOCRATIC PARTY OPERATION, NOT A NEWS PROGRAM

"Over 140,000 comments have been received from the Stations’ local communities—from individual viewers to local police and firefighters, charities, businesses, and schools—and over 95% support the Stations," the filing continued. "These supporters span the ideological spectrum but share a fundamental commitment to free speech and press freedom. This record demonstrates that the Stations serve the public interest with distinction."

ABC issued a scathing filing protesting the FCC's actions, calling it "retaliation." (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto)

ABC insists the FCC "has spent the last 18 months searching for some pretext for revoking the Stations’ licenses," but "has found none, because the Stations easily meet the standard for license renewal—which under the law means that the Commission cannot revoke their licenses or order a hearing on their renewal applications."

The Trump administration has beef with Kimmel, who lampoons the president on a regular basis and whose controversial "expectant widow" joke earlier this year resulted in first lady Melania Trump calling for him to be fired. The FCC has also launched a probe into ABC daytime show "The View," and Carr recently took exception to the Disney-owned network declining to air Trump’s primetime address on linear television.

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

"The retaliation against ABC is a signal to every media company in the country: accommodate the Administration’s view of what news coverage should look like or pay the price. Across the government, regulatory and contracting carrots and sticks have been trained on other disfavored speakers. The tools vary; the objective does not: a media industry too fearful of official reprisal to report the news freely," ABC wrote.

"Calling up the license of a single Station—let alone all eight at once—while the Commission’s DEI investigation has found no violation is unnecessary, premature, and punitive," ABC continued in the filing. "Even if any violation were ever substantiated, the Commission has a graduated set of well-established remedies far short of the corporate death penalty of license non-renewal."

ABC's "The View" has been at the center of the FCC's battle with the Disney-owned stations. (Lou Rocco/Getty Images)

An FCC spokesperson issued the following statement: "For decades, Americans of all stripes have been subsidizing broadcast media to the tune of many billions of dollars by giving TV stations free use of a valuable, public resource—the airwaves. In exchange, broadcasters are required by law to operate in the public interest—not in the narrow or partisan interests of a political party. Broadcasters know that they are prohibited from engaging in invidious forms of DEI discrimination, that they must comply with political equal opportunity regulations, and that they are barred from running broadcast hoaxes or distorting the news. The FCC is going to hold broadcasters accountable to the full extent of the law, regardless of any disinformation campaign that some of them may choose to run."

The Media Research Center (MRC), the conservative watchdog group that previously filed a petition in support of the early review of ABC's broadcasting licenses, doubled down on its stance.

"ABC's defense boils down to this: 'Trust us.' Americans do not, which is why confidence in the media is at historic lows," MRC president David Bozell told Fox News Digital. "Our filing is not based on hurt feelings or political disagreement. It is based on documented conduct. We look forward to the FCC reviewing the facts rather than the distractions."

Brian Flood is a media editor/reporter for FOX News Digital. Story tips can be sent to brian.flood@fox.com and on Twitter: @briansflood.

The association also says social media is driving a surge in cosmetic dental procedures.
