A Georgia mother used a gas pump to fend off a man accused of trying...
articles.body_text:
Surveillance footage captures the frantic moments before police arrested a man accused of attempted kidnapping. (Obtained by WAGA)

A Georgia mother used a gas pump to fend off a man accused of trying to snatch her children at a gas station, with newly released surveillance video capturing the frightening encounter.

The video, obtained by FOX 5 Atlanta, shows the woman pumping gas at a Shell station in Marietta around midnight last week when a shirtless, barefoot man, later identified by police as 30-year-old Jerahn Tucker, approached the family's vehicle.

Marietta Police Department Public Information Officer Charles McPhilamy said Tucker initially spoke with the woman before the encounter suddenly escalated.

FAMILY STOPPED ALLEGED CHILD KIDNAPPER AS POLICE SAY STAFFING SHORTAGE DELAYED RESPONSE UP TO 40 MINUTES

"He appears to charge at the car," McPhilamy said. "He's trying to open the car doors. He's trying to pull the child out of the back seat."

Surveillance video shows a mother pumping gas moments before police say a shirtless man approached her family's vehicle and attempted to grab her children at a Shell station in Marietta, Georgia. (WAGA)

A warrant cited by FOX 5 Atlanta says the mother later told investigators Tucker claimed he had a gun before becoming aggressive.

Surveillance video shows one of the woman's children jumping from the vehicle and running around it as Tucker chased after him. At one point, Tucker opened the rear passenger door while another child remained inside the vehicle.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The mother then grabbed the gas pump hose and used it to keep Tucker away from her children until two bystanders rushed over to help, the video shows.

Surveillance video captures the mother using a gas pump hose to keep the suspect away from her children as police say he tried to pull one of them from the family's vehicle. (WAGA)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

"What is this individual capable of?" McPhilamy said. "What are they doing? Why are they trying to get in my own car? What are they doing? Trying to pull children out of the car."

Two witnesses dropped what they were carrying and rushed over to help as someone called 911, FOX 5 Atlanta reported.

Tucker got into his vehicle and drove away, but officers stopped him a short distance from the gas station and took him into custody.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Surveillance footage shows a man police identified as Jerahn Tucker trying to open the family's vehicle as the mother confronts him during the alleged attempted kidnapping at a Marietta gas station. (WAGA)

"The actions of the mother and everyone on the scene, their ability to remain calm under pressure and push him away, get him away from the children, get a hold of us so that we can get to the area allowed us to hold this individual accountable," McPhilamy told the station.

Tucker remains in the Cobb County Jail on charges including kidnapping and simple assault.

Authorities have not released a possible motive for the alleged attack.

Greg Wehner is a reporter for Fox News Digital covering U.S. news and crime, with a focus on breaking developments, law enforcement, public safety and major stories shaping communities across the country.

articles.title: Sending ace pitcher Tarik Skubal to the Los Angeles Dodgers would officially ruin baseball
articles.excerpt: Guest Host Danny Polishchuk is joined by Cody Tucker and Big Herc to analyze Dr. Anthony Fauci pleading the Fifth on Capitol Hill. Plus, prison live-stream culture, First Amendment auditors, and viral...
articles.body_text:
Guest Host Danny Polishchuk is joined by Cody Tucker and Big Herc to analyze Dr. Anthony Fauci pleading the Fifth on Capitol Hill. Plus, prison live-stream culture, First Amendment auditors, and viral Central Park scandals.

At the end of July, the Los Angeles Dodgers are overwhelming favorites to win the World Series. They are also the team most likely to add the best pitcher in baseball.

According to ESPN insider Jeff Passan, the Detroit Tigers will trade ace Tarik Skubal by the deadline on Monday at 6 p.m.. He adds that most teams anticipate the Dodgers will be the team that acquires him.

"[The rest of MLB] is all almost resigned to the idea that the Los Angeles Dodgers are going to get Tarik Skubal," Passan said Wednesday.

"That's my guess, [that Skubal is traded to the Dodgers], yes," Passan added in a Threads Q&A this week.

The prediction markets tell a similar story. Kalshi gives the Dodgers a 49% chance of trading for Skubal before the deadline. The market also gives them a 53% chance of having Skubal on their roster by Opening Day 2027.

Bob Nightengale reported Thursday that the Dodgers are Skubal's "preferred destination" once he reaches free agency after the season.

Translation: It would be surprising if Skubal is not a Dodger by Monday night.

Detroit Tigers' Tarik Skubal (29) pitches against the Athletics during the first inning of a baseball game Tuesday, July 7, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Duane Burleson) (Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.)

MONICA MCNUTT IS TRYING TO BECOME THE FEMALE RYAN CLARK WITH LATEST CAITLIN CLARK SME

We understand the argument that no one superteam can "ruin" baseball due to the inherent randomness of the sport. Fair enough. Still, it doesn't bode well for the competitive balance of a league when the only real argument against the Dodgers winning a third straight World Series is that randomness could intervene.

Here's what the Dodgers' postseason rotation could look like if they acquire Skubal:

The Dodgers already have the best rotation in baseball. Adding Skubal, whom many consider the best pitcher in the sport, could mark the greatest pitching rotation ever assembled.

And that's before considering the lineup.

The Dodgers already own the best record in baseball and the league's best run differential (+156). They've done so despite extended injuries to Snell and Glasnow. However dominant they've looked through four months, they should be notably better by October.

Traditionally, dynasties are good for professional sports. Casual fans tune in hoping someone finally knocks off the team at the top. But that only works if fans believe someone actually can.

That's the difference between these Dodgers and, say, the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Chiefs won three Super Bowls in five years. They fielded the less talented roster in at least four of those Super Bowls.

No such dynasty exists for the Dodgers. They are clearly better than everyone else – and getting even better.

Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal reacts after striking out Chicago White Sox third baseman Colson Montgomery with the bases loaded to end the fifth inning at Comerica Park in Detroit, Michigan, on June 19, 2026. (Lon Horwedel/Imagn Images)

Consider this: all 29 other teams would improve by adding Skubal. Yet the team that needs him the least is considered the overwhelming favorite to acquire him. That's not good for the sport.

The intrigue would be greater if a contender like the Brewers landed Skubal, narrowing the gap between themselves and Los Angeles. (Don't put too much stock into regular-season records. Milwaukee finished with a better record than the Dodgers last season, yet wasn't remotely competitive in the NLCS.)

For all the issues the NBA has faced over the past several years, competitive balance has quietly become one of its strengths. Eight different franchises have won the past eight championships. Looking ahead, several teams have a realistic chance to win the title next season.

That is also true for the NFL and NHL. Not MLB, where it feels like the Dodgers and the slim chance that randomness intervenes.

ESPN play-by-play announcer Joe Buck, a lifelong baseball fan, agrees. During an interview this week with Jayson Stark and Doug Glanville, Buck said baseball has a competitive imbalance that doesn't exist in the other major sports.

"When I'm doing an NFL season, at the start of the season, who knows who's going to end up in the Super Bowl," Buck explained.

President Donald Trump and Mookie Betts shake hands in the East Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., on Monday, April 7, 2025. Trump is hosting the Los Angeles Dodgers to celebrate their 2024 World Series victory. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Baseball has built notable momentum in recent years. The pitch clock has improved the viewing experience. The league has recognizable stars. The on-field product is strong. However, MLB risks undermining that progress if one team continues separating itself while much of the league sits on the sidelines, content to prioritize profits over building a competitive roster.

The Dodgers deserve no criticism for taking advantage of the system. Their ownership is doing exactly what fans want owners to do: spend money to win. The problem is the system itself. Too many clubs ask fans to support the product while refusing to invest enough to compete with the sport's elite.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

If correcting that imbalance requires a lockout and meaningful structural changes after this season, perhaps it's warranted.

There's a reason spoilers are met with such disdain. Fans don't want to know the ending before they watch the story unfold.

If/when the Dodgers land Tarik Skubal, a spoiler alert for the ending of this MLB season may be apropos.

articles.title: California scientists developing shark-spotting robot ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
articles.excerpt: Jesse Watters hosts Chris Fischer, founder of OCEARCH, to discuss the early surge in shark attacks this summer. Recent incidents include a New York beach closure due to bull sharks, a swimmer bitten i...
articles.body_text:
Jesse Watters hosts Chris Fischer, founder of OCEARCH, to discuss the early surge in shark attacks this summer. Recent incidents include a New York beach closure due to bull sharks, a swimmer bitten in Queens, and a child attacked in knee-deep water in Florida. Fischer notes a rebound in shark populations to 1960s levels, advising beachgoers to avoid swimming when bait fish are active to stay safe.

The world’s best athletes will descend on Southern California for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. And apparently, some of the locals are already circling the competition venues.

Scientists at California State University Long Beach are developing a solar-powered shark-surveillance robot that could help protect athletes and beachgoers during the Games.

The robotic vessel would patrol coastal waters, scanning for tagged sharks, collecting water samples and launching an aerial drone while sending real-time information to lifeguards.

SHARK WEEK SHOCKER AS GREAT WHITE BREACHES JUST YARDS FROM OBLIVIOUS BOOGIE BOARDER

If people are alerted to a shark attack near them, it's much less likely they will also be bitten, experts say. (iStock)

The craft is approximately 10 feet long and about as wide as a paddleboard, according to NBC Los Angeles. Once fully operational, it could patrol specific beaches on its own for as long as a week at a time.

"It will have a drone on it (to) fly around and find sharks," Shark Lab Director Chris Lowe said. "It will be listening for acoustically tagged sharks. It will take water samples to look for white shark DNA."

That could come in handy in 2028, when Southern California hosts Olympic events both in and around the ocean.

Open-water swimming is scheduled to take place in Long Beach, while surfing will be held farther south in Orange County.

"We are going to have athletes swimming in Long Beach harbor, where we know there has been white sharks before," Lowe explained, "so having this device patrolling for lifeguards will help them better protect athletes."

The LA 28 logo is photographed at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, the venue for track and field events, ahead of the LA 28 Summer Olympics on July 22, 2026. (dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images)

The goal is not to sound the alarm every time a shark swims nearby. Sharks already frequent Southern California beaches, usually without bothering anyone.

Instead, the technology would give lifeguards more information when deciding whether conditions warrant warning swimmers or clearing the water.

"Our data suggests that there are sharks around our beaches all the time without incident, but knowing what sharks, and how many are out there help lifeguards make better decisions in beach safety operations and in advising the public," Lowe said.

'SHARK WEEK' HOST FORREST GALANTE EXPLAINS WHY CRUSHING BEERS IN THE OFFICE IS A BAD IDEA

The Shark Lab has already tagged hundreds of juvenile white sharks and currently uses aerial drones and underwater listening stations to track their movements along the California coast. The new surveillance vessel would bring several of those tools together in one platform.

There is still work to be done, though, before a fleet of robotic shark spotters begins protecting Olympians.

"Lots of research and development still needed," the Shark Lab acknowledged. "But we’re off to a great start."

Caroline Marks of Team United States rides a wave during the surfing quarterfinals on day six of the Olympic Games Paris 2024 on Aug. 1, 2024, in Teahupo'o, French Polynesia. (Getty Images)

Funding could also become an obstacle. State funding that helped the Shark Lab build the vessel is reportedly scheduled to expire this fall, potentially forcing researchers to scale back some of their shark-monitoring efforts.

That's a problem because the surveillance robot relies on sharks being tagged in the first place.

"It won’t work if we don’t have tagged sharks out there, so we got to keep tagging sharks," Lowe said.

The Olympics provide an obvious deadline for the new technology, but Lowe said the program is intended to continue well beyond the 2028 Games.

articles.title: Fired HGTV host Nicole Curtis faces Detroit lawsuit alleging her blighted property is a public nuisance
articles.excerpt:
"Zombie House Flipping" star Tommy Harr tells Fox News Digital how rushed home flips and poor inspections are leaving families stuck with costly repairs.

Former HGTV host and queen of rehabbing old h...
articles.body_text:
"Zombie House Flipping" star Tommy Harr tells Fox News Digital how rushed home flips and poor inspections are leaving families stuck with costly repairs.

Former HGTV host and queen of rehabbing old houses Nicole Curtis is in hot water again.

Curtis, former star of the home design and remodeling network's long-running "Rehab Addict," is being sued, along with her company, Detroit Renovations LLC, by the City of Detroit, which alleges she failed to maintain and restore a blighted house in the city.

The civil nuisance-abatement lawsuit alleges the property has continued to be a public nuisance despite Curtis and her company receiving multiple code violations and a 2021 court order requiring the home's renovation.

CANCELED HGTV HOST NICOLE CURTIS FACES SOCIAL MEDIA STORM AFTER ATTEMPTING TO EXPLAIN RACIAL SLUR

Nicole Curtis renovating a home. (Nicole Curtis)

Curtis obtained ownership of the property in 2021 after litigation with the Detroit Land Bank Authority, according to The Detroit News. At that time, Wayne County Circuit Judge Timothy Kenny deemed the 1921 American foursquare-style home a danger to the community and ordered it to be refurbished.

Since then, the city has cited the owner for failing to repair or replace damaged, defective and missing exterior features, as well as failing to repair the roof and gutters, among several other violations. Overall, the city claims the property has never been brought into compliance, causing it to further deteriorate.

Fox News Digital reached out to Curtis for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

HGTV CANCELS NICOLE CURTIS' 'REHAB ADDICT' AFTER STAR WAS CAUGHT USING RACIAL SLUR ON SET

In this March 8, 2021, file photo, a house in need of repair sits along East Grand Boulevard in Detroit. (John Greilick/Detroit News via AP)

Curtis' specialty has always been preserving and restoring 19th- and early 20th-century homes while ensuring they retain their original style and historical character. She has focused much of her work on homes in Detroit and Minneapolis.

Curtis was fired by HGTV in February after video surfaced of her uttering the n-word while filming "Rehab Addict" two years earlier.

Specifically, Curtis blurted out the word "fart" followed by the n-word while standing on a ladder installing wiring.

After realizing what she had said, she immediately asked for the moment to be deleted.

"What the f--- is that that I just said? Nick, you gotta, you gotta, can you kill that?" Curtis is heard saying after uttering the phrase in frustration.

HGTV canceled Nicole Curtis' "Rehab Addict" after the star was caught using a racial slur on set. (Getty Images)

The video was posted by Radar Online on Feb. 11, the same day the series was scheduled to return to television after a three-year hiatus, followed by a second break in July 2025 due to what Curtis described as a "personal setback." HGTV canceled the series permanently in February after the footage became public. It also pulled the show from all of its platforms.

In a statement to TMZ, HGTV said it was "recently made aware of an offensive racial comment made during the filming of Rehab Addict. Not only is language like this hurtful and disappointing to our viewers, partners, and employees — it does not align with the values of HGTV."

Curtis apologized for the remark and expressed "remorse and regret." She later addressed the incident in greater detail on "The Breakfast Club" show.

Nicole Curtis attempted to explain her use of a racial slur during an appearance on "The Breakfast Club." (Getty Images; The Breakfast Club YouTube)

Curtis — who admitted she was ready to have an "open conversation" about the incident — was challenged by hosts Charlamagne tha God and DJ Envy over her language.

"Do you have boys? Boys talk about farts all the time," Curtis, who admitted to often using the terms "fart digger" and "fart knocker," said. "OK, again, I can’t swear on my show. OK, so yes, I’ve made up these crazy words."

Fox News Digital's Christina Dugan Ramirez contributed to this report.

articles.title: US Senate rejects bid to rein in Trump’s authority over Iran war
articles.excerpt:
Measure fails 49-50 as US launches new retaliatory attacks in Iran and lawmakers question the prolonged conflict

The US Senate on Thursday rejected a largely symbolic effort to limit Donald Trump’s a...
articles.body_text:
Measure fails 49-50 as US launches new retaliatory attacks in Iran and lawmakers question the prolonged conflict

The US Senate on Thursday rejected a largely symbolic effort to limit Donald Trump’s authority to wage war in Iran, amid rising regional tensions after the US conducted a “heavy wave” of retaliatory airstrikes.

The war powers resolution failed in a 49-50 vote, marking the second time in two weeks the chamber has taken up legislation aimed at forcing Trump to end hostilities.

The US military said it launched a fresh wave of airstrikes in Iran on Wednesday, in retaliation for an Iranian missile attack targeting a US base in Jordan. The exchange marked an escalation in the Iran war, following the collapse of a ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

The Pennsylvania senator John Fetterman voted with Republicans to sink the measure, the only Democrat to do so. The Republican senators Susan Collins, of Maine, Lisa Murkowski, of Alaska, and Rand Paul, of Kentucky, crossed the aisle to vote in favor of the motion, which would have directed Trump to withdraw US forces from hostilities with Iran absent explicit congressional authorization.

Mitch McConnell was absent for the vote as he continues to recover from a fall in June and has not received medical clearance to return to work.

The vote is the latest sign of eroding patience with a conflict that has now stretched more than five months, far beyond the “four to five weeks” Trump predicted when he co-launched the war with Israel against Iran on 28 February, killing the country’s supreme leader, Ali Khamenei. The often twisty aim has been to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and to curb its support for militant proxies across the Middle East, though under its new leadership the regime seems more inclined to pursue a bomb than ever before.

Iran responded by striking US bases and allied targets across the Gulf region and by disrupting oil traffic through the strait of Hormuz, triggering a global energy shock. A ceasefire brokered in June collapsed within weeks, and fighting resumed with a nearly two-week escalation in July before a renewed pause.

At least 18 US service members have so far been killed in the conflict and more than 450 wounded, according to Pentagon figures, which Democratic lawmakers have questioned over a lack of transparency. Four of those deaths came within a 48-hour span in mid-July, when service members were killed in an attack at Muwaffaq Salti air base in Jordan. Thousands of Iranian civilians and combatants are estimated to have died. The Pentagon has told Congress it needs roughly $80bn more to sustain the war effort, on top of the more than $37bn already spent.

The Senate approved a war powers resolution for the first time in late June, in a 50-48 vote that saw Collins, Paul, Murkowski and Louisiana’s Bill Cassidy break with their party. Trump confronted the defecting Republicans at the Capitol the next day, and Paul and Cassidy both reversed their votes within 24 hours, allowing the Senate to kill a nearly identical measure by a similarly narrow margin.

Since then, the chamber has rejected the legislation repeatedly. The Senate Democratic leader, Chuck Schumer, noted after one earlier defeat that a growing number of Republicans had nonetheless broken ranks over the course of the war.

The House, unlike the Senate, has twice passed its own symbolic resolution calling on Trump to end the war, most recently by 214-208 in late July, with a handful of Republicans joining Democrats. Because the House measure is a concurrent resolution rather than a joint one, it does not carry the force of law and would not go to Trump’s desk even if the Senate followed suit. The Trump administration has separately argued that the 1973 War Powers Resolution, which set out Congress’s authority to check presidential military action, is itself unconstitutional.

The scale of the political problem for Trump was underscored by a new poll from the Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research, released on Thursday. About two-thirds of US adults said the war has not been worthwhile, versus 33% who said it was worth fighting. That includes the vast majority of Democrats and independents, as well as roughly 37% of Republicans.

Ahead of Thursday’s vote, the senator Kirsten Gillibrand, of New York, urged colleagues to back the resolution, arguing that the war was straining household budgets and that Congress held the constitutional authority to end it immediately.

“This reckless war is driving up monthly bills and making everyday life harder for working families,” she said. “Under the constitution, we have the power to end the war today – let’s use it!”

articles.title: Dem senator swipes credit for bill he opposed amid heated reelection bid: 'Disturbing pattern'
articles.excerpt: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth testifies before the Senate, defending the administration's 1.5 trillion dollar budget request as a "generational investment" crucial for military readiness and troop wel...
articles.body_text:
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth testifies before the Senate, defending the administration's 1.5 trillion dollar budget request as a "generational investment" crucial for military readiness and troop welfare. Hegseth states that training will be curtailed without urgent funding, blaming previous administrations for "funding shortfalls" and "deferred maintenance." He argues the budget is necessary to "catch up and get ahead" for soldiers and sailors.

Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., is touting his advocacy for federal investment in Georgia military infrastructure despite having ultimately voted against the bill that secured the improvements.

Most recently, Ossoff highlighted new construction for an elementary school at Fort Benning, improved conditions at Fort Stewart, pay raises for military personnel and improvements to Georgia’s foster care system — all a part of the annual military funding bill known as Military Construction and Veteran Affairs (MilCon-VA).

At the time of its initial passage, Ossoff quickly released a press statement.

FOX NEWS POLL: AN EARLY LOOK AT THE GEORGIA SENATE RACE

(Eric Lee/Bloomberg via Getty Images) (Eric Lee/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"U.S. Senate passes Sen. Ossoff’s Bipartisan Bill that provides most funding for Georgia military construction in 15 years," his website announced.

When reconsidering it for final passage, Ossoff opposed the package.

Notably, Ossoff, as the ranking member on the Senate Subcommittee on Military Construction and Veteran Affairs, voted in favor of the bill in committee and as a standalone bill, but opposed its final passage later that year when it was bundled together with other government funding legislation.

When asked about the voting record, his office reaffirmed the federal support secured in Georgia.

"Let's be clear: Georgia's massive 2026 military construction budget, the highest in 15 years, is a direct and undeniable result of Senator Ossoff's work as the senior Democrat on the Military Construction subcommittee," an Ossoff campaign spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"Senator Ossoff makes no apology for having tried to stop Mike Collins from doubling premiums for more than a million Georgians and throwing 300,000 off their health insurance," they added, referring to Ossoff's Republican challenger, Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., and caps on federal health subsidies Republicans had championed at the time of MilCon-VA's passage.

Like many Democrats, Ossoff has struggled to oppose legislation championed by President Donald Trump while at the same time making his case for reelection in one of the country’s most competitive Senate seats. Ossoff won in 2021 with a 50.6% to 49.4% victory over Republican incumbent Sen. David Perdue, R-Ga.

In the case of the elementary school, Ossoff said he had been calling for those investments for years.

"I have been working for years now for a replacement for Dexter Elementary. That’s really important for those families down there in Columbus," Ossoff said. "I’m just a bit concerned by the lack of attention in this year’s base budget, so we’ll work together on that."

Ossoff made similar remarks about improvements to Fort Stewart, citing concerns in press releases about lead exposure affecting newborns' health on the base, mold contamination and flooded living areas.

Ossoff released findings in a seven-page report about the base’s conditions.

SEN. BLUMENTHAL, REP. TAKANO: CONGRESS CAN FUND VETERANS’ CARE WITHOUT TAKING BENEFITS FROM DISABLED HEROES

Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., speaks during an interview at Dobbins Air Reserve Base, Saturday, April 26, 2025, in Marietta, Georgia. (AP)

"Our military service members and their families make huge sacrifices for the country, and it’s a travesty how they’re being treated by privatized housing contractors in Georgia and nationwide," Sen. Ossoff said.

"The stories in this report should shock our conscience, and I will continue exposing the mistreatment of military families in privatized housing and working to protect them and improve conditions."

Notably, the package Ossoff ultimately voted against contained $8 million for Fort Stewart and $127.4 million to replace the Dexter Elementary School.

A veteran lawmaker ripped Ossoff for highlighting wins he didn’t participate in.

"Last year, he tried to take credit for my veterans housing bill, legislation he had absolutely nothing to do with. A politician who tries to erase a veteran’s work for political gain has forfeited the trust of the people he seeks to represent," Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Wisc., said in a statement, referring to a bill he introduced last year.

Ossoff highlighted the bill on his website, calling it a "bipartisan bill backed by U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff" and announcing that "Sen. Ossoff brings Republicans and Democrats together to protect veterans from foreclosure."

Ossoff was not a sponsor of the bill and, because it passed unanimously in a voice vote, did not cast a vote for it either.

DEM SENATOR ACCUSED OF BEING 'NOWHERE TO BE FOUND' ON CRUCIAL ISSUE IMPACTING KIDS IN SWING STATE

Senator Jon Ossoff, a Democrat from Georgia, during a news conference following the weekly Senate Democrat policy luncheon at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Dec. 9, 2025. (Aaron Schwartz/Bloomberg/Getty Images)

"Ossoff’s disturbing pattern of taking credit for work he didn’t do and claiming victories he didn’t support demonstrates both gross incompetence and a complete lack of integrity," Van Orden said.

Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

articles.title: 'Lord of the Rings' star Sean Astin had to sell his home after negotiating 'small' salary for hit movie
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Sean Astin captured the hearts of fantasy fans everywhere when he starred as Samwise Gamgee in the "Lord of the Rings" but says the ...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Sean Astin captured the hearts of fantasy fans everywhere when he starred as Samwise Gamgee in the "Lord of the Rings" but says the compensation was not what one would expect.

In a new interview with The Guardian, the 55-year-old actor shared just how "small" his payday was for the successful Academy Award-winning trilogy.

"I was not prepared for that level of visibility and access," he said. "And there was a disconnect between the attention that I was getting and how much money we had. It was not a lot of money. In fact, I had to sell my house because I negotiated such a small amount on the trilogy."

He revealed in a November 2017 interview on the "Jim and Sam Show" that he made $250,000 for his work on the trilogy in addition to some profit from merchandise sales, but no residuals.

Astin shared that his paycheck for "Lord of the Rings" was not as big as everyone probably thinks. (New Line/courtesy Everett Collection; Frazer Harrison/WireImage)

'MARRIED... WITH CHILDREN' STAR TED MCGINLEY REVEALS HE GETS PENNY RESIDUAL CHECKS FROM HIS HIT TV SHOWS

The "Stranger Things" star said he had purchased a home in Los Angeles and was told he needed to make $250,000 a year to pay the mortgage when he got the role in the films.

"It was an offer for $250,000 for a year and a half," he said. "And I was like, ‘Wait a minute, my pen signed this contract, which obligated me to $250,000 a year, and I’m gonna sign this contract, which will make it so that I absolutely cannot satisfy that other thing.'"

He added that, in the end, it was all about negotiating. He also clarified that by the time the third movie was released, he "was feeling a little bit better" in terms of finances.

"By then, I had done a lot of other work, and we were fine," he added.

Astin's co-star in the first installment of the trilogy, Cate Blanchett, who played Galadriel, also spoke about how little she was paid for her role, telling Andy Cohen in an August 2024 episode of "Watch What Happens Live," "No one got paid anything to do that movie."

Astin said he was paid $250,000 for all three films combined. (JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I wanted to work with the guy who made 'Braindead,'" she said about why she took the role despite the low pay. "I mean, I basically got free sandwiches. And I got to keep my ears, which is something."

Other cast members, including Orlando Bloom and Elijah Wood, have also spoken about how little they were paid for their work in the films, with Bloom telling Howard Stern in 2019 he was paid $175,000 for the trilogy.

Also starring Viggo Mortensen, Sean Bean and Ian McKellen, the trilogy became a huge blockbuster success.

The first film, "Fellowship of the Ring," raked in about $897 million at the worldwide box office, with its sequels bringing in about $945 million and $1.15 billion, respectively.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The films also starred Sean Bean, Ian McKellan, Elijah Wood, Orlando Bloom and others. (Frank Micelotta/ImageDirect)

All three films were also critically acclaimed, earning a combined 30 Academy Award nominations and 17 wins. The third film alone, "Return of the King," won all 11 categories it was nominated in, including best picture, tying the record for the most Oscars won by a single film.

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Jimmy Hoffa's family marks 51 years since iconic disappearance
articles.excerpt:
'Riddle: The Search for James R. Hoffa' is available to stream on Fox Nation. Hosted by Eric Shawn, the show explores the 1975 disappearance of the legendary Teamsters union president.

Jimmy Hoffa di...
articles.body_text:
'Riddle: The Search for James R. Hoffa' is available to stream on Fox Nation. Hosted by Eric Shawn, the show explores the 1975 disappearance of the legendary Teamsters union president.

Jimmy Hoffa disappeared 51 years ago today, and his family has not given up hope that the answers to their painful loss will finally come.

"We want the case solved," Hoffa's son, James P. Hoffa, the former five-term president of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, told Fox News. "The family wants to have accountability for this horrible crime. We want the case solved so that the family can have closure."

Despite the passage of time, the FBI says the case remains ongoing and active. The bureau’s Detroit office is in charge of the case.

"The FBI has worked for five decades to investigate Jimmy Hoffa's disappearance, following every lead and carefully examining all evidence related to this investigation," the bureau said in a statement to Fox News.

TIPSTER CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER POLICE SAY ANONYMOUS CALL HELPED SOLVE 30-YEAR DISAPPEARANCE

Fifty-one years after Teamsters leader Jimmy Hoffa disappeared, his family says it still hopes investigators will uncover the truth behind one of America's most enduring mysteries. (Getty Images)

"If the public has any new, credible information regarding the disappearance of Jimmy Hoffa, the FBI will investigate," the FBI said.

Hoffa vanished on this day in 1975 as he was on his way to what he thought was a meeting to help his bid to regain the Teamsters union presidency. He was last seen in the parking lot of the Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, restaurant, the Machus Red Fox, at about 2:30 p.m. getting into a car that whisked him away. It is believed that the Detroit Mafia kidnapped and killed him to stop his efforts to take back the union.

SAMMY 'THE BULL' REVEALS WHY HIS LOVE FOR JOHN GOTTI TURNED INTO PRISON HATE

The eight-part documentary series, "Riddle, The Search for James R. Hoffa," streaming on Fox Nation, focuses on a dominant theory. It says that Hoffa was picked up at the restaurant by Detroit mob capo Vito "Billy Jack" Giacalone, who, along with mobster Anthony "Tony Pal" Palazzolo, drove Hoffa to a nearby home owned by mobster Carlo Licata and murdered him. His remains were then possibly disposed of in a mob-run sanitation facility in Hamtramck.

Hoffa believes that his father was picked up at the restaurant by Giacalone, but beyond that, he will not speculate about who killed his father.

Fox Nation's "Riddle" series reported that an informant told the FBI that he was present when Hoffa was murdered and said that Giacalone killed him. Such information would have been documented in the FBI records, called 302s, but so far the information has not been made public.

Detroit journalist and mob historian Scott Burnstein, who runs the website "Gangster Report," has confirmed that the 302 exists and reported that "confidential informants" told the FBI "that 'Tony Pal" was the 'doer" in the Hoffa homicide conspiracy, and that Giacalone "headed the Hoffa hit team and was present at the time Palazzolo kidnapped and clipped Hoffa."

COVERT DNA SAMPLE FROM COLORADO MAN'S TRASH REVIVES 44-YEAR-OLD TEXAS MURDER CASE: REPORT

Hoffa said that he has been aware of the information that Giacalone murdered his father but cannot confirm that. He does say that his dad was lured to the meeting by Giacalone and his brother Anthony "Tony Jack" Giacalone, who was considered the Detroit mob's street boss. Both men have since died.

In a letter to FBI Director Kash Patel obtained by Fox News, Hoffa wrote last month, "It is important to us and the country that the truth about my father's disappearance (be) told and those involved in his disappearance, even if they are deceased, be exposed."

Through the years there have been a variety of claims about Hoffa's fate.

Fox Nation's series investigated the claims of Frank Sheeran, "The Irishman," which proved to be unfounded. It's also been said that Hoffa's remains were buried in a mob-owned garbage dump in the New Jersey Meadowlands, but the FBI dug at the site in 2022 and came up empty. Stories have circulated that he was cremated or entombed in the downtown Detroit Renaissance Center office building complex.

Independent investigator Roscoe Clark told Fox News that he is certain that Hoffa is buried in an undisclosed location in Michigan, and that it would take less than five minutes.

"Forensics will help solve the Jimmy Hoffa cold case," Clark said. "A team of experts is ready to move forward because of a lack of action by law enforcement. A location has been identified within three feet," and he said the necessary locating equipment is ready to be deployed.

The FBI said it has "received countless tips and information from the public, which have been a tremendous help to the FBI. We are grateful to the public, and most importantly, for the Hoffa's family assistance and support over the years."

UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH STUDENTS SAY SUDIKSHA KONANKI'S 'CRAZY' DISAPPEARANCE COULD 'HAPPEN TO ANYBODY'

Observers note that the legacy of Jimmy Hoffa is not what happened to him, but what he accomplished. His hard-fought victories at the bargaining table and on the picket lines enabled generations to enjoy the American Dream, with healthcare and benefits, good pay and retirement. Millions of sons and daughters and their families still benefit from the feisty labor leader's achievements. In some ways, that is how Jimmy Hoffa is still with us, even as he is still deeply missed and mourned by his family.

James Hoffa, his sister Barbara, their adult children and grandchildren somberly mark this day with each passing year.

Every July 30 "is a hard day," said James Hoffa. "We always spend time with it. It is special time, a time to remember. The good thing is, that I had a great father and he did a great job in raising our family. He was a great man and we miss him."

The in-depth series "Riddle, The Search for James R. Hoffa," is streaming on Fox Nation.

Eric Shawn, a New York-based anchor and senior correspondent for FOX News Channel (FNC), joined the network when it launched in 1996. He is currently the co-anchor of FOX News Live. Shawn is also the host of Riddle: The Search for James R. Hoffa on FOX Nation, FNC's on-demand subscription-based streaming service, which is based upon his extensive reporting into the appearance of notorious Teamsters boss Jimmy Hoffa.

articles.title: WNBA admits controversial betting video featuring Angel Reese, Paige Bueckers 'missed the mark'
articles.excerpt: A Seattle Storm co-owner was suspended after allegedly cursing at teenage fans who supported Sophie Cunningham's stance on women's sports. Former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines discusses the incident, emph...
articles.body_text:
A Seattle Storm co-owner was suspended after allegedly cursing at teenage fans who supported Sophie Cunningham's stance on women's sports. Former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines discusses the incident, emphasizing the importance of fair and safe opportunities for biological girls in sports. The Seattle Storm later apologized, stating their commitment to an inclusive environment.

The WNBA doesn't appear to be taking what could be a direct violation of its own anti-gambling policy very seriously whatsoever.

Ahead of Wednesday night's matchup between the Dallas Wings and Atlanta Dream, the WNBA's official X account shared a video showing Dallas' Paige Bueckers and Atlanta's Angel Reese – two of the league's most well-known players – making a $400 wager on the game. The WNBA was quick to delete the post, but not before many were able to share and also capture recordings of the video.

A WNBA spokesperson released a statement on Thursday claiming that the quickly deleted video was "intended to be lighthearted," but that it "simply missed the mark."

Paige Bueckers #5 of the Dallas Wings and Angel Reese #5 of the Chicago Sky react during the 2025 AT&T WNBA All-Star practice sessions at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on July 18, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images)

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"While the social media post was intended to be lighthearted, WNBA players are well aware of the league's policies prohibiting betting on WNBA games and receive training every year reinforcing those policies," the statement read.

"We recognized that the post missed the mark, removed it shortly after it was published, and addressed the matter internally. We will also use this as an opportunity to reemphasize with the players involved that conversations about wagering on WNBA games, even when intended as a joke, can have negative consequences."

It is unclear whether the statement's note that the matter was handled "internally" is in reference to the league having conversations with Reese and Bueckers about the clip or the individual who originally shared the video across the league's official social media. OutKick contacted the league for further clarification but did not immediately hear back.

Paige Bueckers #5 of the Dallas Wings plays defense on Angel Reese #5 of the Atlanta Dream on May 22, 2026 at Gateway Center Arena at College Park in Atlanta, Georgia. (Joe Boatman/NBAE via Getty Images)

When reached for comment about the video and any potential in-house investigations regarding the video, a Dream spokesperson told OutKick that the team has "no additional information to share other than what the league released." The Wings were not reached for comment.

Following Atlanta's 82-81 win on Wednesday, a laughing Reese joked that she would be requesting Bueckers' Apple Pay to receive her winnings from the wager.

Betting of any kind is strictly prohibited under the WNBA's new collective bargaining agreement, with Section 5 of Article 14 in the agreement dedicated to gambling regulations.

"Any player found by the Commissioner after a hearing to have been guilty of wagering (directly or indirectly), or of offering or attempting to wager, money or anything of value on the outcome, score, or any other aspect of any WNBA Competition shall, in the sole discretion of the Commissioner, be subject to a fine, suspension, and/or dismissal and disqualification from any further association with the WNBA," subsection c in the agreement reads.

While the WNBA described the wager between Bueckers and Reese as being "lighthearted," it was still a bet made between two players, caught on video, and shared across social media. One would think that WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert has the evidence to potentially impose punishments.

Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese of the USA during the Women's World Cup 2026 Qualifying Tournament Content Day on March 10, 2026, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. (Alexa Alejandro/FIBA via Getty Images)

Other professional sports leagues have strict anti-gambling policies in place that carry severe punishments.

NFL players are prohibited from placing any wagers on NFL games. An NFL player wagering on an NFL game that does not involve his team carries an indefinite suspension of 1-year minimum, while wagering on your own team results in an indefinite two-year suspension.

In the MLB, if a player is found to be betting on games not involving their own team, the player is handed a one-year suspension. If found to be betting on games involving their own team, a lifetime ban is enforced under Major League Rule 21.

OutKick's Alejandro Avila contributed to this report.

articles.title: F1 boss invokes George Lucas while talking about how the series can appeal to new fans
articles.excerpt: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert continues to face intense scrutiny for her leadership missteps, especially surrounding Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark. But despite mounting criticism, some in ...
articles.body_text:
WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert continues to face intense scrutiny for her leadership missteps, especially surrounding Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark. But despite mounting criticism, some in the media are rushing to shield her.

I'm a massive fan of George Lucas as a person. I grew up with the Star Wars prequels, and I like that, despite being a gazillionaire, he's still rocking the same flannels he always has.

The legendary filmmaker — fresh off a great cameo in the movie "Minions and Monsters" — is a big racing fan, and is often seen at Formula 1 races.

He also binned a Scion during the old Toyota Pro/Celebrity Race at Long Beach in one of my favorite videos ever.

George Lucas visited the Ferrari garage at this past weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix. (Photo by Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto)

So he knows racing — hell, he invented podracing — but F1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali revealed a wild bit of advice he got from the man who somehow invented both Darth Vader and Jar-Jar Binks: no one is interested in how F1 cars are driven.

I don't think that's true, but let's hear him out.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The series has faced a lot of flak for its current cars that rely more heavily on battery power and have effectively changed how drivers have to drive. Certain iconic corners are no longer taken flat out, and the need to recharge batteries has led to people calling the racing artificial.

It has also led to claims that F1 should offer more info about the batteries and their state of charge for fans to follow along.

F1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali addressed what he — and George Lucas — believe fans are looking for when it comes to the sport. (Photo by Marcel van Dorst/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"I think that the truth is exactly the other way around, because no one is interested in how you drive your car," Domenicali said, per Motorsport. "The people are interested in whether you are overtaking or not. That's the vast majority of people."

He noted that while some people are interested in this sort of thing, casual fans aren't.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Then he delivered one of the greatest name drops I've ever read.

"I had an interesting discussion with George Lucas in Hungary, and he was giving me an incredible view on how the new fans are watching F1," Domenicali said. "And I think that he gave us an incredible clearance to see how we can really simplify things because the new fans are not understanding the truth, what is behind the scenes."

I think new fans appreciate the sport more once they get a firmer grasp on the behind-the-scenes stuff, but it's interesting Lucas made this point because it sounds to me like he's saying what's most important is providing an entertaining product.

He knows quite a bit about that. Hell, he just opened a massive museum devoted to the medium of storytelling.

George Lucas has a long history with F1, including the 2005 Monaco Grand Prix in which Red Bull ran a livery promoting "Star Wars: Episode III: Revenge of the Sith." (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

And, if you think about it, every race is one big story, and it makes sense that F1 would want that at the forefront for newer fans.

But, if you're already in the door, there's always room to nerd out on the strategies and tech and science behind the sport, just like if you're a fan of a movie, you can geek out on the plot devices and the structure and even what pen or script software the person who wrote it used.

It's an interesting thing to think about... and even more fun because it seems to have sprung from the flannel-shirted mind of one George Lucas.

Rescuers in New Jersey are still searching for ...
articles.body_text:
Rescuers in New Jersey search for a 10-year-old girl in the Passaic River. The body of the girl's 10-year-old brother was already found. (Credit: WNYW)

Rescuers in New Jersey are still searching for a 10-year-old girl after finding her 10-year-old brother's body in the Passaic River late Wednesday night, Passaic Mayor Hector Lora told reporters.

'Right now, all of our efforts are in trying to recover the body but hoping that perhaps, maybe hope against all things, that we could find the little girl still alive," Lora told FOX 5 New York in an interview.

Lora hoped aloud that the little girl was still alive, hypothesizing that her now deceased brother helped push her to safety.

‘HERO' MOM DIES AFTER USING LAST STRENGTH TO SAVE 4-YEAR-OLD SON FROM FLORIDA RIVER

Passaic Police and other assisting towns work the scene where a 10-year-old boy was found dead, and an ongoing operation is underway to find a 10-year-old girl after both children were in the Passaic River in the vicinity of Veterans Ct near a park in Passaic, New Jersey, on Wednesday, July 29, 2026.  (Kyle Mazza/Sipa USA)

"The 10-year-old boy, as he was going down, maybe an angel, maybe God used him to push his little sister, and now she made her way out so she's home. But the mother has lost her little boy," Lora said.

Lora also told reporters that calls for help came in around 6:20 p.m. local time Wednesday after bystanders saw three children in the water, according to FOX 5.

A good Samaritan unsuccessfully tried to help the children out of the water, the outlet reported.

Passaic Police and other assisting towns work the scene inside the Passaic River where a 10-year-old boy was found dead and an ongoing operation is underway to recover a 10-year-old girl after both children were in the Passaic River in the vicinity of Veterans Ct near a park in Passaic, New Jersey,  (Kyle Mazza/Sipa USA)

PARK VISITORS FACE FLOOD DANGER OUT WEST WHILE SEVERE STORMS RIP THROUGH NY, NJ

Search and rescue operations were ongoing into Thursday morning. The efforts were hampered in part by high water levels due to recent storms.

The search and rescue operations included members of the the Passaic Police Department, the Passaic County Sheriff's Office and the New Jersey State Police.

Passaic Police and other assisting towns work the scene inside the Passaic River after two children were swept into the Passaic River in the vicinity of Veterans Ct near a park in Passaic, New Jersey, on Thursday, July 30, 2026. A (Kyle Mazza/Sipa USA)

Fox News Digital contacted the Passaic Police Department, the Passaic County Sheriff's Office and the New Jersey State Police for further information.

articles.title: Bodycam shows Los Angeles County deputy stabbed seconds after arriving at knife attack

Deputies responded to reports of a man armed with multiple knives when the suspect suddenly charged an arriving deputy. (Credit: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

Newly released body camera an...
articles.body_text:
Deputies responded to reports of a man armed with multiple knives when the suspect suddenly charged an arriving deputy. (Credit: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

Newly released body camera and surveillance footage shows a Los Angeles County sheriff's deputy being stabbed within seconds of arriving at a call about an armed man before deputies opened fire, fatally shooting the suspect.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department on Tuesday released body camera and surveillance video from the June 20 incident in a Lancaster parking lot that left a deputy wounded and 23-year-old Robert Castro shot. Castro died after the shooting.

The incident began with a 911 caller reporting a man wielding multiple knives in public.

WISCONSIN PROTESTER BRANDS MADISON AS 'CORRUPT CITY' DURING ANTI-POLICE TIRADE FOLLOWING DEADLY SHOOTING

"Hey, I just want to make a report of a guy with some knives ... swinging them in public," the caller told a dispatcher.

Body camera footage released by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department shows 23-year-old Robert Castro moments before authorities say he stabbed a sheriff's deputy during a June 20 encounter in Lancaster, California. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

The caller said Castro appeared to be "fighting with someone" while carrying a large knife and expressed concern after seeing him look toward a woman walking to a nearby bus stop.

Surveillance video shows deputies arriving with emergency lights activated as Castro walked across the parking lot while still armed.

VIDEO SHOWS UNDERCOVER COPS SHOOTING MAN THREATENING SHOPPERS WITH FAKE GUN IN ‘JUSTIFIED’ DEFENSE: OFFICIALS

According to the sheriff's department, Castro suddenly changed direction before the first deputy's patrol vehicle had come to a stop, rushed toward the deputy, pulled a knife and stabbed him.

A still image from deputy body camera footage released by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department shows Robert Castro approaching an arriving deputy while holding what investigators say was one of three knives recovered at the scene. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The wounded deputy then drew his service weapon and opened fire.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

The deputy activated his body camera after firing his weapon, but the camera's pre-event recording feature captured the 60 seconds leading up to the stabbing without audio.

EIGHT NYPD OFFICERS INJURED IN MASSIVE EXPLOSION WHILE RESPONDING TO KNIFE-WIELDING MAN IN QUEENS HOME

A second deputy's body camera captured him arriving as the first deputy fired his weapon.

Surveillance video released by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department shows deputies arriving at the scene before investigators say Robert Castro suddenly charged toward an arriving deputy and stabbed him. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

The video shows Castro on the ground as the deputy checked on his wounded colleague. When Castro moved one of his hands, the deputy repeatedly yelled, "Stop reaching," before opening fire again.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department released images of two knives recovered after authorities say 23-year-old Robert Castro stabbed a sheriff's deputy during a June 20 confrontation in Lancaster, California. (Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department)

Deputies rendered medical aid to Castro until Los Angeles County Fire Department personnel arrived. Castro was transported to a hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

Authorities said Castro was armed with three knives, including the one investigators say he used to stab the deputy.

The wounded deputy was hospitalized for treatment. No other deputies or civilians were injured.

The California Department of Justice is investigating the shooting, as required under state law for officer-involved fatalities.

The sheriff's department said it released the video before the investigation was complete "in the interest of transparency with the community we serve."

Greg Wehner is a reporter for Fox News Digital covering U.S. news and crime, with a focus on breaking developments, law enforcement, public safety and major stories shaping communities across the country.

articles.title: Older adults taking 5 or more prescription drugs face higher risk of death, study finds
articles.excerpt: Older adults who walked at a significantly faster speed than their peers were about half as likely to develop cognitive impairment, according to Dr. Joe Verghese, MD, neurologist at Stony Brook Medici...
articles.body_text:
Older adults who walked at a significantly faster speed than their peers were about half as likely to develop cognitive impairment, according to Dr. Joe Verghese, MD, neurologist at Stony Brook Medicine.

Older adults who take five or more prescription medications face a significantly higher risk of death compared to those taking fewer drugs, according to a study published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society.

The research highlights the growing concern over polypharmacy, the medical term for taking five or more daily prescriptions, and its long-term effects on aging populations.

Led by Dr. Alexander Chaitoff of the University of Michigan School of Medicine, researchers analyzed national survey data collected from 7,828 adults aged 65 and older between 1999 and 2016.

LONGER LIVES, WORSE HEALTH? SCIENTISTS UNCOVER TROUBLING TREND ACROSS GENERATIONS

Trained staff directly inspected participants' pill bottles to verify medication use over the previous 30 days, then followed them for an average of 8.5 years, according to a press release.

More than half of participants (54.3%) fell into at least one high-risk medication category. The largest group consisted of older adults taking five or more prescription drugs (polypharmacy).

Over 40% of older adults studied were taking five or more prescription medications, a situation known as polypharmacy. (iStock)

Another group, 37.6% of those studied, used medications deemed risky for older individuals, such as drugs that can increase the risk of confusion or falls, the study revealed.

DOCTORS REVEAL HIDDEN DANGER FOR SOME OZEMPIC, WEGOVY USERS WITH BRAIN DISORDERS

Additionally, 11.4% took combinations of medications that are known to cause major drug-to-drug interactions.

After accounting for overall health and underlying conditions, taking five or more prescriptions was associated with a 38% increase in overall mortality risk. Each additional prescription medication added to a patient’s routine was linked to a 7% increase in death risk.

Taking multiple medications has been shown to increase the likelihood of side effects, adverse drug reactions and accidental overdose, particularly as the liver and kidneys age and process drugs less efficiently, according to medical experts at Cleveland Clinic.

Researchers emphasized that these findings can help doctors identify patients who would benefit from safely stopping or reducing unnecessary medications. (iStock)

The total number of medications participants took was the strongest independent predictor of mortality, even after accounting for drug-to-drug interactions and potentially inappropriate prescriptions.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

These findings could help doctors determine which patients are the best candidates for "deprescribing," or carefully reducing or stopping unnecessary medications, the researchers stated.

The authors noted several limitations, including that the study focused strictly on community-dwelling older adults, excluding those living in nursing homes or assisted care facilities.

Because the study relied on a single 30-day snapshot of medication use, it shows an association rather than direct proof that the prescriptions caused the higher death risk. (iStock)

Additionally, medication use was documented during a single 30-day snapshot at the start of the study, meaning researchers could not track subsequent changes in prescriptions or evolving health conditions over time.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Experts emphasized that observational studies show association rather than direct causation. Older adults taking higher numbers of prescriptions often suffer from multiple severe or complex health conditions, which independently carry a higher mortality risk.

Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

articles.title: Savannah Bananas stars trade baseball dreams for kids' smiles: 'Exactly where God put me'
articles.excerpt:
Members of the Savannah Bananas didn't have this type of fame on their bingo card, but they have no complaints after surprising children at a hospital.

Reese Alexiades and DR Meadows had baseball dre...
articles.body_text:
Members of the Savannah Bananas didn't have this type of fame on their bingo card, but they have no complaints after surprising children at a hospital.

Reese Alexiades and DR Meadows had baseball dreams just like the rest of us – getting to the major leagues. But their journeys took them on a route unimaginable even less than five years ago.

Alexiades played college ball at Pepperdine University, while Meadows played for Division II school Columbus State. Neither played minor league ball, but they now play in front of one of the largest baseball crowds ever.

Alexiades and Meadows hit the big time in another way, becoming stars for the Savannah Bananas. Meadows is the organization's all-time leader in "trick plays," while Alexiades plays with a cape on.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Savannah Bananas Reese Alexiades and DR Meadows meet with children at a children's hospital with Dairy Queen. (Dairy Queen)

Despite selling out MLB ballparks and even playing in front of six-figure crowds at football stadiums, baseball purists will never get on board – unless, Alexiades says, "if they came to a game and caught an out." (If a fan catches a ball on the fly, the batter is out.)

But what fans do not understand the most, Meadows says, is that, contrary to popular belief, their games are not "scripted" like, say, the Harlem Globetrotters.

"There's a huge difference. In our league, all our teams are out to win. We're very competitive... Just this past weekend, we lost two out of three in Chicago against the Firefighters, and our guys were not happy," Meadows told Fox News Digital in a recent interview. "At the end of the day, we're there for a bigger picture: to put on a show for the fans, break down the wall for the kids there and put smiles on faces. That's what makes Banana Ball beautiful. Even though we get to have fun competing, winning and losing, we still get to make somebody's day."

No one Meadows and Alexiades' age grew up wanting to be Bananas – but that may have changed by now.

"One of the big reasons why I fell in love with baseball is looking up to other players. Now kids can look up to us, and what we're all about is bringing fun to the game of baseball. Kids being able to see us and see how much fun we have, that's what it's all about. We try to be the best role models we can be for kids because the kids are what it's all about," Alexiades said.

Meadows added, "You see kids at the Little League World Series listing their favorite players, and some are Bananas players. To know we have that kind of platform — and like Reese was saying, it all comes from having fun, playing the game and having fun. Youth sports these days should be less pressure and a lot more fun. I think it's cool that kids are getting to see how much fun we have and get to take that to their own game."

The Savannah Bananas' mascot Split dances atop the first-base dugout. (Ben McCanna/Portland Press Herald via Getty Images)

FORMER SAVANNAH BANANAS PLAYER NAMED MLB ALL-STAR, HOURS AFTER HITTING FOR CYCLE AS A ROOKIE

Alexiades and Meadows recently visited a children's hospital in Tennessee to give them some Dairy Queen, and on Thursday, for every Blizzard bought at select locations, at least $1 will be donated to Children’s Miracle Network to help support local children’s hospitals.

"That's the beauty of our platform and this partnership: We can really make an impact, and so can other people," Alexiades said.

"Getting to see those kids, put a smile on their faces, bring them Blizzard Treats and enjoy those with them was super cool. The amount of joy DQ brings and the Bananas bring – it all made sense," added Meadows.

So, while it may not be the big time they originally envisioned, it's the 2026 version of the big time, which is just fine with the baseball player in a cape – literally and figuratively.

Members of the Savannah Bananas attend a children's hospital with Dairy Queen. (Dairy Queen)

"The whole goal is to be able to play the game we love for as long as we can. A lot of us, me included, and people in this organization have been told no at some point in their careers. The Bananas have given me a chance to keep going, keep playing and realize that it's for a bigger purpose now," Alexiades said.

"I get to go and probably have more fun than I would have ever had if I played in the major leagues. So I'm having the time of my life, and this is exactly where God put me."

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X, and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

articles.title: White House blasts Spanish government as thousands of migrants surge from Morocco, emergency request denied
articles.excerpt:
Thousands of migrants from Morocco pored over the country's border with Spain and into Spain's African enclave of Ceuta July 30, 2026. (Reuters)

The White House bashed Spain's left-wing government af...
articles.body_text:
Thousands of migrants from Morocco pored over the country's border with Spain and into Spain's African enclave of Ceuta July 30, 2026. (Reuters)

The White House bashed Spain's left-wing government after the border between Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta and Morocco collapsed Thursday.

"President Trump has long warned Europe what would happen if they continue to implement far-left, globalist policies, including enabling mass migration," White House principal deputy press secretary Anna Kelly told Fox News in a statement.

"Spain and other countries who have adopted this destructive philosophy should immediately reverse course or risk their own demise."

TRUMP CRITICIZES SPAIN AMID IRAN, NATO RIFT AS PM SANCHEZ FACES QUESTIONS OVER POLITICAL MOTIVES

Ceuta's president formally requested a national emergency declaration Thursday after more than 2,000 migrants crossed the border from Morocco in the past 10 days. Videos showed chaotic scenes of migrants pouring into the Spanish territory.

Video shows hordes of apparently military-aged men smiling and posing for cameras, some carrying swimming flippers, and sprinting through the streets as authorities struggle to corral the unruly masses.

Migrants run and cheer as they cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco after swimming over from the Moroccan side and overwhelming police at the city's breakwater, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, in Ceuta, Spain, July 30, 2026. (Faro TV via Reuters)

Other footage shows crowds of migrants emerging from the sea, climbing up onto Ceuta's rocky shores and working their way around border fences.

Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas formally requested that Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declare a national emergency to help respond to the border crisis, Spanish media outlets reported. Madrid, however, denied the request.

DEM REP SETH MOULTON SAYS PARTY HAS NO IMMIGRATION PLAN, IS ONLY ‘OPPOSITION TO TRUMP’

"The declaration of a national emergency is part of the state civil protection regulations, which do not consider migratory flows as a risk to the National Civil Protection System, nor do they establish special plans, basic guidelines, or specific civil protection instruments for their management. Therefore, it is not possible to activate this mechanism, as requested by the president of the Government of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas," Spain's Ministry of the Interior said in a statement, according to Spanish outlet El País.

Ceuta’s government, in its request for a national emergency declaration, noted that immigration from Morocco is always a problem for the Spanish enclave but claimed the last 10 days represented a peak "of particular intensity." That peak has seen more than 2,000 migrants cross the border in the past 10 days, Ceuta officials said, according to El País.

Spanish and Moroccan maritime patrols, supported by Spain's Maritime Rescue service, conduct rescue operations off the southern coast of Ceuta after a sharp increase in migrant arrivals to the Spanish enclave in North Africa. (Antonio Sempere/JNA Press/Sipa USA)

"The Government of Spain is fully committed to providing an immediate response to the situation in Ceuta. We are mobilizing all necessary resources, working with Moroccan and international authorities, and preparing the necessary measures to restore normalcy as soon as possible," Sánchez wrote in a Thursday post on X.

BIDEN ADMINISTRATION FORCED A FALSE CHOICE ON AMERICANS ABOUT IMMIGRATION

Sánchez has faced considerable backlash from his country's conservatives for his policies on immigration, with many arguing that Spain's policy of guaranteeing social services to minors who illegally enter the country incentivizes mass migration.

Migrants cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco by attempting to swim, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, near the border with Ceuta, in Fnideq, Morocco, July 30, 2026, in a still image obtained by Reuters (Reuters)

"When they cross the border as minors, you cannot send them back to Morocco," Javier Negre, a conservative Spanish journalist and owner of La Derecha Diario and UHN Plus, told Fox News Digital.

"The Spanish state has to take care of them and pay money to NGOs to care for these minors until they turn 18," Negre continued.

"It’s proof that Europe and Spain are on the verge of becoming a failed continent because of the future policies and promotion of this illegal invasion under Pedro Sánchez."

Sánchez, for his part, has claimed that accepting migrants is necessary to keep Spain's economy alive, arguing the country's low birth rates necessitate accepting immigrants.

Spain's Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, delivers a statement at the Moncloa Palace in Madrid, Spain. (AP Photo/Andrea Comas)

"The West needs people. Currently, few of its countries have a rising population growth rate," Sánchez wrote in a February op-ed in The New York Times.

"Unless they embrace migration, they will experience a sharp demographic decline that will prevent them from keeping their economies and public services afloat. Their gross domestic product will stagnate. Their public healthcare and pension systems will suffer.

"Neither AI nor robots will be able to prevent this outcome. ... The only option to avoid decline is to integrate migrants in the most orderly and effective way possible."

Fox News Digital contacted the offices of Sánchez and Vivas for further comment.

Fox News' Patrick Ward contributed to this report.

articles.title: Ex-White House counsel says Epstein accuser’s testimony ‘lacked inherent credibility’
articles.excerpt:
Kathryn Ruemmler was blasted by family of late Virginia Giuffre after House committee transcripts were released

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A former White House counsel and for...
articles.body_text:
Kathryn Ruemmler was blasted by family of late Virginia Giuffre after House committee transcripts were released

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A former White House counsel and former general counsel of Goldman Sachs, who has faced scrutiny over her past ties to Jeffrey Epstein, told a House committee this month that some of the allegations made by one his most prominent accusers “lacked inherent credibility”, according to newly released transcripts.

Kathryn Ruemmler’s name appeared thousands of times in records related to Epstein, the disgraced financier and convicted sex offender, that were released earlier this year by the US Department of Justice under the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

The files revealed Ruemmler had accepted gifts from Epstein, who died by suicide while awaiting trial in 2019 after he was arrested by federal authorities, at times addressed him as “Uncle Jeffrey” and “sweetie” in emails, and offered him informal advice on how to respond to questions about his sex crimes.

Ruemmler’s testimony before Congress when she was asked about Virginia Giuffre, a victim of Epstein’s abuse, was swiftly criticized by Giuffre’s family. “She should be ashamed of herself,” Giuffre’s brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts, told CNN. Giuffre died by suicide in April 2025.

“Do you believe that Virginia Giuffre was a victim of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell?” the House oversight committee asked Ruemmler, who served as the White House counsel in the Obama administration, during her interview with the panel earlier this month part of its investigation into Epstein.

“I don’t know,” she responded, according to a transcript released on Wednesday.

Ruemmler went on to add: “If she says that she was, I don’t have a reason to doubt that. However, there were allegations that she made that were, I believed based on my experience as a former prosecutor and as a defense counsel, that were of such a nature that they were – they lacked inherent credibility.

“Typically, when someone says, I was sex trafficked to someone, they say who, when, where, not multiple world leaders, multiple foreign presidents,” she said.

Her remarks were condemned by Giuffre’s brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts, who said in a statement to CNN that it as “reprehensible” to “attempt to cast doubt on Virginia, whose bravery was the reason so many other survivors stepped forward, resulting in more than 50 people having to step down from their positions of power”.

They said that “the only person who lacks credibility is Kathy Ruemmler”.

Giuffre, one of Epstein’s most prominent accusers, had previously testified and alleged that Epstein and Maxwell had abused her as a teenager, and trafficked her to powerful men, including Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, who has repeatedly denied the allegations against him.

Jennifer Connelly, a spokesperson for Ruemmler, said in a statement: “As Ms Ruemmler told the committee, she had no knowledge of any ongoing criminal activity by Epstein and there is not a shred of evidence to suggest otherwise.”

“Ms Ruemmler would never turn a blind eye to any criminal activity and if she had seen or heard anything to suggest that Epstein was harming women or girls, she would have taken action to stop it,” she added.

Another representative for Ruemmler also told CNN in a statement – before Giuffre’s family members had issued their statement – that Ruemmler “was responding to a specific discussion about specific allegations” and was “expressing skepticism regarding particular claims that had not been substantiated, not every allegation Ms Giuffre ever made”.

The transcript was released about two weeks after Ruemmler appeared before the committee. She was called to testify after the Epstein files revealed dozens of emails between her and Epstein between 2014 and 2019. At one point she had been listed as a backup executor of his will, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Ruemmler told lawmakers during the interview that they had a professional relationship and that Epstein had “used” her “to legitimize his standing” and that “it was a mistake to deal with” him.

She insisted that she never saw any “evidence of ongoing criminal conduct or misconduct of any kind by Epstein during the time I dealt with him” and also told lawmakers that “many” of her emails with Epstein had been “taken out of context or do not mean what some have speculated or suggested”.

Ruemmler announced in February that she would be resigning from her role at Goldman Sachs as chief legal officer.
