articles.title: SEN DEB FISCHER: The left's war on the Senate and Supreme Court puts our republic at risk
articles.excerpt:
Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Nebr., weighs in on the Democrats’ agenda ahead of the midterm elections during an appearance on ‘Mornings with Maria.’

The Democratic Socialists of America recently rolled out a ...
articles.body_text:
Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Nebr., weighs in on the Democrats’ agenda ahead of the midterm elections during an appearance on ‘Mornings with Maria.’

The Democratic Socialists of America recently rolled out a policy platform wrapped in delusional promises — free government-run health care, the abolition of the police and prison systems, and the defunding of our military. While those proposals sound crazy enough, something far more radical is buried underneath: a call to abolish the Senate and subordinate the presidency and the Supreme Court to a new unicameral body that would choose and control the executive and judicial branches.

That proposal is not just unserious — it is a direct assault on the Constitution. The attacks on the Supreme Court's legitimacy and the calls to abolish the Senate spring from the same impulse: impatience with constitutional limits on political power. When institutions become obstacles to ideological goals, the answer should never be to tear them down.

That dangerous mindset has consequences beyond political rhetoric. Our Supreme Court justices and their families have been subject to escalating threats in recent years.

DSA CO-CHAIR EMBRACES ABOLISHING SENATE, ICE, BORDERS AS DEMOCRATIC INFIGHTING ESCALATES

During a recent Senate Appropriations Committee hearing, I heard directly from Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan. Both described a security posture that has not kept pace with the threats they now face. In fact, after the leak of the court’s decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, Justice Barrett came home from work wearing a bulletproof vest given to her by her security detail. She recounted placing the vest on a table and having to explain to her 12-year-old son what it was and why she had it.

No justice should fear for their safety because they faithfully discharge their constitutional duty. Yet instead of treating this as the urgent, nonpartisan security matter it is, we continue to hear rhetoric that attacks the very legitimacy of the court as an institution. In 2020, Sen. Chuck Schumer said Justices Brett Kavanaugh and Neil Gorsuch would "pay the price" if they acted to restrict abortion. His comments were inappropriate and dangerous. Unfortunately, this sentiment has continued to proliferate and fuel physical threats. More recently, congressional Democrats have called the Supreme Court "corrupt," "rigged" and "a disgrace."

The three branches of government conceived by the Founders have served our democracy well. Republicans and Democrats alike should reject calls to dismantle our constitutional order.

Criticism of the court's decisions is part of a healthy democracy. Justice Kagan said as much herself. But there is a clear difference between criticizing a ruling and undermining the legitimacy of the institution or inciting threats against those who serve on it.

JUSTICE NEIL GORSUCH BREAKS SILENCE ON VIOLENT THREATS AGAINST JUDICIARY, SUPREME COURT LEAKS

The same impatience animates the DSA's call to abolish the Senate. The Senate provides a necessary counterbalance to the House of Representatives. It balances power by granting each state equal representation, protecting smaller states from being steamrolled by larger ones. Because senators serve staggered six-year terms, the body is insulated from drastic swings in public opinion. That deliberate friction is what has allowed the republic to endure for generations.

The three branches of government conceived by the Founders have served our democracy well. Republicans and Democrats alike should reject calls to dismantle our constitutional order.

Now is the time to reaffirm our commitment to those institutions. Congress can ensure that Supreme Court justices have the security resources necessary to carry out their duties without fear or intimidation.

I will continue making this a priority through my role on the Appropriations Committee. But we need every American to reject the DSA’s reckless calls to dismantle the constitutional framework that has preserved our republic for 250 years.

The answer to political disagreement is not to weaken the Constitution — it is to defend it.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM SEN. DEB FISCHER

Deb Fischer, a Republican. represents Nebraska in the U.S. Senate.

articles.title: LA real estate vet comes at Mayor Bass with receipts over damning homelessness report: 'She doesn't get it'
articles.excerpt:
John Alle, a business owner and co-founder of the Santa Monica Coalition, told Fox News Digital Karen Bass "doesn't get it" as homelessness rises in Los Angeles.

LOS ANGELES, CA – As new data show ho...
articles.body_text:
John Alle, a business owner and co-founder of the Santa Monica Coalition, told Fox News Digital Karen Bass "doesn't get it" as homelessness rises in Los Angeles.

LOS ANGELES, CA – As new data show homelessness rising in Los Angeles, local activist John Alle said Mayor Karen Bass has neglected her responsibility to address the issue and witness firsthand the crime, drug use and deteriorating conditions in some of the city's hardest-hit neighborhoods.

The Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority released its 2026 annual homeless count Friday, finding overall homelessness increased 3.4% in LA and 1.2% across the Los Angeles Continuum of Care following two consecutive years of declines, though LAHSA said "neither change is considered statistically significant."

The count estimated 45,194 people were experiencing homelessness in LA and 73,040 across the Continuum of Care, which excludes Long Beach, Pasadena and Glendale.

"She doesn't get it. She doesn't see it," John Alle, a Santa Monica business owner and co-founder of the Santa Monica Coalition who owns properties across Los Angeles, told Fox News Digital in an interview last month.

KAREN BASS GRILLED OVER BROKEN HOMELESSNESS PROMISE, BLAMES BUREAUCRACY FOR SLOWED PROGRESS

John Alle, a Santa Monica business owner and co-founder of the Santa Monica Coalition, blasted Mayor Karen Bass' response to homelessness as new data show the crisis is worsening in Los Angeles. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images ; Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"We've invited her numerous times to ride along with us through Alvarado, Third Street, Park View, MacArthur Park and Westlake. Come drive with us. Have a police officer follow behind for security. And she refused."

The report also found street homelessness rose 7.9% in Los Angeles and 3.3% countywide, with an estimated 29,115 people living on the streets in the city. LAHSA said funding cuts affecting Time-Limited Subsidies and other economic factors reduced the number of people permanently housed by about 5,100 from the "record high of 28,625 people housed permanently in 2024."

In a press release Thursday responding to the data, Bass argued funding cuts "at the federal and state levels" contributed to the rise, adding the Trump administration had "driven up the cost of gas, groceries, and rent — pushing more families to the edge — and slashed critical safety net funding."

"For two years straight, we drove down homelessness by historic margins — but as expected, last year our efforts ultimately couldn’t keep up with policies and funding cuts at the federal and state levels that pushed more people onto the streets," she said.

Bass also admitted in a May interview with CNN's Elex Michaelson that she did not fulfill her promise to end street homelessness in the city by 2026 because she "didn't anticipate some of the bureaucratic barriers" her administration would face.

Alle said crime has "gotten so bad" in neighborhoods including Little Bangladesh, which Bass has previously described as one of "LA's most vibrant communities."

"In Little Bangladesh, the crime is so bad that we're finding people on the streets unconscious," he said. "We're having handymen pick up needles and dispose of them."

SPENCER PRATT SAYS HIS POLICY WILL FORCE HOMELESS OUT OF LA AND INTO CITIES LIKE SEATTLE

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass prepares to leave the scene where city workers clear a large homeless encampment behind a public storage facility along the San Diego (405) Freeway at the end of Oxnard Street in Van Nuys on July 31, 2025 (Genaro Molina/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

Pointing to his tenants' experiences, Alle said he sees the impact of the crisis every day on the "mom-and-pop" renters who live in his apartment buildings and pay thousands of dollars a month, saying "it doesn't sit well with me."

"From people overdosing outside the gated apartment buildings I own, to people attacking each other, murders, and calling 911 only to be put on hold for sometimes an hour, and then being told, 'Well, you're lucky. Sometimes it's two hours,'" he said.

Alle accused Bass of ignoring neighborhood conditions despite living nearby at Getty House, the mayor's official residence in Windsor Square.

"The streetlights are out," he said. "The rubbish isn't collected. The streets are dirty. It's one thing to complain about copper wire theft, but we're just talking about normal streetlights and replacing the bulbs."

But it's not just residents who are affected, according to Alle, who said small businesses are being forced to close early to avoid crime and making it harder to stay in the city.

"When I see them having to leave work at four o'clock, I see them having to close their businesses at four o'clock during the winter and at dusk during the summer," he said. "That's not good. I want them to succeed. If they don't succeed, they can't afford to stay in LA I feel for them, and their problems are my problems."

HOUSING FIRST IS A DISASTER. I SAW SACRAMENTO'S HOMELESS CHAOS FIRSTHAND

A homeless encampment near Venice Beach in Los Angeles. Residents have called for stronger oversight of nearby supportive housing programs and improved public safety. (Jill Connelly/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Multiple studies have found that a large portion of homeless individuals in Los Angeles County aren't originally from there and Alle has been vocal about how his coalition partnered with an artificial intelligence company to create an AI-powered hotline that has helped more than 40 homeless people return to their home states over the past year.

"They've called us from shelters," he said. "They've called us from parks. The people calling aren't entrenched with the drugs or the gangs. They came here for noble reasons."

Additionally, Alle said his coalition collaborates with local law enforcement, paying for bus, plane or train tickets to help homeless people voluntarily return home, where they can reunite with family or enter treatment programs.

"We're not gonna put them behind the slammer," he said.

Alle said the most "heartbreaking" part is watching families embrace loved ones returning home, with many looking "completely different" after recovery.

"It's a long road ahead, but they're trying because they've seen hell in LA," he said.

While acknowledging the program won't end all homelessness, Alle said helping even a small number of people rebuild their lives is a victory.

"One person saved is great. Fifteen percent, and the 40 people we've saved, is tremendous," he said.

Bass will face off against progressive city councilwoman Nithya Raman, who has her own ties to the homeless crisis as chair of the Los Angeles City Council's Housing and Homelessness Committee, in her bid to win another term as mayor in November.

Kiera McDonald is a Production Assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Washington mother pulls children from school after Pride lesson shown in music class without notice
articles.excerpt: Rod Theis, an Oregon social worker, was fired after displaying children's books like "He Is He" and "She Is She," which affirm biological gender. He lost his First Amendment case against the school di...
articles.body_text:
Rod Theis, an Oregon social worker, was fired after displaying children's books like "He Is He" and "She Is She," which affirm biological gender. He lost his First Amendment case against the school district, with Judge John Owens ruling that schools can dictate content during work hours. The case highlights a double standard, as other teachers displayed LGBTQ+ messaging without issue.

A Washington mother says she is withdrawing her children from an elementary school after learning a Pride-themed lesson had been presented during music class without advance notice to parents or an opportunity to opt out, raising questions about district policies governing classroom instruction.

"I assumed I had probably missed an email asking for consent, but there was nothing," Maria Varchetto said in communications with school administrators, which she shared with Fox News Digital on Monday. "No advanced notice, no opportunity to review the lesson, no information letting parents know this topic would be discussed. No option to request that our kids be allowed to opt out and participate in an alternative activity. There was nothing."

Varchetto alleged the lesson was presented to elementary school students, including her daughter, on June 15 at Martha Lake Elementary School in the Edmonds School District as part of a music class and that parents were not informed beforehand.

TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS WOKE SCHOOLS ACCUSED OF HIDING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

A school classroom filled with desks. (Jeffrey Basinger/Newsday RM via Getty Images)

Varchetto said that a video entitled, "Why is Pride in June," from the YouTube account, "Queer Kid Stuff," which, according to the account, "imagines a kinder and more equal future through highly-accessible education and entertainment for kids ages 3+," was shown to her fourth-grade daughter.

The YouTube channel describes itself as an "LGBTQ+ educational webseries for children ages 3+ hosted by a tie-wearing queer lady, Lindsay, and her non-binary best-stuffed friend, Teddy. Gender Studies 101 meets Mr. Rodgers’ Neighborhood!"

Varchetto said the incident prompted her to remove her children from the school.

VIRGINIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER ALLEGED POLICY OF KEEPING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS HIDDEN FROM PARENTS

A high-angle view of a female teacher engaging with multiracial high school students during a lesson in a classroom. (iStock)

"We are 100% removing our kids from this school as I have no trust in the leadership," Varchetto said.

Other materials Varchetto said were included were a list of videos from musicians in the LGBTQ+ community such as Freddie Mercury of Queen, Lil Nas X, and Billy Porter dancing in a ballgown on Sesame Street.

Varchetto told school officials that her daughter recalled hearing during the lesson that students could identify as gay, lesbian, transgender, asexual, nonbinary or Two-Spirit.

She said an administrator told her she had not been aware those topics were part of the classroom discussion, leaving Varchetto wondering whether the lesson included more than the materials she had been shown.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS

Rearview of a large group of students raising their arms to answer the question in a class at elementary school. (Sky Nesher/Getty Images)

"No handouts were sent home (which is typical for music class)," Varchetto told Fox News Digital in a statement.

Varchetto said she asked the school for a copy of the lesson materials but was told they could only be reviewed in person rather than sent electronically. She also said parents were not notified beforehand that the lesson would be taught, were not given an opportunity to opt their children out, and received no advance communication about its content.

She said that cultural lessons were taught every month for the theme of that month, but that Pride month was left off of the list of lessons.

"I feel mad they did this, mad they hid it," Varchetto said. "I feel insulted, offended, angry, and sad that my kids are now being taken out of a lifestyle they've grown to love, away from the friendships they've built, all because this one teacher didn't care to ask permission and a principal lied and hid it."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for Edmonds School District said, "The lesson was not part of a districtwide Pride curriculum. It was a music lesson developed by the school’s music teacher that highlighted the contributions of influential musicians, including some who identify as LGBTQ+."

The interior of a school classroom with wooden desks, student backpacks hanging on chairs, blackboard and whiteboard at front, windows letting in bright natural sunlight, education and learning concept. (Getty Images)

The spokesperson continued, "The purpose of the lesson was to teach music and music history through the lives and contributions of notable artists. Discussions about an artist’s background or identity were included as relevant biographical context, similar to how students may learn about other aspects of historical figures’ lives that helped shape their experiences and contributions."

The spokesperson added, "We expect instructional materials to be age-appropriate and aligned with district expectations and state standards. As with any concern raised about classroom instruction, we will work with the school administrator to determine whether they met those expectations."

Rachel del Guidice is a culture reporter for Fox News covering the intersection of politics, faith, family, and American culture.

articles.title: It was ‘most likely’ a Russian cruise missile that crashed in Poland, defence minister says – Europe live
articles.excerpt:
Inspector of the Polish Air Force says as part of Russia’s attack on Ukraine last night two missiles were identified as posing direct threat to Poland

Poland’s defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kam...
articles.body_text:
Inspector of the Polish Air Force says as part of Russia’s attack on Ukraine last night two missiles were identified as posing direct threat to Poland

Poland’s defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz confirms it’s “most likely” it was a Kh-101 air-launched cruise missile.

“That’s the most probable hypothesis,” he says.

He says Poland is in regular contact with Nato allies on the incident.

Maj Gen Ireneusz Nowak, the Inspector of the Polish Air Force, joins in to offer a bit more detailed briefing.

He says that Russia fired 20-22 Kh-101 missiles inside Ukraine last night as part of its strikes on the country, and two missiles were identified as posing potential threat to Poland’s territory.

An F-16 fighter jet was scrambled to follow one of the missiles and observed the moment of its crash in an uninhabited area.

Poland’s foreign minister Radosław Sikorski warned against any potential attempts to blame Ukraine for the incident, saying on X:

“Getting ahead of Putin’s disinformation, please read this: ‘Missiles (Kh-101) are exclusively used by Russia’s strategic air force.’”

Earlier, the Polish PM’s office issued a separate warning against disinformation on social media.

With Poland now confirming it was “most likely” a Russian missile, it appears to be one of the most serious airspace violations of a Nato member state since the beginning of the full-scale Russian aggression on Ukraine in 2022.

In November 2022, a Ukrainian S-300 surface-to-air missile used to intercept incoming Russian strikes accidentally strayed into Poland and killed two people.

in December 2022, an unarmed Russian Kh-55 air-launched cruise missile flew into Polish airspace, where it was only discovered a few months later.

Some 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace in September 2025.

Multiple incursions were also reported into Romania.

In May, where two people were injured after a drone crashed into an apartment block in the ​southeast Romanian ⁠town of Galati, near the Ukrainian border.

Ukraine has requested to join the Polish investigation into the missile incident, Lublin prosecutor Grzegorz Trusiewicz told a media briefing.

“This request is currently being considered, and it is possible that they will come here and work with Polish authorities to identify the object that entered Polish airspace and determine what exactly we are dealing with.”

The crash site is being “mapped” and will be examined in detail, he says.

Poland’s defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz confirms it’s “most likely” it was a Kh-101 air-launched cruise missile.

“That’s the most probable hypothesis,” he says.

He says Poland is in regular contact with Nato allies on the incident.

Maj Gen Ireneusz Nowak, the Inspector of the Polish Air Force, joins in to offer a bit more detailed briefing.

He says that Russia fired 20-22 Kh-101 missiles inside Ukraine last night as part of its strikes on the country, and two missiles were identified as posing potential threat to Poland’s territory.

An F-16 fighter jet was scrambled to follow one of the missiles and observed the moment of its crash in an uninhabited area.

Poland’s Tusk says that it’s “an unusual coincidence” that the incident took place just hours after his meeting with Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, during which they discussed bilateral cooperation, including on antiballistic defence.

“Zelenskyy had warned me that they had precise information on Russia’s upcoming massive attack” on Ukraine, Tusk said.

Poland’s PM Tusk is speaking now, chairing an emergency meeting on the incident with senior representatives of the military and the emergency services.

He confirms “a missile” fell on the Polish territory, and says “it looks like” it was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, as reported by Ukraine (9:19).

“Let’s not jump to conclusions before the detailed investigation is complete; we’ll want to be 100 percent certain about what kind of projectile was fired.”

He calls the incident “serious,” but confirms there are no casualties or damage.

He says Poland was prepared to shoot down the rocket if it continued its flight into the Polish territory.

European Council president António Costa stressed that “Russia’s aggression is a threat to the security of Europe as a whole,” as he condemned the overnight strikes on Ukraine and an airspace violation in Poland.

“Last night, Russia launched a massive combined strike against Ukraine.

During the attack, Polish airspace was also violated, underlining once again that Russia’s aggression is a threat to the security of Europe as a whole.

My thoughts are with the victims of these attacks. The European Union stands in full solidarity with the Ukrainian and Polish authorities working tirelessly to protect and defend their citizens.

We are stepping up our support to strengthen Ukraine’s air defence, including anti-missile and anti-drone capabilities. Europe will continue to stand united in the face of this aggression.”

We are getting some first pictures from the site of the incident in Poland, via Poland’s state broadcaster TVP Info.

Estonian president Alar Karis warned that Russia’s war “continues to endanger lives far beyond Ukraine,” as he expressed his nation’s solidarity with Ukraine and Poland.

“Another night of Russian attacks. Civilians killed, including children. Homes destroyed. Cities across Ukraine set ablaze. Now a reported explosion & debris on NATO territory in Poland.

Russia’s war continues to endanger lives far beyond Ukraine. We stand with Poland & Ukraine.”

Polish prime minister Donald Tusk and defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz will chair an emergency meeting on the incident at 10.15 local time (9.15 UK), the Polish government said.

Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said “a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crossed into Poland as part of Russia’s massive strike against Ukraine, violating Nato airspace.”

Polish authorities have yet to formally identify the object that exploded in eastern Poland.

“This is yet another clear demonstration that strengthening Ukraine’s air defence now is urgent and serves as a guarantee for the protection of the entire Euro-Atlantic community,” Sybiha said.

Referencing recent bitter disputes between Poland and Ukraine over shared history, Sybiha added:

“The Russian missile incursion into Poland also serves as a reminder that there is nothing more urgent for our two countries than countering our common, ages-old enemy, which poses a direct threat to both of our nations.

All other disagreements must be put aside during this brutal war. Our top priority must be our shared security.”

At least eight people were killed and dozens injured in another night of heavy Russian attacks on Ukraine, with neighbouring Poland also investigating a reported airspace violation and explosion on its territory.

Russia launched 74 missiles and 284 drones against targets in Ukraine, with casualties reported primarily in Dnipropetrovsk and Lviv regions.

“This Russian terror once again proves that protection against the Russian missile threat is the most important,” Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in response to the attacks, adding Ukraine faced a “critical shortage of air defence missiles from our partners”.

Meanwhile, neighbouring Poland is examining an impact site in the east of the country after “an unidentified object moving westward was detected in Polish airspace” and crashed near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia, some 80 km from the Polish-Ukrainian border.

Local police said that officers investigating reports of a loud bang “discovered a crated and scattered debris from an unidentified object in a field located about 2 km from the nearest buildings.”

Separately, air raid sirens sounded in the eastern city of Lublin. The incident took place just hours after Zelenskyy met in Lublin with Poland’s prime minister Donald Tusk.

Tusk is travelling to the impact site this morning, a government spokesperson said.

Separately, I will also keep an eye on the heatwave hitting large parts of western Europe, and ongoing battle against wildfires in France and Spain.

It’s Thursday, 30 July 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

Reuters has corrected its earlier reporting at 8:12 BST, revising the number of people killed in Russian overnight strikes on Ukraine from 13 to 8.

articles.title: US borrowing costs hit 19-year high as Fed holds interest rates
articles.excerpt:
Bank’s chair pledges to keep up fight against inflation but decision brings fears of a failure to keep pace

US government borrowing costs have hit their highest level since 2007 after the Federal Res...
articles.body_text:
Bank’s chair pledges to keep up fight against inflation but decision brings fears of a failure to keep pace

US government borrowing costs have hit their highest level since 2007 after the Federal Reserve voted to hold its key interest rate steady, feeding fears that the central bank may not move fast enough to tame a rise in inflation.

The yield – or interest rate – on the 30-year US Treasury bond rose 14 basis points to nearly 5.24%, a 19-year high, after the Fed announced its decision to hold its main rate at between 3.5% and 3.75% for the fifth meeting in a row.

Kevin Warsh, the Fed chair, said the bank would “not waver” in its commitment to tackling rising prices.

A prolonged period of high inflation meant that some Americans believed the central bank had an “implicit target” above its 2% target, he added.

“There is no soft implicit target: not on this committee’s watch,” Warsh said. “There’s only a target and it’s 2%. This Fed will not waver … Our credibility rests on performing our duties and delivering on our responsibilities.”

The decision to leave rates on hold spooked investors who are worried about the US economy’s ability to absorb a rise inflation triggered by Donald Trump’s war in Iran.

US inflation cooled to an annual rate of 3.5% in June after Washington and Tehran agreed a brief ceasefire – but this has since ended, with both sides exchanging fire and sending oil prices climbing higher again.

Felix Schmidt, a senior economist at the bank Berenberg, said Warsh had not “conclusively answered the question of why the Fed did not hike”.

He noted that Warsh implied at a press conference that an interest rate rise in the near term might not be necessary due to the rise in bond yields, which has already pushed up the cost of borrowing across the US economy.

“Perhaps Warsh hopes that higher capital market interest rates will help fight inflation in the short term, while the US central bank under new leadership decides on its approach,” Schmidt said.

Before the Fed’s meeting this week, financial markets had priced in a 30% chance of a rate rise and, in the absence of such a move, nearly a 100% chance of an increase at the Fed’s September meeting.

After Wednesday, however, traders put the chance of a rate rise in September at about 57%, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.

US stocks also fell sharply on Wednesday, with the blue chip S&P 500 index closing down 1.5%. The Dow Jones industrial average fell 2.2% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 1.7%.

articles.title: Protest group says 30 dead in Pakistan-administered Kashmir vote unrest
articles.excerpt: Watchdogs have raised concerns over mounting reports of deadly clashes during regional elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, where a banned activist group has boycotted the vote and staged prote...
articles.body_text:
Watchdogs have raised concerns over mounting reports of deadly clashes during regional elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, where a banned activist group has boycotted the vote and staged protests.

The clashes between police and protesters earlier this week killed more than 30 people in the region, according to the leaders of the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).

In a video statement on Wednesday shared by Arab News Pakistan, JAAC committee member Sardar Umar Nazir claimed 20 of the group’s supporters had been killed during a march on Monday, when the first round of voting took place.

He listed reports of at least 10 other protesters being killed the following day in the towns of Rawalakot, Mirpur and elsewhere, including during sit-ins.

“Our demand was peaceful, it was peaceful, we tried to keep it non-violent and bullets were fired at it,” said Nazir in the video statement.

Pakistani authorities said a member of the security personnel was killed and five more were injured in clashes on Monday.

Rights group Amnesty International called the reports of lethal force against protesters in the area “disturbing” and urged an investigation.

Pear Pandya, a senior analyst at conflict monitor ACLED, said the violence in Pakistan-administered Kashmir “is bound to overshadow the legitimacy of the entire electoral exercise”.

Monday’s first-round vote – covering the districts of Mirpur, Kotli and Bhimber – will be followed by two more rounds on August 2 and August 10.

Pakistan’s primary governing party, ⁠the PML-N, won nine out of the 13 seats that were up for election on Monday.

JAAC was banned by the local government under “anti-terrorism laws” in June, causing deadly protests to erupt in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

Banking, roads and internet services have largely been disrupted since then, hindering the flow of information.

Pakistani officials have justified the crackdown by alleging that armed and India-backed fighters joined the Kashmiri protesters. India has rejected similar accusations in the past.

Amnesty has called the ban on JAAC unlawful and said it does not provide justification for authorities to “mete out deadly violence against protesters”.

The rights group has also urged Pakistani authorities to ”restore all communications access and allow media and independent observers into the area”, its acting regional director for South Asia, Isabelle Lassee, said.

One of JAAC’s central demands regarding the regional elections is the abolition of 12 assembly seats reserved for Kashmiri refugees.

JAAC supporters say the seats are used by major Pakistani political parties to tip the composition of the local parliament in their favour with those who mostly live outside the region.

To form a regional government, the PML-N would likely need the support of some of the 12 representatives, said Hasan Askari, ‌a political analyst.

“But when their government is dependent on those 12 controversial seats, how would it be able to find a solution for this issue?” Askari told the Reuters news agency.

Even among the candidates that did not boycott the vote on Monday, the results were contested. Parties accused each other of ballot ‌box ‌stealing and vote rigging.

articles.title: Reform UK to hold press conference after Met rules out investigating Polanski over anti-Farage message – UK politics live
articles.excerpt:
Green party said it was ‘obvious from the start’ that Polanski had not committed an offence

Good morning. Reform UK are holding a press conference this morning. It is going to feature Robert Jenrick,...
articles.body_text:
Green party said it was ‘obvious from the start’ that Polanski had not committed an offence

Good morning. Reform UK are holding a press conference this morning. It is going to feature Robert Jenrick, the party’s Treasury spokesperson, and he wants to talk about Andy Burnham’s speech yesterday about social care reform. But we already know what Jenrick thinks about that, and there are plenty of other stories that reporters might want to ask about.

For a start, there is Anna Isaac’s latest Guardian scoop about George Cottrell.

Someone might want to ask about a Reform UK councillor from Sunderland being charged with posting a grossly offensive message on social media after allegedly making a racist comment about Nigerians.

And Jenrick may want to talk about a different police charging decision – the Met saying no further action will be taken against the Green party leader, Zack Polanski, after a photo of a man with a T-shirt showing a guillotine and the phrase “we’re only making plans for Nigel”.

Here is Aletha Adu’s story about this announcement.

And here is the full press release from the Metropolitan police. The Met says it is “unlikely that the sharing of the image online would constitute a criminal offence” and that, because more than 100 other people shared the post, it would be unfair just to take action against Polanski, and disproportionate to investigate everyone who did the same.

Reform UK are not happy about this. “Once again we see that we are living in two-tier Britain,” a party spokesperson claimed.

But the Green party said it was “obvious from the start” that Polanski had not committed an offence and that Reform UK were “always using this as a political football for their own cynical purposes to distract from questions” about how Farage’s party was funded.

9.30am: The Ministry of Justice publishes figures about assaults and deaths in prisons in England and Wales.

10am: Reform UK’s Robert Jenrick holds a press conference.

Morning: Andy Burnham is on a visit in Cumbria to confirm an £8bn spending announcement as part of the next phase of the nuclear submarine replacement programme.

Also, in Greater Manchester people are already voting in the byelection for a new mayor, to replace Andy Burnham.

As I explained earlier this month, we are no longer going to have comments open below the line on this blog. From today, if you want to contact me, or anyone else writing the blog when I am not here, please email politics.live@theguardian.com. You can use this to flag up corrections, comments for publication, questions or complaints. There is a longer post here about how we hope this will work.

Robert Jenrick, Reform UK’s Treasury spokesperson, is speaking at the start of his press conference.

Expanding on the statement he issued yesterday, he claims that Andy Burnham is firmly committed to introducing a “death tax” to fund his plans for social care reform.

There were an estimated 2,877 heat-associated deaths during hot weather in May and June this year, almost double the figure reported for the summer of 2025, the UK Health Security Agency has said.

I will post more on this when I get further details.

There was a time when a government announcement about an investment in nuclear deterrent would focus on what this might mean for Russian cities that could be wiped out. Now, though, the government likes to frame the massive spending allocated to the Trident renewal programme as a job creation programme for Britain.

Here is the No 10 news release on Andy Burnham’s visit to Barrow today. It’s headlined:

double quotation markBurnham drives defence to deliver security and growth in every postcode with £8.4bn nuclear submarine investment supporting 22,000 apprenticeships

And here is Dan Sabbagh’s overnight news story.

As Dan explains, this is not really a new announcement; the £8.4bn investment was already in the pipeline. And the 22,000 covers the total number of apprenticeships likely to be supported up to 2035 as a result of the entire project building four new Dreadnought submarines to replace the four Vanguard submarines that are currently carrying the nuclear deterrent.

There is one new apprenticeship scheme that Burnham is announcing. But it is fairly minuscule. As No 10 explains in its news release:

double quotation markThe trailblazing initiative will help local small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the local defence supply chain to recruit and train 30 apprentices across the next three years and will use the successful apprenticeship model set up by BAE Systems in the region.

It is an example of how the government is baking in opportunities for young people to its approach to procurement and paves the way for more schemes to help those who miss out on their first choice apprenticeships– delivering growth and prosperity for local communities across the UK.

As Politico explains in its London Playbook briefing, it is unusual for a PM to be associated with such a small-scale announcement. But Burnham is focused on the big headline numbers, and he knows that just because the media have heard these numbers before, that does not mean the public has registered them. He is also committed to reindustrialising Britain and keen to promote any initiative that will support this narrative.

In its statement yesterday the Metropolitan police said that “a crime should be recorded” in relation to the person wearing the T-shirt showing a guillotine and the phrase “we’re only making plans for Nigel” that was in the picture shared by Zack Polanski. The Met said:

double quotation markThe event where that occurred took place in Bristol and as a result, we have transferred the crime report to Avon and Somerset police. They will consider what further action should now follow.

But Avon and Somerset police have decided not to take any further action. A spokesperson for the force said:

double quotation markWe have carefully considered the available evidence in relation to a photograph taken at a political event in Bristol and subsequently shared on social media as part of a gallery of 20 images.

Particular consideration has been given to the context around the image; its use of song lyrics, and the marketing of the T-shirt as a satirical piece.

No complaints were received from people at the event at which it was worn and there is no evidence the wearer of the T-shirt intended to threaten any individual, or encourage anyone else to do so.

As a result, a senior detective has determined that the threshold for a criminal offence has not been met and no further action will be taken.

The safety of elected politicians is something we take extremely seriously and we continue to take action wherever a threat is identified.

The affected parties have been updated of our decision.

Good morning. Reform UK are holding a press conference this morning. It is going to feature Robert Jenrick, the party’s Treasury spokesperson, and he wants to talk about Andy Burnham’s speech yesterday about social care reform. But we already know what Jenrick thinks about that, and there are plenty of other stories that reporters might want to ask about.

For a start, there is Anna Isaac’s latest Guardian scoop about George Cottrell.

Someone might want to ask about a Reform UK councillor from Sunderland being charged with posting a grossly offensive message on social media after allegedly making a racist comment about Nigerians.

And Jenrick may want to talk about a different police charging decision – the Met saying no further action will be taken against the Green party leader, Zack Polanski, after a photo of a man with a T-shirt showing a guillotine and the phrase “we’re only making plans for Nigel”.

Here is Aletha Adu’s story about this announcement.

And here is the full press release from the Metropolitan police. The Met says it is “unlikely that the sharing of the image online would constitute a criminal offence” and that, because more than 100 other people shared the post, it would be unfair just to take action against Polanski, and disproportionate to investigate everyone who did the same.

Reform UK are not happy about this. “Once again we see that we are living in two-tier Britain,” a party spokesperson claimed.

But the Green party said it was “obvious from the start” that Polanski had not committed an offence and that Reform UK were “always using this as a political football for their own cynical purposes to distract from questions” about how Farage’s party was funded.

9.30am: The Ministry of Justice publishes figures about assaults and deaths in prisons in England and Wales.

10am: Reform UK’s Robert Jenrick holds a press conference.

Morning: Andy Burnham is on a visit in Cumbria to confirm an £8bn spending announcement as part of the next phase of the nuclear submarine replacement programme.

Also, in Greater Manchester people are already voting in the byelection for a new mayor, to replace Andy Burnham.

As I explained earlier this month, we are no longer going to have comments open below the line on this blog. From today, if you want to contact me, or anyone else writing the blog when I am not here, please email politics.live@theguardian.com. You can use this to flag up corrections, comments for publication, questions or complaints. There is a longer post here about how we hope this will work.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia confirmed to host Asian Champions League Elite finals
articles.excerpt: Saudi ‌Arabia will organise the next three ⁠editions ⁠of the Asian Champions League Elite finals after the Asian Football Confederation’s ⁠executive committee confirmed the country’s provisional hosti...
articles.body_text:
Saudi ‌Arabia will organise the next three ⁠editions ⁠of the Asian Champions League Elite finals after the Asian Football Confederation’s ⁠executive committee confirmed the country’s provisional hosting rights had been made permanent.

The Saudis have hosted the first two editions of the event, which sees the quarterfinals, semifinals and final played in ‌a centralised venue, since the continent’s premier club competition was restructured before the 2024/2025 season.

Jeddah-based outfit Al-Ahli have won the title on the two occasions the city has hosted the ⁠finals, defeating Japan’s Kawasaki ⁠Frontale in 2025 before beating Machida Zelvia, also from Japan, in May.

The upcoming edition of the tournament, which ⁠features the domestic champions of the leading competitions from ⁠the region, will ⁠see the league phase expanded from 24 to 32 teams.

The qualifying rounds will start on August 11, ‌with the draw for the league phase to be held in Kuala Lumpur ‌on ‌August 18 and play commencing on September 14.

Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli completed their back-to-back victories with a 1-0 win after extra time against Machida Zelvia, of the Japanese J1 League, in last year’s final.

Fellow Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal are the record winners of the competition with four wins from nine appearances in the final – which is also a record.

Japan’s Urawa Red Diamonds and South Korea’s Pohang Steelers have each lifted the trophy twice, having both appeared in the final on three occasions.

articles.title: Major incident declared in Suffolk as 90 firefighters tackle wildfire on heathland
articles.excerpt:
Several people evacuated after ‘large-scale, wind-driven’ fire breaks out at Dunwich Heath near Leiston

A major incident has been declared as firefighters battle a large heathland fire on the Suffolk...
articles.body_text:
Several people evacuated after ‘large-scale, wind-driven’ fire breaks out at Dunwich Heath near Leiston

A major incident has been declared as firefighters battle a large heathland fire on the Suffolk coast.

Suffolk fire and rescue service was called to reports of a wildfire at Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, shortly after 5.30pm on Wednesday, and crews remained at the scene on Thursday morning. About 90 firefighters were tackling the blaze, while several people had been evacuated. Leiston is about 5km away from Sizewell B, but firefighters have said there is not thought to be any danger to the nuclear power station at this time.

The service said a major incident had been declared “due to the size and complexity” of the blaze. People have been urged to avoid the area where possible and keep windows and doors closed.

In an update on Thursday morning, the fire service said: “At this time there is no current risk to Sizewell B, due to the distance from the fire and the direction it is travelling (easterly). However, this is a live and dynamic situation and as a result any further updates will be shared accordingly.”

As a precaution, crews have been focused on protecting nearby properties, while preparations have been made for the potential to evacuate about 200 caravans at the Cliff House holiday park if conditions deteriorate.

Dan Davis, a station manager with Suffolk fire and rescue service, said: “Crews from Leiston attended the scene and were met with what is a large-scale, wind-driven forestry fire.

“The incident has subsequently been upgraded to a major incident. We currently have approximately 90 firefighters on scene working incredibly hard in arduous conditions to bring this fire under control.”

People displaced by the fire have been advised to attend Westleton Village Hall at 8am for further updates.

Specialist drones were being overnight to assess fire behaviour and support operational decision-making, while crews also deployed multipurpose all-wheel-drive Unimogs and 4x4 quad bikes.

The UK Health Security Agency had issued an amber heat-health alert for the East Midlands, the east and south-east of England and London, which was to remain in place until 9am on Thursday. The agency has warned that rising temperatures could increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups.

In Scotland, crews said they were making significant progress tackling a wildfire in the Cairngorms that broke out two weeks ago.

articles.title: ‘Grey lump with orange wings’: migrating moth descends on UK gardens
articles.excerpt:
Boom in hummingbird hawk-moth sightings put down to hot weather, strong winds and food scarcity in Europe

He had just sat down to dinner in the garden when a speedy visitor whizzed by – a “grey lump ...
articles.body_text:
Boom in hummingbird hawk-moth sightings put down to hot weather, strong winds and food scarcity in Europe

He had just sat down to dinner in the garden when a speedy visitor whizzed by – a “grey lump with orange wings”, recalled Luke Burstow, from Sussex. It was a hummingbird hawk-moth, a flying insect that migrates to the UK from continental Europe and north Africa.

“I was like: ‘Wow!’,” said the software project manager. “I didn’t even know they existed.”

Burstow is one of many UK wildlife watchers who have described seeing the moth on social media lately. “This made my day,” wrote one Reddit user after their sighting.

Butterfly and moth experts told the Guardian that 2026 could be a bumper year for hummingbird hawk-moths in the UK after a boom in sightings during recent weeks. Hot weather and strong winds appear to have brought many of the insects here from more southerly climes.

Burstow, who, along with his wife, spied the hummingbird hawk-moth enjoying buddleia flowers on 30 June, said: “It was just so different to everything else you normally see.” After quickly Googling the species, Burstow ran inside to grab his camera and managed to take some photos of the creature. He marvelled at how, even with a very fast shutter speed, the moth’s wings – which beat roughly 80 times per second – still appeared slightly blurry in his photos.

“We’ve had a big increase in sightings and inquiries about the hummingbird hawk-moth sent to us this year,” said Richard Austin, a recording schemes officer at the charity Butterfly Conservation. “We expect it is going to be a great summer for them.” Austin cautioned, however, that it was too early to compare their numbers with previous years.

Hummingbird hawk-moths may be spotted all around the UK, including in Northern Ireland and even northern Scotland. Warm southerly winds associated with recent heatwaves could have helped bring high numbers of the moths to the UK, said Richard Harrington, an honorary fellow of the Royal Entomological Society. “It may also be that their food plants are drying out in their Mediterranean breeding areas,” he added.

Sunny weather in the UK has perhaps encouraged people to spend more time than usual in their gardens, raising the chances that they will spot one of the moths, said Ray Barnett, a council member at the British Entomological and Natural History Society. “I’m in Bristol and there’s lots of people recording it locally,” he said.

There’s a chance the hummingbird hawk-moths could stick around, should the UK continue to experience milder winters due to global warming, Barnett added.

Hibernating adults that make it through the British winter may go on to reproduce in the UK on a regular basis. Hummingbird hawk-moth larvae feed on plants including lady’s bedstraw and hedge bedstraw, which are common wildflowers in the UK.

“If these weather patterns continue, then [the moth] is going to survive winters regularly,” said Barnett. “It’s almost becoming a resident species rather than a purely migratory species.”

articles.title: Infantino insists FIFA’s World Cup plan is proposal and not ‘obligation’
articles.excerpt: FIFA President Gianni ⁠Infantino has called ⁠the plan to sell stakes in the World Cup a proposal but “not an obligation”, after the idea ⁠provoked a furious response from a number of football authorit...
articles.body_text:
FIFA President Gianni ⁠Infantino has called ⁠the plan to sell stakes in the World Cup a proposal but “not an obligation”, after the idea ⁠provoked a furious response from a number of football authorities.

FIFA announced plans this week to create a $20bn subsidiary to run ⁠the World Cup and its other events, and said it will offer stakes of up to 20% in it to external investors.

The proposal drew strong criticism from the sport’s regional confederations, ‌which said they were blindsided by the plan by world football’s governing body to bring private investors into the sport.

But Infantino said strengthening the commercial side of the game is the natural next step in this evolution.

“It’s part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above ⁠all, it is an opportunity but not ⁠an obligation, and, as I said, it kicks off the consultation process,” Infantino said in a video provided by FIFA on Wednesday.

FIFA is one ⁠of the world’s wealthiest sporting organisations, generating billions of dollars in revenue, largely from ⁠broadcasting rights, sponsorship and other commercial deals ⁠linked to the World Cup.

Infantino insisted in his remarks that fans will remain the cornerstone of football and said, “FIFA obviously continues to govern football without any external interference.

“And the flagship tournament it ‌organises, ‌like the FIFA World Cup or the FIFA Women’s World Cup, will always remain.”
