“This is about bringing back hope that we can finally fix the difficult issues that have been ignored for too long, and making Britain believe again. That’s why I’m making this choice and I’m prepared to put everything I’ve got behind it.”

An average of 13,600 people a day were stuck in hospital beds last month despite being medically fit to leave, including some delayed because of the availability of adult social care, underlining the pressure on the NHS.

While Labour MPs have broadly welcomed the prospect of reform, several cautioned that there would have to be serious consideration of how to protect people from losing their homes to care costs or penalising those who had already saved for retirement and care with new taxes.

One minister said the prime minister “must exercise a lot of care” in managing the sensitive trade-offs between the quality of care versus the cost and who pays for it.

“There are no easy answers, and I don’t think we can just dive straight into saying ‘This is the solution and this is what’s going to happen,’ because we have a prime minister and in many ways a government … with no specific mandate on a specific measure.”

A centrist Labour MP said: “It’s vital that the UK at least tries to do something because we will never be able to contain the rising costs of the NHS. Our ability to genuinely improve the quality of health care will be stymied if we don’t have a quality social care service that relieves pressure.”

Others on the party’s left urged the government to consider adopting a full NHS-style system that would rely on some taxation, but would also highlight that Burnham’s premiership is ready to not just “talk the talk but also walk the walk”.

“If we’re talking big and bold we shouldn’t shy away from this option. It took from 1945 to 1948 to get the NHS up and running. We’ve still got years to start the process but we have to really try to shake this broken system,” one said.

“Andy doesn’t have the goodwill from the electorate that Keir did in 2024 because we messed it up over the last two years so people feel betrayed and ignored,” another added. “This is a moment where we now have to prove ourselves.”

A Tory source said: “If Burnham was serious about working cross-party he would have given us more than 18 hours’ notice for a 30-minute meeting during recess and the invitation wouldn’t have been immediately press released. It’s almost like it’s only being done for show.”

Davey posted on X: “I’m with my family in France and as people know I have a disabled son who needs 24/7 care so I can’t be back in Westminster tomorrow but I look forward to meeting Andy Burnham over Zoom. I’m hopeful this call may prove to be the first step towards fixing our broken care service.

Nigel Farage, who has not been invited to attend as he is not currently a sitting MP and Reform has just seven seats, accused Burnham of “conspiring behind closed doors with the failed political establishment”.

The Reform leader and candidate for Clacton added: “If Andy Burnham is serious about putting politics aside to solve Britain’s biggest problems, it’s remarkable that he’s chosen to ignore the party that led over 300 national opinion polls and represents thousands of councillors and millions of Britons across the country.”

articles.title: Former Gavin Newsom aide shares fresh details of affair
articles.excerpt:
Ruby Rippey writes in Vanity Fair of relationship with then San Francisco mayor and appears to contradict his account

A former aide to Gavin Newsom has publicly shared for the first time her full acc...
articles.body_text:
Ruby Rippey writes in Vanity Fair of relationship with then San Francisco mayor and appears to contradict his account

A former aide to Gavin Newsom has publicly shared for the first time her full account of their affair, which took place more than two decades ago when Newsom was mayor of San Francisco.

In a new essay published in Vanity Fair on Tuesday, Ruby Rippey writes about her struggles with alcoholism, substance abuse and her relationship with Newsom while she worked as his appointments secretary and was married to his deputy chief of staff and later the manager of the mayor’s re-election campaign.

The essay provides the most detailed look yet at Rippey’s relationship with Newsom, now in the final year of his second term as governor of California – and is likely to rekindle interest in the scandal ahead of his widely expected run for the White House in 2028. In the essay, Rippey does not refer to Newsom by name, but as her “boss” and the “mayor”.

“For my former boss, it is a footnote in a longer arc of ascent,” Rippey writes in the Vanity Fair essay, titled How I Blew Up – Then Rebuilt – My Life. “For me, it is the fracture that split my life into before and after.”

Newsom, who was single at the time, publicly admitted to the relationship in 2007, memorably telling reporters at a city hall press conference: “Everything you’ve heard and read is true.” In his new memoir, Newsom describes their relationship as “the briefest of affairs”. But Rippey’s telling complicates his account of their story.

Newsom writes in his new book that he “came clean” to her husband and his top aide Alex Tourk – a version Rippey says gives Newsom “credit for something I had already done”.

“Technically defensible, perhaps, but one that leaves the unmistakable impression that he, not I, was the one who told Alex the truth,” she writes.

In the essay, Rippey describes the early days of the newly elected mayor’s administration, her marriage, pregnancy, struggles with alcohol and her ensuing relationship with Newsom as it veered into an extramarital affair.

She eventually went to rehab and left her job with the mayor’s office.

After the story became public, Rippey was inundated with calls from journalists and was the subject of frenzied media coverage about the affair.

Jennifer Siebel Newsom, the first partner of California who started dating Newsom shortly afterward, told journalists in 2007 that Rippey was the “culprit”– remarks she later apologized for.

The office of the governor and a spokesperson for Siebel Newsom did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In the aftermath of the incident, Kamala Harris, then the district attorney, contacted Rippey, she writes. Rippey was being urged to speak publicly about the incident, she told Harris, who advised her to pause and that taking time would give her “better perspective”.

“It turns out to be the best advice I receive. I am newly sober and still inside the wreckage – unable to make sense of anything, let alone speak clearly about it,” Rippey writes.

Rippey and her husband eventually divorced.

For years, Rippey said little publicly about her relationship with Newsom. During the MeToo movement, she observed a new narrative about their relationship emerge in which Rippey saw herself cast as a “powerless subordinate”, she writes.

At the time, Rippey said she was doubtful it applied to her situation. Although she was Newsom’s “subordinate”, she said in 2018, she was also “a free-thinking, 33-year-old, adult married woman and mother. Also happened to have an unfortunate inclination toward drinking-to-excess and self-destruction.”

Taking responsibility felt like the last form of agency, Rippey writes in the essay. But since the reckoning, she has re-evaluated the role power can play in a relationship between a subordinate and their boss.

“Both things are true,” she writes. “I am responsible for what I did. Power does not distribute consequences evenly.”

Rippey is now 20 years sober, she writes, and has remarried and rebuilt her relationship with her ex-husband.

articles.title: Draymond Green returns to Golden State for $27M after Warriors' pursuit of LeBron James falls flat
articles.excerpt:
ESPN host Monica McNutt is under EXTREME heat after claiming Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark needs to show more "accountability and self-awareness."

Draymond Green is staying put, and it cost t...
articles.body_text:
ESPN host Monica McNutt is under EXTREME heat after claiming Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark needs to show more "accountability and self-awareness."

Draymond Green is staying put, and it cost the Golden State Warriors exactly what it would've cost them all along.

The 36-year-old is returning on a one-year, $27.7 million contract, according to Klutch Sports.

Draymond Green of the Golden State Warriors reacts during a game against the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, Calif., on April 10, 2026. (Rocky Widner/NBAE)

Back in June, Green declined his original $27.7 million player option to help Golden State create cap space for a run at LeBron James. The Warriors believed they had a legitimate shot at pairing James with Stephen Curry.

LEBRON JAMES MAKES NBA FREE AGENCY DECISION, ANNOUNCES PLANS TO SIGN WITH 76ERS

Instead, James chose Philadelphia, signing a two-year deal with the 76ers. Golden State's LeBron gamble failed, leaving the Warriors right back where they started with Green.

April 27, 2021; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green (23) during the third quarter against the Dallas Mavericks at Chase Center. (Kyle Terada-USA TODAY Sports)

The deal does not include a no-trade clause. It also pushes Golden State over the first apron, limiting the Warriors to veteran minimum additions while preserving future cap flexibility.

Both Green and James are represented by Rich Paul and Klutch Sports. Green's opt-out gave Golden State its cleanest path to LeBron while leaving the Warriors with virtually no realistic scenario in which they could turn around and offer him less if the recruiting pitch failed.

Golden State Warriors' Draymond Green (23) celebrates after scoring against the Cleveland Cavaliers in December.

Once LeBron picked Philadelphia, re-signing Green became the obvious move. General manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. had even less incentive to alienate a franchise cornerstone after missing on James, especially after reports last season linked Green to trade discussions with Milwaukee.

The one concession Dunleavy secured was keeping the deal to a single year. Green isn't the athlete he was during Golden State's dynasty years. The shorter contract preserves future flexibility while avoiding a longer commitment to an aging star.

The Warriors get their emotional enforcer and defensive anchor back, but they're still paying premium money for a roster that looks well past its championship window.

They cleared cap space chasing LeBron, struck out, then circled back and paid Green exactly what he would've earned anyway.

Sometimes the biggest move of the offseason is paying for the one that never happened.

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

articles.title: Australia news live: Jacinta Allan was subjected to ‘vile sexism’ as premier, Julia Gillard says

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Forme...
articles.body_text:
Former PM says ousted Victorian premier was ‘courageous in combating misogyny’ and was a trailblazer for other women. Follow updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former prime minister Julia Gillard says departing Victorian premier Jacinta Allan has been subjected to “vile sexism” during her term in office.

Posting on Instagram yesterday, Gillard said Allan would be remembered as a role model and trailblazer who governed for all Victorians, but particularly for the lives of women and girls.

double quotation markThere is no doubt that as the second woman to lead the state, she has been subjected to vile sexism.

She has been courageous in calling it out and combating this misogyny. As a result, she has made it easier for the women that follow.

Gillard herself went viral globally in 2012, after delivering her now famous misogyny speech attacking the opposition leader Tony Abbott in the Australian parliament. The 15-minute tirade against Abbott inspired a range of diverse musical adaptations of the speech from classical choral arrangements to punk anthems.

Gillard, who represented the Victorian electorate of Lalor from 1998 to 2013, now sits on the boards and trusts of a number of NGOs focusing on health and women’s rights, and works the speaking circuit.

Her post also congratulated the man who toppled Allan as premier, Ben Carroll.

double quotation markI know how hard working he is and how much he cares about ensuring every child gets the best possible start in life. I wish him and his team well in the months to come.

CSIRO head to defend agency, and job cuts, in press club address

The head of Australia’s national science agency will defend planned job cuts, warning without a refocus the organisation risked doing nothing at scale in the future, AAP reports.

In an address to the National Press Club in Canberra on Wednesday, CSIRO chief executive Doug Hilton is expected to address the agency’s choice to cut jobs from key areas in the face of funding pressures.

He is expected to say the organisations faced a sobering backlog of essential repairs and renewal at the end of 2025. More than 80% of CSIRO’s 800 buildings were no longer fit for purpose, he will say.

Hilton is expected to say the leadership team chose to exit some areas of science and narrow its focus rather than run the risk of doing nothing at scale.

Last November, the science agency said up to 350 research positions would be slashed as the “cost of doing science has gone up”.

Good morning, Nick Visser here to guide you through the day’s news. Let’s get to it.

Bill Shorten backs royal commission into the construction sector

Former union boss and former leader of the Labor party Bill Shorten has leant his support behind newly crowned Victorian premier Ben Carroll’s announcement he will call a royal commission into the construction sector.

double quotation markHe wants to act with integrity, and he wants to act in everyone’s interests.

I think he understands [what] people will be assessing: is he serving the people or is he just playing politics? So I thought he was very straight. He’s in there for Victorians, not trying to just tick the box and get particular interest groups on side.

Shorten, former national secretary of the Australian Workers’ Union before entering parliament in 2007, said Carroll’s call yesterday to set up a royal commission was timely.

double quotation markI think the national mood or the state mood was there for it. I just think that the costs of construction … there may be exaggerations, but there is something rotten going on in construction, and people want to see it can be dealt with. This is public infrastructure, so it’s taxpayer money.

You can read more about Carroll’s announcement here:

Former prime minister Julia Gillard says departing Victorian premier Jacinta Allan has been subjected to “vile sexism” during her term in office.

Posting on Instagram yesterday, Gillard said Allan would be remembered as a role model and trailblazer who governed for all Victorians, but particularly for the lives of women and girls.

double quotation markThere is no doubt that as the second woman to lead the state, she has been subjected to vile sexism.

She has been courageous in calling it out and combating this misogyny. As a result, she has made it easier for the women that follow.

Gillard herself went viral globally in 2012, after delivering her now famous misogyny speech attacking the opposition leader Tony Abbott in the Australian parliament. The 15-minute tirade against Abbott inspired a range of diverse musical adaptations of the speech from classical choral arrangements to punk anthems.

Gillard, who represented the Victorian electorate of Lalor from 1998 to 2013, now sits on the boards and trusts of a number of NGOs focusing on health and women’s rights, and works the speaking circuit.

Her post also congratulated the man who toppled Allan as premier, Ben Carroll.

double quotation markI know how hard working he is and how much he cares about ensuring every child gets the best possible start in life. I wish him and his team well in the months to come.

Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it’ll be Nick Visser with the main action.

articles.title: Donald Trump and world leaders attend Lindsey Graham’s funeral
articles.excerpt:
Hundreds of mourners have paid their respects to the late Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina.

The Republican lawmaker and key ally of President Donald Trump unexpectedly died on July 11.

Graha...
articles.body_text:
Hundreds of mourners have paid their respects to the late Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina.

The Republican lawmaker and key ally of President Donald Trump unexpectedly died on July 11.

Graham was elected to the US Senate in 2002 and was re-elected in 2008, 2014 and 2020. In 1994, he was elected to ⁠the US House of Representatives, the lower house of the US Congress, for South Carolina’s third congressional district. He recently served as chairman of the Senate Budget Committee. Graham also served as a member of ‌the Senate Committee on Appropriations, the Senate Judiciary Committee and the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works.

He was a strong supporter of the 2003 US invasion of Iraq and had long pushed for military action against Iran.

Graham was a longtime backer of Israel and supported Trump’s ongoing war on Iran. In a planned documentary, Graham told the filmmakers he “almost cried” after the US and Israel began strikes on Iran in February.

He also vocally supported Ukraine after Russia invaded the country in 2022.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and several other world leaders attended Graham’s funeral service on Tuesday afternoon at the Washington National Cathedral in Washington, DC.

Trump gave remarks, calling Graham a force in the world and US politics. He called Graham “a beloved friend” and said that he “died doing the work he was born to do”.

“For more than 30 years, nothing of consequence happened in this capital without Lindsey Graham knowing about it. Nothing of significance happened anywhere in the world without Lindsey Graham having a view on it,” Trump said. “And no bill became law in the most exceptional republic in human history without Lindsey Graham having a say in it.”

He added: “He was a man who gave America the full measure of his good and mighty heart until that heart itself just gave out.”

articles.title: WNBA media predictably embarrasses itself again by ignoring Sophie Cunningham story over All-Star Weekend
articles.excerpt: WNBA player Sophie Cunningham stirs debate by doubling down on her defense of women's sports, emphasizing the foundational role of Title IX. XX-XY Athletics founder and CEO Jennifer Sey champions Cunn...
articles.body_text:
WNBA player Sophie Cunningham stirs debate by doubling down on her defense of women's sports, emphasizing the foundational role of Title IX. XX-XY Athletics founder and CEO Jennifer Sey champions Cunningham's stance, noting its alignment with widespread beliefs and legal precedents despite media backlash.

The WNBA media had every opportunity to show it could cover the league like a serious professional sport over All-Star Weekend in Chicago.

Reporters had access to the league’s biggest players and Commissioner Cathy Engelbert just days after Sophie Cunningham said biological males should not compete in girls' and women's sports. Yet not one public answer emerged from the weekend about whether the league’s stars agreed with her.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said protecting young girls in sports is "common sense." (Getty Images)

One important disclosure: OutKick and Fox News Digital attempted to cover All-Star Weekend in person, and I planned to ask the players and Commissioner Cathy Engelbert about Cunningham’s comments (if given the chance). We applied for a credential through the NBA/WNBA credential portal, but the league denied the request because it was submitted 10 days after its June 16 deadline.

The portal was still open and accepted the application, which was submitted four weeks prior to the event.

I had not received the WNBA’s original credential advisory or either of the two reminder emails the league said it sent. We asked the league to reconsider, noting that OutKick and Fox News Digital were approved to cover last year's All-Star Game, but the WNBA stood by its decision.

So, no, OutKick did not ask the players in Chicago because we didn't have access to do so.

That left the job to the reporters who received credentials.

After reviewing the publicly available press conferences, interview videos, transcripts and coverage from All-Star Weekend, I could not find one instance of a WNBA All-Star or Commissioner Cathy Engelbert being asked about Cunningham’s statement.

Cunningham’s comments came in an ESPN profile published just before the All-Star break.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’" Cunningham said. "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

Reporters grilled Cunningham just before the break. She did not retreat.

"I said what I said. I think it’s kinda common sense," Cunningham said.

The story quickly moved beyond Cunningham.

Las Vegas Aces forward Brianna Turner publicly defended transgender participation in women’s sports. The White House backed Cunningham. The Associated Press identified the transgender-athlete debate as one of the major cultural issues hanging over All-Star Weekend.

Brianna Turner of the Las Vegas Aces thinks biological males should be allowed to compete in women's sports and use women's locker rooms. (Getty Images)

In other words, this wasn't an obscure social media controversy that reporters could credibly claim they hadn't seen.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SEES SUPPORT SURGE AFTER STAR PUTS CAREER ON LINE FOR GIRLS SPORTS

An active WNBA player had taken a clear position on one of the biggest debates in women’s sports. Her comments drew a response from another player and reached the White House. The league’s most prominent athletes were about to gather in the same city for several days of media availability.

The questions practically wrote themselves.

Should women’s sports be reserved for biological females?

Do Cunningham’s comments conflict with the values of the WNBA?

The WNBA assembled 22 All-Stars in Chicago, including Caitlin Clark, A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Paige Bueckers and Cunningham’s Indiana Fever teammates Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston. Players participated in practice interviews, informal scrums and official press conferences throughout the weekend.

There is always a chance that a reporter asked someone about Cunningham during a scrum that was not recorded or published. It is impossible to prove that the topic never came up once over the weekend.

But journalism is not a private conversation between a reporter and an athlete. The point is to provide information to the public.

No outlet appears to have produced an answer from an All-Star. No videos surfaced, no quote appeared in a story and no reporter posted a player’s response on social media.

If someone asked, the answer apparently was not important enough to publish. The practical result is the same.

The public still has no idea what the WNBA’s most prominent players think about trans-identifying biological males competing in women's sports and using women's locker rooms.

WNBA "reporters" don't appear to have asked a single All-Star about Sophie Cunningham's comments. (NBAE via Getty Images)

The irony is that All-Star Weekend included the inaugural WNBA Media & Innovation Summit. The event’s stated theme was "From Participation to Power," and organizers promoted it as a discussion about who will shape the future of women’s sports.

Evidently, asking female athletes whether women’s sports should be reserved for females didn't fit the program.

The failure to question Engelbert was particularly glaring.

The commissioner began her All-Star press conference by addressing racism, misogyny, homophobia, harassment and threats against players. She said the league is built on "inclusion and respect" and pledged to make every player feel safe and supported.

That provided a natural opening to ask about Cunningham.

Does the commissioner believe Cunningham’s comments are consistent with the WNBA’s values?

What is the league’s position on transgender eligibility?

Does Engelbert believe supporting a female-only athletic category is exclusionary?

Not one WNBA "reporter" asked Commissioner Cathy Engelbert about Sophie Cunningham's stance on trans-identifying athletes. (TNS)

Instead, reporters questioned Engelbert about the new replay center, international games, the Las Vegas Aces investigation, the relationship between the league and its players, officiating, security, her future as commissioner, coaching diversity, HBCU internships and her communication style.

Several were legitimate questions. The problem is not that reporters asked about officiating or league operations. The problem is that the full press conference ended without anyone addressing the controversy involving one of Engelbert’s players.

Engelbert even talked about young girls viewing WNBA players as role models.

Cunningham’s entire argument was that young girls deserve protection in locker rooms and athletic competition. Still, no one in the room made the connection. Or, possibly, no one in the room wanted to make the connection.

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

Some reporters had plenty to say about Cunningham. They just didn’t appear interested in asking WNBA players about her.

The Guardian published an All-Star Weekend feature that characterized Cunningham’s comments as "transphobic language." The story included fresh quotes from Courtney Williams, Becky Hammon, Jessica Shepard and A’ja Wilson on other subjects.

Yet the published article contained no response from any of them about Cunningham’s comments.

That captures the problem with much of the media covering this league.

A reporter was comfortable delivering a moral judgment about Cunningham’s statement. Getting a prominent WNBA player on the record about that statement was apparently less important.

The Associated Press also included the controversy in its scene-setting story from Chicago. But the article relied on Cunningham’s previous ESPN quote and Turner’s social media comments rather than producing a response from an All-Star attending the weekend.

The media knew it was a story. They wrote about it. They just decided not to do any actual reporting.

In 2024, Caitlin Clark went through a massive media tour before entering the WNBA. Reporters asked her the same safe questions repeatedly, but no one asked the most influential young woman in American sports what she thought about transgender athletes competing against females.

Like the other WNBA All-Stars, Caitlin Clark wasn't asked about her teammate's comments. (Getty Images)

Later that year, USA Today reporter Christine Brennan asked DiJonai Carrington whether she intentionally poked Clark in the eye. It was a completely reasonable question about something that happened during a basketball game.

The WNBA Players’ Association responded by calling on USA Today to discipline Brennan and suggesting that she should lose access.

Then came the Brittney Griner controversy last season. A viral video showed Griner saying something after fouling out against the Indiana Fever. Many viewers believed she made a racially charged remark.

For nearly three weeks, no WNBA reporter asked Griner what she said. OutKick sought credentials specifically to ask the question and was denied by multiple teams before the Washington Mystics eventually granted access.

When we finally asked Griner, she denied using the phrase attributed to her. The controversy largely died because an athlete finally answered the actual question.

That should have been a lesson for everyone covering the league.

Instead, All-Star Weekend showed that nothing has changed.

The WNBA and its players say they want the attention, revenue and stature afforded to major professional sports leagues. That comes with real media coverage. Sometimes athletes have to answer questions they would rather avoid.

A reporter didn't have to agree with Sophie Cunningham to ask about her comments. In fact, anyone who believed her statement was offensive or harmful had an even stronger reason to ask other players for their views.

OutKick sought access because we intended to ask.

The league denied our credential request, and the reporters who were admitted apparently decided the answer was better left unknown.

The WNBA and its media cheerleaders spent All-Star Weekend celebrating the growth of women’s sports while avoiding the most basic question about who should be allowed to compete in them.

articles.title: Iran and Oman exchange proposals to manage Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt: Iran and Oman have exchanged proposals regarding the future management of the Strait of Hormuz, as points of contention continue to exist between the two nations whose territorial waters border the st...
articles.body_text:
Iran and Oman have exchanged proposals regarding the future management of the Strait of Hormuz, as points of contention continue to exist between the two nations whose territorial waters border the strategic waterway.

Oman presented a proposal to Iran ⁠for ⁠a joint regional mechanism to manage the Strait of Hormuz with “voluntary fees”, Reuters reported on Tuesday. Under the Omani proposal, which reportedly has regional backing, Iran would not exercise sole control ⁠of the strait, an unnamed Gulf source and Western diplomat ⁠told the news agency.

Oman’s proposal is reportedly based on the Strait of Malacca, which connects the Indian and Pacific Oceans. There, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore ask ships that use the strait to voluntarily contribute to fund navigation, environmental protection, and ‌search-and-rescue operations.

This proposal aims to contribute to ending the global disruption to trade caused by the strait’s closure in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Tehran, however, says the strait ⁠cannot go back to its pre-war status where shipping flowed freely,

In comments to Iranian state media on Tuesday, Kazem Gharibabadi, the country’s deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, said Tehran rejects an Omani proposal for an equal division of transit routes between the two countries, as such a plan does not address Tehran’s security concerns.

Gharibabadi said that Tehran proposed to Oman that Iran would manage shipping through its side of ‌the strait and Muscat would manage part but not all of the opposite lane.

He added that Tehran has “no plans to negotiate with the US”, but affirmed talks are proceeding “step by step” with Oman, warning that Tehran will consider “any action” to maintain control over the strait, including the resumption of war.

“The Omanis are now suggesting three lines for the maritime traffic: one that runs through Iran’s territorial waters, an international one, and one through Omani territorial waters,” said Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar, reporting from Tehran. “Despite public statements, our sources tell us Iran is demonstrating some flexibility.”

Al Jazeera’s Tohid Asadi, also reporting from Tehran, said there remain many “points of contention” between Oman and Iran on Hormuz. These include the trajectory of the ships, the fees, the question of who will define the arrangements, and mine clearances – which will reportedly be Iran’s responsibility.

Paul Musgrave, a professor at Georgetown University in Qatar, said Oman’s proposal to Iran to get the Strait of Hormuz running again is positive, but it remains to be seen if hardliners in Iran will go for it.

Musgrave noted that under the Strait of Malacca model, voluntary contributions raise about $70m annually, far from the $1m per ship that’s reportedly been proposed by Tehran as a “service fee” in the Strait of Hormuz.

Meanwhile, Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) foreign ministers met via video call on Tuesday to discuss the latest developments in the conflict, including ways to improve cooperation on issues surrounding freedom and navigation through the waterway, a statement from the Qatari Foreign Ministry said.

The United States suspended a nearly two-week-long campaign of air strikes against Iran over the weekend after pressure from regional mediators to find a diplomatic solution and to return to the memorandum of understanding signed in June, which would allow shipping to resume in the Strait of Hormuz. The strait carried one-fifth of global energy supplies before ⁠the February 28 start of the US-Israel war on Iran.

articles.title: Ex-FDA commissioner confronted on 'outrageous' Fauci diaries by CNBC host
articles.excerpt:
Former FDA commissioner Scott Gottlieb was confronted by CNBC host Joe Kernen on the Anthony Fauci diaries on Monday, as he admitted he was disappointed in them.

Scott Gottlieb, a former FDA commissi...
articles.body_text:
Former FDA commissioner Scott Gottlieb was confronted by CNBC host Joe Kernen on the Anthony Fauci diaries on Monday, as he admitted he was disappointed in them.

Scott Gottlieb, a former FDA commissioner, was confronted about former National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director Anthony Fauci's diaries on Monday in a back-and-forth on CNBC, which host Joe Kernen called "outrageous."

"How about your buddy Fauci, that I've asked you about in the past. You've defended him quite a bit," Kernen said. "I've asked about whether he orchestrated a cover-up of the lab origin because of his involvement in making gain-of-function research possible again in China, which he did. He knew that would come back to haunt him and then basically told his colleagues go with the natural origin. It was obvious three years ago, Scott, to me anyway, and everybody else, that he orchestrated that."

Fauci’s diary entries were released on Saturday by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., detailing the doctor’s role during the COVID-19 crisis through conversations with President Donald Trump, governors, world leaders, media appearances and his personal observations as the pandemic unfolded in 2020.

"Well look, and I've looked through the emails, some of them have been online, I think it's disappointing to see him trying to suppress alternative opinions, and that clearly was evidence from the emails. I thought it was disappointing. The part of it that also disappointed me was how much he enjoyed the media associated with the event and his own appearances," Gotlieb said.

ABC, NBC, CBS, CNN AND MS NOW IGNORE FAUCI DIARY ENTRIES THAT REVEAL FIXATION ON FAME DURING COVID

Scott Gotlieb speaks during an appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on July 27, 2026. (CNBC/SquawkBox)

"I think a lot of us went on to media out of a sense of obligation," he continued. "It was a hard time for all of us. I know it was a hard time for you. I think a lot of us felt an obligation to inform the public. And it wasn't particularly enjoyable. I mean, I got a lot of threats, others did as well, associated with that, and so to see those emails where he is evidencing some pleasure in the notoriety that he achieved, that's disappointing."

Kernen pushed back and said it was "outrageous."

"Does having a reputation totally in the toilet at 85 years, does that hold him to account for what he was responsible for?" Kernen asked.

Gottlieb said the Fauci he knew over the years was not the one he saw in the emails, and said the former NIH head was always careful and thoughtful.

Kernen specifically brought up Fauci's relationship with members of the liberal media. Fauci’s closest media ally appeared to have been CNN anchor Jake Tapper, who was mentioned 41 times in the diary.

FAUCI'S DIARY SHOWS HE FED QUESTIONS TO JOURNALISTS, BUILT FRIENDSHIPS WITH MEDIA FIGURES

Anthony Fauci, the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, listens during a Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee hearing in Washington, D.C., on Thursday, Nov. 4, 2021. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Did you figure out the obsession with mainstream media in defending him and Jake Tapper having multiple dinners and best friends? What did that come from? And I know people around here that would call Tony Fauci a hero," Kernen said.

Gottlieb said he couldn't dissect the relationship, but again said he was disappointed by the emails.

Fauci did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

According to the diary, Tapper texted Fauci to mock rival cable news hosts and other doctors. On one occasion, Tapper called to check on Fauci after an appearance on his show irked Trump supporters.

"Jake wanted to make sure the interview did not cause me any problems," Fauci wrote on April 13, 2020.

EXCLUSIVE: BIDEN PARDON WON'T SHIELD FAUCI IF HE LIES TO CONGRESS, COMER SAYS

In July 2020, Fauci gushed that he was forming a friendship with Tapper.

"Had dinner over Jake Tapper and Jen Tapper’s home in DC. Terrific couple. Friendship building," Fauci wrote, according to the diary.

Later that month, Fauci wrote that he "gave Jake some questions to ask" pediatrician Brett Giroir during an interview on CNN’s "State of the Union." But Tapper would later express frustration, waking Fauci up in the process.

"Tapper woke me up at 11:23 AM (I went to bed early) furius [sic] at POTUS for tweeting about the fact that Jake severly [sic] questioned Brett Giroir on SOTU CNN show today. Jake was really pissed at the craziness of it all," Fauci wrote.

Fox News' Brian Flood and Joseph Wulfsohn contributed to this report.

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

articles.title: New York offers college admission for residents unenrolled from Howard University
articles.excerpt:
Historically Black institution withdrew more than 500 first-year students for missed tuition payments

New York residents who were unenrolled from Washington DC’s Howard University have been offered a...
articles.body_text:
Historically Black institution withdrew more than 500 first-year students for missed tuition payments

New York residents who were unenrolled from Washington DC’s Howard University have been offered a reprieve after the historically Black institution withdrew more than 500 first-year students for missed tuition payments in late July. On 27 July, Kathy Hochul, New York’s governor, announced that affected New Yorkers can seek admission at the City University of New York (Cuny) and the State University of New York (Suny) for the fall 2026 semester.

Students will be offered expedited late admissions review at the Suny campuses at Buffalo, Albany, Buffalo State University, Binghamton, Oneonta, Stony Brook and New Paltz, with other schools assessing capacity.

“Hundreds of students, including New Yorkers, are scrambling and scared since they’ve been disenrolled from their intended college just a few weeks before classes are set to begin,” Hochul said in a statement.

“New York is home to the nation’s finest systems of public higher education, and we are ready to welcome these talented students with the opportunity they deserve. To every student who is worried that their educational future has been disrupted: New York is ready to support and empower you.”

Howard University said that 502 students did not submit their tuition payments by the school’s 10 July deadline, despite notifications that began in March. But some students have shared on social media that they never received the notifications.

“I worked like crazy to get into this school,” Saniah Collins told the AP. The school sent her an email last week notifying her that she had missed the payment deadline. “Howard has been my everything. My whole senior year, my whole summer I worked consistently on scholarships. We tried to make ourselves 10 steps ahead to make sure we were on the right page.”

The disenrollment follows a similar predicament last year where hundreds of students were unable to register for Howard University’s fall 2025 classes due to long-overdue balances. Most of the accounts were resolved in the following months; in early September 2025, Howard University told the Guardian that only 150 students had not registered for fall 2025 classes. At the time, Howard had transitioned from its BisonWeb platform to the new BisonHub platform, which caused a delay in about 1,000 student account updates between January and June 2025.

“Past due student balances are not the result of delayed account updates. The past due balances occurred when students did not resolve their balances by the specified date,” Howard University said in a statement to the Guardian in September 2025.

“Each student’s financial situation is unique, and we recognize that many of our students are doing everything they can to remain in good financial standing. Because of the system changeover, the university understands that there may have been some legitimate misunderstanding of amounts due to resolve long overdue balances. However, each long overdue balance should have been well understood and resolved by the student.”

Last year, students created a movement called “Whose Howard Is It” to demand better financial aid support.

articles.title: Philadelphia Eagles lock up Jalen Carter through 2031 with record $152M contract extension
articles.excerpt:
Colin Cowherd counts down the top 10 new additions across the NFL this offseason, including Myles Garrett and A.J. Brown.

The national stage wasn't kind to Jalen Carter at the start of the 2025 seaso...
articles.body_text:
Colin Cowherd counts down the top 10 new additions across the NFL this offseason, including Myles Garrett and A.J. Brown.

The national stage wasn't kind to Jalen Carter at the start of the 2025 season when we saw him get kicked out of the regular-season opener for spitting at Dak Prescott, but the start of this season is getting off on much brighter note.

As in, a Brink's truck full of $100 notes.

That's because Carter has agreed to a four-year contract extension worth a reported $152 million with $106 million guaranteed that makes him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history.

Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter (98) walks off the field after being disqualified for unsportsmanlike conduct before an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys Thursday, Sept. 4, 2025, in Philadelphia. (AP Photo/Matt Slocum)

PATRICK MAHOMES LEAPS PAST DAK PRESCOTT AS NFL'S HIGHEST-PAID QB WITH RECORD CHIEFS EXTENSION WORTH $504.75M

The deal, negotiated by agents Drew and Jason Rosenhaus, will pay Carter $38 million in new money on an annual average basis.

The average vaults Carter past Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons ($35.2 million), and Kansas City Chiefs lineman Chris Jones ($31.75 million) as the league's only interior linemen exceeding $30 million per season.

That's, shall we say, nothing to spit at.

Kansas City Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones (95) gestures to teh crowd during the third quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on Dec. 25, 2025. (Jay Biggerstaff/Imagn Images)

Carter is now under contract with Philadelphia through 2031.

The No. 9 overall pick of the 2023 draft, Carter finished second in the Defensive Rookie of the Year voting behind Will Anderson Jr.

Carter was instrumental in helping the Eagles win Super Bowl LIX to cap the 2024 season. Last year he only played in 11 games until he required shoulder surgery in both shoulders.

Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter walks off the field after being disqualified for unsportsmanlike conduct before an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys Thursday, Sept. 4, 2025, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (AP Photo/Matt Slocum)

But he played at least 90 percent of the snaps in four of those 11 games and his 55.9 snaps per game was the most among defensive tackles.

Carter is two-time Pro Bowler and the Eagles obviously believe his best days are ahead because that's exactly what $38 million per season should deliver.

Especially in games played on the national stage.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Dakota Johnson stuns as Marilyn Monroe in first look after director doubted casting
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Forget Dakota Johnson — the actress looked every bit the blonde bombshell as she transformed into Marilyn Monroe.

A new set photo o...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Forget Dakota Johnson — the actress looked every bit the blonde bombshell as she transformed into Marilyn Monroe.

A new set photo offered fans a first glimpse at Johnson's striking new role in "Flesh Impact." The short film, written and directed by Maggie Gyllenhaal, will premiere at the Venice Film Festival in September.

The shocking transformation is just one piece of Gyllenhaal's fresh take on the Hollywood legend.

ELLEN BURSTYN ON THE HABITS SHE GAVE UP TO STAY THRIVING AT 93 YEARS OLD

Dakota Johnson transforms into Marilyn Monroe in the first-look image from Maggie Gyllenhaal's short film, "Flesh Impact," which premieres at the Venice Film Festival in September. (Courtesy of Genesis)

Maggie Gyllenhaal initially worried that Johnson didn't look enough like Marilyn Monroe for the role. (Matt Winkelmeyer/GA/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images)

Instead of a traditional biopic, "Flesh Impact" imagines Monroe beyond the platinum hair and red lipstick, exploring the woman behind one of pop culture's most enduring personas.

Gyllenhaal first worried Johnson didn't look enough like Marilyn Monroe to play the part.

"Then I thought, ‘That’s ridiculous. Who cares?’" she told Vanity Fair. "I don’t know that anyone even really totally knows what Marilyn looks like because she’s been so commodified and made into this myth, and she’s very blurry in my mind."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Ellen Burstyn portrays a fictionalized older version of Marilyn Monroe in Maggie Gyllenhaal's "Flesh Impact," a short film reimagining the Hollywood icon beyond her public persona.  (Courtesy of Genesis)

For "Flesh Impact," Johnson portrayed Marilyn Monroe at age 36, the age at which the Hollywood icon died in 1962, while Ellen Burstyn played a fictionalized older version of the blonde bombshell.

Oscar-winner Ellen Burstyn plays a fictionalized older version of Marilyn Monroe in the 17-minute short film which will premiere at the Venice Film Festival. (Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images)

The 17-minute short film aims to explore Monroe beyond her enduring public image. Rather than being a traditional biopic, the film blends reality and imagination to examine her identity, legacy and the experience of being an actress in honor of her 100th birthday.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

American film actress Marilyn Monroe is shown in a portrait photograph circa 1954. (Baron/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

"I’ve always been fascinated by Marilyn Monroe," Gyllenhaal said in a press release. "So, when Genesis first came to me with the idea of a celebratory project for her centennial, I knew I wanted to work together on bringing this story to life.

"With ‘Flesh Impact,’ we showcase the timeless icon we know and love through a modern lens that reclaims her story," she added.

articles.title: ESPN's Dan Orlovsky weighs in on Florida coach Jon Sumrall's pedicure preferences, immediately gets roasted
articles.excerpt:
ESPN host Monica McNutt is under EXTREME heat after claiming Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark needs to show more "accountability and self-awareness."

While last week's SEC Media Days saw plenty ...
articles.body_text:
ESPN host Monica McNutt is under EXTREME heat after claiming Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark needs to show more "accountability and self-awareness."

While last week's SEC Media Days saw plenty of coaches putting themselves in the spotlight with a litany of quotes, one coach from the Southeastern Conference rose above the rest.

Florida's Jon Sumrall made quite a name for himself in Tampa last week during his inaugural spin as a head coach in the SEC, creating a bit of a stink on social media with his comments regarding a reporter's cell phone going off.

Sumrall apparently wasn't done hogging the limelight, though this time it was his wife generating the headlines when she dropped the bombshell that one of the toughest coaches in the conference loves getting pedicures.

Jon Sumrall speaks during a press conference introducing him as the new Florida Gators football head coach at the University of Florida in Gainesville, Fla., on Dec. 1, 2025. (Getty Images)

FLORIDA COACH BRINGS LAUGHS, NO FILTER AND LANE KIFFIN COMPARISON REBUTTAL TO FIRST SEC MEDIA DAYS

The internet once again reacted in kind, with fans and media members arguing both sides of the issue.

Some saw no problem with a man taking care of his feet - especially feet that used to play linebacker in the SEC - while others said the revelation that Sumrall gets his toes worked on pokes holes in his "tough guy act."

A few fans even suggested his wife was in the wrong for airing out his dirty laundry (and clean feet) and giving his rivals ammo to use against him.

One man who isn't necessarily a rival coach is ESPN analyst and former NFL quarterback Dan Orlovsky.

Orlovsky was asked about "Pedicuregate" on the show "Get Up" Tuesday morning, and the ex-Detroit Lion did not mince words.

"I have never gotten a pedicure, and I never will," said Orlovsky. "I am completely against pedicures for dudes."

ESPN PARTING WAYS WITH NFL ANALYST RYAN CLARK AHEAD OF NETWORK'S FIRST SUPER BOWL BROADCAST

Sumrall is pretty clearly a dude, so it sounds like Orlovsky is against the new Gators head coach getting a pedicure.

ESPN Broadcaster Dan Orlovsky speaks before the game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Detroit Lions at M&T Bank Stadium on Sept. 22, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (G Fiume/Getty Images)

Orlovsky was roundly mocked by all of his co-hosts on "Get Up" during the segment, but that was nothing compared to what fans on X had in store for him.

One subset of fans - both Florida and otherwise - correctly pointed out that Orlovsky calling a guy out for getting pedicures while he wears makeup on the set of a TV show feels a tad bit hypocritical.

Another subset of fans took things on a bit more of a personal route, and brought up Orlovsky's very infamous trip out of the back of the end zone during the 2008 NFL season (a season in which the Lions notoriously completed an 0-16 campaign).

I also have to say, it is relieving that fans of teams other than the Florida Gators are hopping to Jon Sumrall's defense.

I thought I was going to have to defend this take as a massive Gator homer like that one scene in "Game of Thrones" where Jon Snow has to take on hundreds of soldiers all by himself in The Battle of the Bastards.

Head coach Jon Sumrall of the Florida Gators waits to take the field before the Orange and Blue Game at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on April 11, 2026, in Gainesville, Fla. (Getty Images for ONIT)

In all seriousness, I'm not a pedicure guy. I really don't like strangers touching me in general so that rules out massages, too.

But I am in no way going to shame a man for getting his feet taken care of.

Manicures, though? That's a different story.

articles.title: Georgia teen who killed four in school shooting sentenced to life in prison without parole
articles.excerpt:

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A US judge on Tuesday sentenced a teenager wh...
articles.body_text:
Cole Gray pleaded guilty to 55 counts, including murder, for shooting at Apalachee high school in 2024

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A US judge on Tuesday sentenced a teenager who killed two students and two teachers in a shooting at Apalachee high school in Georgia to serve life in prison without the possibility of parole.

Colt Gray, 16, had pleaded guilty on Friday to 55 counts, including murder, in the 4 September 2024, shooting at the school about 45 miles (73km) north-east of Atlanta. Gray, who was 14 at the time, was charged as an adult.

Nicholas Primm, a Barrow county superior court judge, handed down the sentence after hearing from family members of those killed and victims, as well as investigators, a forensic psychologist who had evaluated Gray, a youth detention center counselor and Gray’s grandmother.

The minimum penalty for murder in Georgia is life with the possibility of parole. That left Primm with the decision of whether Gray should ever be eligible for parole. He decided the teen should never be allowed out.

Brad Smith, a district attorney, had argued that Gray “cannot be in society”. “We’ve seen no evidence he has any ability to develop a conscience or any ability ever to fully value human life,” Smith said.

The defense attorney W Charlton Allen told the judge his client was “not irretrievably broken”. Giving him the possibility of parole would give him “an opportunity of hope”, Allen said, adding that without hope, “that takes away the ability for him to change”.

Two teachers, Richard “Ricky” Aspinwall, 39, and Cristina Irimie, 53, and two students, Mason Schermerhorn and Christian Angulo, both 14, died in the shooting. Another teacher and eight more students were wounded, seven of them hit by gunfire.

Victims of the shooting and family members of those killed conveyed their anger and grief to Primm on Friday, almost all of them asking him to impose a sentence of life without the possibility of parole.

Shayna Aspinwall, the wife of math teacher and football coach Richard Aspinwall, described “a life sentence of grief and trauma for those left behind”.

articles.title: Leading economist warns of rise of 'Gen Z affordability socialism'
articles.excerpt:
Diogo Costa says a new generation is embracing price controls and government intervention despite wanting to live in a market economy.

Artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming the global...
articles.body_text:
Diogo Costa says a new generation is embracing price controls and government intervention despite wanting to live in a market economy.

Artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming the global economy at breakneck speed, but Diogo Costa argues that the real threat to prosperity isn't technological disruption; it's the return of bad economic ideas.

As the president of FEE (the Foundation for Economic Education), America's oldest free-market think tank, Costa is concerned that the affordability crisis is providing the perfect opportunity to tempt the next generation with the ideas of socialism, and argues that economic education is the antidote.

Recently, he sat down with Fox News Digital at Freedom Fest in Las Vegas for a discussion about the intellectual defense of free markets, the intersection of freedom and technology, and how his upbringing in Brazil brings a unique perspective to today's economic policy debates.

GEN Z IS WORKING HARD, BUT THE ECONOMY IS PUTTING THE AMERICAN DREAM OUT OF REACH FOR MANY

"The biggest challenge today is the different ways that ‘anti-economics’ keeps reappearing. And this time, it's reappearing through a new kind of socialism. So through the 20th century, we had different flavors of socialism, labor union socialism, environmental socialism, anti-globalization socialism. Now we see this cost-of-living socialism, affordability crisis socialism."

While young people are aware that they are better off in a market economy, Costa argues, they still want heavy-handed intervention if they perceive it benefits them.

"Young people, they want to live in a market economy. They don't want to move to Venezuela or Cuba, but they want price controls in everything. They want to freeze the rent, they want free rides in buses, they want to make sure that groceries are either run by the government or price controlled somehow. And this is not just a phenomenon in New York City or California. This is something that's happening globally.

"And this is the new kind of ‘anti-economics.’ So, Leonard Read [founder of FEE] understood that economics is always one generation away from turning prosperity into poverty. The good ideas need to keep being recycled, they need to be reframed, and this is a challenge that we have right now, the rise of this Gen Z affordability socialism."

He further argues that while the technology produced by vibrant market economies has incredible potential, the ideological foundation of capitalism is under attack like never before:

"We're in a golden age for technology, not necessarily for the ideas behind it…the ideas behind the market economy are not as well understood. And when you talk about AI, people are thinking all the jobs are going to be gone. Humanity is on the verge of extinction.

"So there is a lot of pessimism at the same time that you have these wonderful technologies. So the ideas that help us explain and help us work with technology are what's missing."

Costa's studies of the Austrian school of economics lead to separating the economic power of the free-market from its cultural power:

March 2, 2012: Traders crowd on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange. (AP)

"Joseph Schumpeter, the Austrian economist, said that capitalism would be economically powerful and at the same time culturally weak because you have companies that will be doing amazing things, but capitalism makes things more abstract…and at some point people stop seeing exactly how they are part of this amazing complexity.

DEMOCRATS LURE ‘POLITICALLY HOMELESS’ GEN Z TOWARD SOCIALISM — A COUNTERATTACK IS TAKING SHAPE

"That's why with FEE we sometimes go back to a pencil. We just ask people ‘do you understand how a pencil is made?’ Because if you see the complexity, the network, the amazing, marvelous market system around... Just building a single pencil, you start to understand how you are part of the complexity and you benefit from it."

Costa's own experience growing up in Brazil during the economically chaotic 1990s was pivotal in shaping his outlook on policy and the need for economic education.

"I grew up in a country that had hyperinflation. When I was 10 years old, 11 years old, yearly inflation was above 1000%, 1200%, 1300%. That meant the prices were changing literally every day. And it's hard to understand how if you live in a society that is that economically chaotic all your life is designed around those problems.

"So as a child, when I was going to the grocery store because my mom gave me a $1,000 bill to buy a bag of chips, I had to think, ‘Oh, I need to get there before the price tagger starts changing the prices’."

"My parents had to turn a bedroom in our house into a pantry because when they got their paychecks the first thing they did was go to the grocery store and buy everything you can…So your life starts to be designed around these big issues. And this is something that some people take for granted."

Rio de Janeiro, Brazil - December 28, 2013: Aerial view from a helicopter of Rio de Janeiro with the Corcovado mountain and the statue of Christ the Redeemer with Sugarloaf mountain in the background. (iStock)

But it was not only hyperinflation that opened Costa's eyes about economic education; he also first hand the effects of a fundamentally protectionist economic system:

"It's the same thing with protectionism…as a young boy in the early 90s, I wanted video games. Brazil had strict protectionism. So I could buy these dupe video games, but I couldn't get the real deal. And this was something that people now take for granted, but this was how the Brazilian economy was being shaped.

"And Milton Friedman has this saying that he thinks that we never actually learn economics as humanity, we learn as individuals, we learn maybe as generations, but now that we don't live under hyperinflation people forget what that's like, now that we don't live under hyperprotectionism people forget what it's like. So it's very easy to drift towards inflation, to drift towards protectionism, to drift towards anti-economics and economics needs to be re-taught every generation."

David Unsworth reports on Latin America. You can follow David Unsworth on Twitter @LatinAmerUpdate

articles.title: World-famous Catholic shrine torched, 'Devil in a skirt' scrawled on Virgin Mary statue
articles.excerpt: Tony Tripp, faculty member at Holy Innocents Catholic School, details the extensive vandalism, including a destroyed Virgin Mary statue and tabernacle. The DOJ launches a civil rights probe into the L...
articles.body_text:
Tony Tripp, faculty member at Holy Innocents Catholic School, details the extensive vandalism, including a destroyed Virgin Mary statue and tabernacle. The DOJ launches a civil rights probe into the Long Beach, CA, incident.

A man has been arrested after one of the world's most famous Catholic pilgrimage sites was vandalized and partially set on fire, with a statue of the Virgin Mary defaced and the words "Devil in a skirt" scrawled across its pedestal in black, according to reports.

Bosnian police arrested a suspect Tuesday in connection with the overnight vandalism and arson at the Shrine of Our Lady in Medjugorje, according to Vatican News.

Authorities have not released the man's identity as investigators work to determine a motive and whether he was responsible for other incidents reported at the shrine that same night, the outlet said.

NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES

Police were first called around 4:30 a.m. July 27 after the face and hands of the statue of the Virgin Mary on Apparition Hill, also known as Podbrdo, were found covered in black paint. (Associated Press)

Police were called around 4:30 a.m. July 27 after the face and hands of the statue of the Virgin Mary on Apparition Hill, also known as Podbrdo, were found covered in black paint.

The pedestal at the foot of the statue was spray-painted with the English phrase "Devil in a skirt," while other graffiti and the statue's hands were painted black.

An outdoor altar nearby was also set on fire near St. James Church, the outlet said.

Surveillance footage reportedly at that location showed a man pouring what investigators believe was gasoline onto the altar before setting it ablaze. The fire was extinguished.

REPORT DETAILS RISING PRESSURE ON UNDERGROUND CATHOLICS AS CHINA DENIES CRACKDOWN

Police were first called around 4:30 a.m. July 27 after the face and hands of the statue of the Virgin Mary on Apparition Hill, also known as Podbrdo, were found covered in black paint. (Associated Press)

The two attacks came just days before Medjugorje's annual youth prayer festival, which is expected to draw more than 50,000 pilgrims from around the world.

In a statement Tuesday, the Medjugorje Parish Office condemned the vandalism and urged Catholics to respond with "prayer, fasting, and forgiveness" rather than anger.

"It is with great sadness that we received the news of the act of vandalism," the parish said.

Church officials also said cleanup and repairs began immediately so the damaged prayer sites could once again welcome pilgrims.

"The affected areas are being cleaned and restored as quickly as possible," the parish said, thanking volunteers for helping preserve the shrine as "a place of encounter with God, a place of peace."

CATHOLIC NUNS SUE NEW YORK, SAY ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW FORCES THEM TO VIOLATE THEIR FAITH

Church officials also said cleanup and repairs began immediately so the damaged prayer sites could once again welcome pilgrims. (Associated Press)

Rather than calling for retribution, the parish urged the faithful to pray for those responsible.

"We pray for the conversion of the hearts of those who committed this act," the statement said, asking that God "touch them with His grace and lead them on the path of goodness."

The parish also appealed for peace, encouraging Catholics "not to return evil for evil," but instead to bear witness through "love, forgiveness and hope."

Despite the attack, officials said the shrine remains open, and its regular schedule of Mass and prayer services will continue as planned.

Located about 85 miles southwest of Sarajevo, Medjugorje became one of the world's best-known Catholic pilgrimage destinations after six children and teenagers reported seeing apparitions of the Virgin Mary there in 1981.

The Vatican gave the green light for Catholics to continue flocking to Medjugorje offering its approval for devotion at one of the most contested sites of Roman Catholic practice in recent years, The Associated Press reported Tuesday.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title: Utah woman set fire to church a day before wedding, authorities say

Lenita Moreno, 25, arrested over fire – which allegedly caused $108,000 in damage – at Mormon church in Kaysville

A Utah woman set fire to the church where she was scheduled to get married a day befo...
articles.body_text:
Lenita Moreno, 25, arrested over fire – which allegedly caused $108,000 in damage – at Mormon church in Kaysville

A Utah woman set fire to the church where she was scheduled to get married a day before the wedding, allege authorities investigating what may have been an extreme case of cold feet.

Lenita Moreno, 25, was arrested on a count of aggravated arson in connection with the 10 July blaze, which investigators say caused $108,000 in damage and was started using a tampon and other flammable items.

According to court documents reported on by Utah news outlet KUTV, the fire started in the Relief Society room of a Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints building when Moreno, her unidentified groom and family members were setting up in the church building for the couple’s wedding the next day.

The family reportedly said they were about to leave the church in Kaysville when the fire alarm went off. A bystander used water from wedding decorations to put out the blaze while another used a fire extinguisher, said the documents cited by KUTV.

Investigators said the fire appeared to have been started under a chair using “items that were out of the ordinary, including what appeared to be a tampon”.

The groom allegedly told detectives he and Moreno were in the room where the fire started. He also reportedly told detectives he and Moreno had been to an Ace Hardware earlier in the day.

Police said they contacted the store, and employees there provided video footage of Moreno stealing two cigarette lighters. Police alleged they could see Moreno walk towards the lighters, take an unknown number and hide them on her person.

They said Moreno admitted to stealing from the Ace Hardware, but that she would not disclose what she had taken.

“It is believed that Lenita (Tessa) started a fire within a church building while five others were still inside,” the probable cause stated. “Lenita did not obtain a marriage license for her own wedding that was to occur the following day after the fire but had lied stating she had.”

Beside arson, Moreno was booked with retail theft and providing false information to a peace officer.

Moreno, who KUTV reported was set to be married under the name of Tessa Moran, was being held without bail as of Tuesday.

The US event insurance company Eventsure estimates that 15 to 20% of weddings are called off.

While a change of heart is not covered under a policy, Eventsured states: “Sometimes you have to cancel your wedding for reasons out of your control whether it’s a fire, illness, etc.

“In these cases, consider getting cancellation insurance.”

articles.title: Spanish soccer player makes good on his promise to get tattoo of team's manager after World Cup win
articles.excerpt:

Spain is still...
articles.body_text:
Fox News chief correspondent Jonathan Hunt reports on Spain winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup final against Argentina in a match at New York New Jersey Stadium on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’

Spain is still taking a well-deserved victory lap after locking up the World Cup title earlier this month, and for one player, that involved getting some fresh ink.

And what better way to commemorate the win than by getting the World Cup trophy permanently drawn on your body?

I'll tell you one: getting your manager's big ol' mug holding the World Cup trophy permanently drawn on your body, which is what Spain's Marc Cucurella did.

SPAIN BEATS ARGENTINA TO WIN 2026 FIFA WORLD CUP BEHIND FERRAN TORRES' EXTRA-TIME GOAL

Spain's Marc Cucurella made good on his pre-World Cup promise to get a tattoo of his manager's face if the team won it all. (Photo by Eduardo Carmim/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Even before the tournament started, Cucurella pledged to get a tattoo of his manager's face if the team went all the way.

He may have thought he was in the clear when Spain opened the tournament with a 0-0 draw against Cape Verde, but that turned out to be the only blemish on their World Cup record.

Spain defeated reigning champs Argentina for the title on July 19, and now Cucurella is making good on his promise.

There had to be a point, as Spain was closing in on the final, where Cucurella was hoping everyone had forgotten about all of this tattoo business.

FERRAN TORRES SPORTS 'MAKE SPAIN GREAT AGAIN' HAT SIMILAR TO TRUMP'S SLOGAN AT WORLD CUP HOMECOMING PARADE

Unfortunately for him, the internet doesn't forget.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But it's a unique memento from Spain's World Cup run, and good on him for sticking to his word.

Spain's Marc Cucurella celebrates the team's World Cup win at a parade in Madrid. (Photo by Luciano Lima/Getty Images)

I think he's going to get irritated in a hurry when he has to keep fielding the questions, "Who is that old guy on your arm?" over and over and over.

Hell, he might just want to get a second tattoo right under that just says, "Before you ask me, it's Spanish national soccer team manager Luis de la Fuente."

articles.title: Trump says heroic teen lifeguard who saved boy from towering waves deserves White House honor
articles.excerpt:
Frantic scenes unfolded at Santa Cruz's Seabright Beach as powerful, tsunami-like swells tossed rescuers through crashing waves. (Scott Vander Dussen / Instagram @santacruznow)

President Donald Trump...
articles.body_text:
Frantic scenes unfolded at Santa Cruz's Seabright Beach as powerful, tsunami-like swells tossed rescuers through crashing waves. (Scott Vander Dussen / Instagram @santacruznow)

President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised the teenage lifeguard who went viral after rescuing a young boy from towering waves in Santa Cruz, California, saying he wants to invite the teen to the White House and potentially award him a high civilian honor.

The lifeguard, identified as 16-year-old Ryder on social media, was captured in a heart-stopping video Saturday battling massive surf as he repeatedly disappeared beneath crashing waves while maintaining a relentless grip on the child he was rescuing.

After seeing the dramatic rescue, Trump said the teen deserved national recognition.

"We’re going to bring this heroic young man, and his family, into the White House with, perhaps, the boy he saved, to give him a High Civilian Honor. Very brave, he deserves it!" Trump said in a post on X.

HEROIC 16-YEAR-OLD LIFEGUARD RESCUES CHILD FROM MONSTER SURF IN HEART-STOPPING VIDEO

A heroic 16-year-old lifeguard repeatedly disappeared beneath towering waves while refusing to let go of a child swept into dangerous California surf. (Scott Vander Dussen/Instagram @Santacruznow)

Hours earlier, Eric Trump also praised the rescue on social media, calling for the teen to receive the nation's highest civilian recognition.

"Give this 16-year-old lifeguard the highest civilian honor. This is truly the best of America! Well done!" he said.

The rescue drew thousands of reactions online, with many praising Ryder for battling powerful waves that appeared too dangerous even for bystanders who attempted to help.

One person claiming to have witnessed the rescue said it lasted far longer than the viral video showed. Beachgoers reportedly formed a human chain in an effort to help before it was eventually broken apart by the pounding surf, according to social media users.

MAN, WOMAN KILLED IN RIP CURRENT AS LIFEGUARD SHORTAGE LEAVES DANGER ZONES IN BEACH DESTINATION

President Donald Trump speaks at Verst Logistics in Hebron, Kentucky, on March 11, 2026. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)

After pulling the child safely onto the beach, Ryder reportedly sprinted past his lifeguard tower to get additional assistance before paramedics arrived to evaluate the boy, the witness said. Despite the dramatic rescue, Ryder later returned to duty and continued watching over beachgoers for the rest of the evening.

The rescue may have come during Ryder's first season as a lifeguard. California State Parks requires state lifeguards to be at least 16 years old.

Another social media user who said she knew Ryder emphasized how extraordinary the rescue was.

"I’m not sure how many people know how hard it is to hold onto someone like that in the ocean, during these heavy conditions and pounding shore break. This lifeguard handled it like a pro, pulled him in most of the way solo and never gave up. Taht is a feat in itself, especially in those conditions. A true Hero & waterman. I seriously hope he gets recognized for this," the user said.

Other people claiming to have witnessed the incident said the surf had initially appeared relatively calm, with many beachgoers standing at the water's edge when a massive wave suddenly crashed ashore.

Terrifying video captures a teenage lifeguard risking his own life as relentless waves repeatedly swallowed him and a struggling child. (Scott Vander Dussen/Instagram @Santacruznow)

"It was so big it nearly reached us by our things all the way up the beach!" the witness said.

Seabright Beach is known for its powerful shore break, with waves shaped by swells arriving from multiple directions, creating hazardous conditions even for experienced swimmers.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

articles.body_text:
The army says it’s retaken a key highway linking Khartoum to El-Obeid.

Three years of fighting between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have devastated Sudan.

The conflict has caused the world’s largest humanitarian crisis, displacing more than 13 million people and killing tens of thousands of civilians.

More than half of the population needs aid. The health system is in ruins, and millions of children are out of school. Both sides have been accused of war crimes and other abuses.

Recent fighting has centred around the city of el-Obeid, under siege by paramilitaries. The army has retaken a main highway linking it to the capital, which could weaken the RSF.

But hundreds of thousands of people trapped there are still at risk.

So, what will it take to stop the conflict?

Sanosi Zakaria – Editor-in-chief of the Sudan Mirror and former Sudanese army officer

Shashwat Saraf – Sudan country director for the Norwegian Refugee Council
